units.zh: 高季興，字貽孫，陜州硤石人也。
units.en: Gao Jixing, whose courtesy name was Yisun, came from Xiashi in Shanzhou.
units.literal: Gao Jixing, courtesy name Yisun, was a native of Xiashi in Shan Prefecture.

units.zh: 本名季昌，及後唐莊宗即位，避其廟諱改焉。
units.en: He had originally been named Jichang, but when Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang acceded to the throne he changed his name to avoid the imperial temple taboo.
units.literal: His original name was Jichang; when Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang took the throne, he changed it to avoid the taboo on the temple name.

units.zh: 幼隸於汴之賈人李七郎，梁祖以李七郎為子，賜姓，名友讓。
units.en: As a boy he served under Li Qilang, a merchant of Bian; the Liang founder adopted Li Qilang as a son, bestowed a surname on him, and gave him the name Yourang.
units.literal: In youth he was attached to a Bian merchant named Li Qilang; the Founding Emperor of Liang took Li Qilang as a son, granted him a surname, and named him Yourang.

units.zh: 梁祖嘗見季興於仆隸中，其耳面稍異，命友讓養之為子。
units.en: The Liang founder once noticed Jixing among the household servants—his ears and facial features were slightly unusual—and ordered Yourang to bring him up as his own son.
units.literal: The Liang founder once saw Jixing among the servants; his ears and face were somewhat unusual, and he ordered Yourang to raise him as a son.

units.zh: 梁祖以季興為牙將，漸能騎射。
units.en: The Liang founder appointed Jixing to the guard corps, and he gradually became adept at horsemanship and archery.
units.literal: The Liang founder made Jixing a palace guard officer, and he gradually mastered riding and archery.

units.zh: 唐天復中，昭宗在岐下，梁祖圍鳳翔日久，眾議欲班師，獨季興諫止之，語在《梁祖紀》中。
units.en: During the Tang Tianfu period, while Emperor Zhaozong was at Qizhou, the Liang founder had long besieged Fengxiang; when many urged a withdrawal, Jixing alone dissuaded him—the story is recorded in the 《Annals of the Liang Founder》.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era of Tang, Emperor Zhaozong was at Qixia; the Liang founder had besieged Fengxiang for a long time, and the assembly discussed withdrawing the army—only Jixing advised against it; the account is in the 《Annals of the Liang Founder》.

units.zh: 既而竟迎昭宗歸京，以季興為迎鑾毅勇功臣、檢校大司空、行宋州刺史。
units.en: In the end the court brought Emperor Zhaozong back to the capital, and Jixing was rewarded with the title of meritorious minister of the imperial escort, honorary Grand Minister of Works, and acting prefect of Songzhou.
units.literal: Subsequently they did welcome Emperor Zhaozong back to the capital; Jixing was made a meritorious minister for welcoming the imperial carriage, with the honorary title of Grand Minister of Works and acting prefect of Songzhou.

units.zh: 從梁祖平青州，改知宿州事，遷潁州防禦使，梁祖令復姓高氏，擢為荊南兵馬留後。
units.en: After accompanying the Liang founder in the pacification of Qingzhou, he was reassigned to administer Suzhou, then promoted to defender of Yingzhou; the Liang founder had him resume the surname Gao and appointed him military intendant of Jingnan.
units.literal: Following the Liang founder in pacifying Qingzhou, he was changed to administer Suzhou affairs, then promoted to military commissioner of Yingzhou; the Liang founder ordered him to resume the Gao surname and elevated him to military intendant of Jingnan.

units.zh: 荊州自唐乾符之後，兵火互集，井邑不完，季興招輯離散，流民歸復，梁祖嘉之，乃授節鉞。
units.en: Jingzhou had been ravaged by war ever since the Tang Qianfu years, its towns left in ruins; Jixing rallied the displaced and brought the refugee population back, and the Liang founder, pleased with his work, invested him with full military authority.
units.literal: Since the Qianfu era of Tang, Jingzhou had suffered repeated warfare and its towns were incomplete; Jixing gathered the scattered population and refugees returned; the Liang founder commended this and granted him the seal of command.

units.zh: 梁開平中，破雷彥恭於朗州，加平章事。
units.en: During the Liang Kaiping period he defeated Lei Yingong at Langzhou and was given the title of Grand Councillor.
units.literal: In the Kaiping era of Liang, he defeated Lei Yingong at Langzhou and was made a participant in government.

units.zh: 荊南舊無外壘，季興始城之，遂厚斂於民，招聚亡命，自後僭臣於吳、蜀，梁氏稍不能制焉，因就封渤海王。
units.en: Jingnan had never had outer fortifications until Jixing built city walls; he then levied heavy taxes, gathered desperadoes, and afterward acted as a rival vassal to Wu and Shu while the Liang court gradually lost control—whereupon he accepted enfeoffment as Prince of Bohai.
units.literal: Jingnan had formerly had no outer ramparts; Jixing was the first to wall the city, then heavily taxed the people and gathered fugitives; afterward he played the vassal to Wu and Shu while Liang could scarcely control him, and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Bohai.

units.zh: 嘗攻襄州，為孔所敗。
units.en: He once attacked Xiangzhou but was defeated by Kong Qing.
units.literal: He once attacked Xiangzhou and was defeated by Kong Qing.

units.zh: 及莊宗定天下，季興來朝於洛陽，加兼中書令，時論多請留之，郭崇韜以方推信義於華夏，請放歸藩，季興促程而去。
units.en: Once Emperor Zhuangzong had unified the empire, Jixing traveled to Luoyang to pay homage and was further appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat; many at court argued that he should be held, but Guo Chongtao urged that, having only just begun to promote faith and righteousness across the realm, the throne should let him return to his post—so Jixing hurried home.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong had settled the realm, Jixing came to court at Luoyang and was additionally made Director of the Secretariat; contemporary opinion largely urged detaining him, but Guo Chongtao, as the court was just promoting trust and righteousness throughout China, requested he be released to his domain; Jixing hurried on his journey and left.

units.zh: 至襄州，酒酣，謂孔曰：「是行有二錯：來朝一錯，放回二錯。」
units.en: At Xiangzhou, when the wine had gone to his head, he said to Kong Qing, "This trip involved two blunders: paying court was the first blunder, and being sent back was the second."
units.literal: When he reached Xiangzhou, as the wine took hold he said to Kong Qing: "This journey had two mistakes: coming to court was the first mistake, and being sent back was the second."

units.zh: 洎至荊南，謂賓佐曰：「新主百戰方得河南，對勛臣誇手抄《春秋》；
units.en: After he reached Jingnan he told his advisers, "The new emperor won the Central Plains only after countless battles, yet he boasts to his meritorious ministers that he copied the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 by hand;
units.literal: When he reached Jingnan he told his staff: "The new ruler won the lands south of the Yellow River only after a hundred battles, yet he boasts to his meritorious ministers that he copied the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 by hand;

units.zh: 又豎手指云：『我於指頭上得天下。』
units.en: and he holds up a finger and says, 'I won the empire on the tip of this finger.'
units.literal: and he holds up a finger and says, 'I won the realm on the tip of this finger.'

units.zh: 如此則功在一人，臣佐何有！
units.en: If that is so, all the credit belongs to him alone—what is left for his ministers!
units.literal: In that case all merit belongs to one man—what room is there for his ministers!

units.zh: 且遊獵旬日不回，中外之情，其何以堪，吾高枕無憂矣。」
units.en: And he goes hunting for days on end without returning—how can the court and the realm endure it? I can sleep soundly from now on."
units.literal: Moreover he goes hunting for ten days at a stretch without returning—how can court and countryside bear it? I may rest easy on a high pillow."

units.zh: 乃增築西面羅城，備禦敵之具。
units.en: He then extended the western outer rampart and stockpiled weapons and supplies to repel invaders.
units.literal: He then extended the western outer wall and prepared equipment for defense against enemies.

units.zh: 時梁朝舊軍多為季興所誘，由是兵眾漸多，跋扈之志堅矣。
units.en: Many veterans of the former Liang armies were lured into his service, so his forces steadily grew and his ambition to defy the throne hardened.
units.literal: At that time many veterans of the Liang army were enticed away by Jixing; thus his forces gradually grew and his will to act overbearingly hardened.

units.zh: 明年，冊拜南平王。
units.en: The following year he was invested as Prince of Nanping.
units.literal: The next year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping.

units.zh: 魏王繼岌平蜀，盡選其寶貨浮江而下，船至峽口，會莊宗遇禍，季興盡邀取之。
units.en: When Prince of Wei Jiji conquered Shu, he loaded its treasures onto boats bound downriver; at the gorge mouth Zhuangzong met his death, and Jixing seized the entire convoy.
units.literal: Prince of Wei Jiji pacified Shu and selected all its treasures to float down the river; when the boats reached the gorge mouth, Zhuangzong met with disaster, and Jixing intercepted and took everything.

units.zh: 明宗即位，復請夔、峽為屬郡，初俞其請，後朝廷除刺史，季興上言，稱已令子弟權知郡事，請不除刺史。
units.en: After Emperor Mingzong acceded, Jixing again asked that Kuizhou and Xiazhou be placed under his jurisdiction; the court initially agreed, but when it later named official prefects he protested that his sons were already administering those districts and begged that no outside appointees be sent.
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Jixing again requested that Kuizhou and Xiazhou be made his subordinate prefectures; at first the request was granted, but later the court appointed prefects; Jixing memorialized that he had already ordered his sons and younger brothers to administer the prefectures provisionally and asked that prefects not be appointed.

units.zh: 不臣之狀既形，詔削奪其官爵。
units.en: When his rebellious conduct became unmistakable, an edict stripped him of rank and title.
units.literal: Once his disloyal conduct had become manifest, an edict stripped him of his offices and titles.

units.zh: 天成初，命西方鄴興師收復三州，又遣襄州節度使劉訓總兵圍荊南，以問其罪，屬霖潦，班師。
units.en: Early in the Tiancheng era the court ordered Xifang Ye to recover the three prefectures and sent Liu Xun, military commissioner of Xiangzhou, to besiege Jingnan and punish his rebellion; relentless rains forced a withdrawal.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Tiancheng era, Xifang Ye was ordered to raise troops to recover the three prefectures, and the military commissioner of Xiangzhou Liu Xun was also sent to command forces besieging Jingnan to call him to account; because of heavy rains the army withdrew.

units.zh: 三年冬，季興病腳氣而卒。
units.en: In the winter of the third year Jixing died of gout.
units.literal: In the winter of the third year Jixing died of foot ailment.

units.zh: 其子從誨嗣立，累表謝罪，請修職貢。
units.en: His son Conghui succeeded him and sent repeated memorials confessing fault and asking to resume tribute and service.
units.literal: His son Conghui succeeded him, repeatedly memorializing to confess guilt and requesting to resume tribute duties.

units.zh: 由是復季興官爵，謚曰武信。
units.en: The court thereupon restored Jixing's offices and titles and gave him the posthumous name Wuxin, Martial and Faithful.
units.literal: Thereupon Jixing's offices and titles were restored, and he was given the posthumous title Martial and Faithful.

units.zh: 從誨，初仕梁，歷殿前控鶴都頭、鞍轡庫副使、左軍巡使、如京使、左千牛大將軍、荊南衙內都指揮使，領濠州刺史，改歸州刺史，累官至檢校太傅。
units.en: Conghui began his career under the Liang, rising through posts from commander of the Palace Crane Guards and deputy of the saddlery office to patrol commissioner, capital envoy, Thousand-Ox general, and overall commander of the Jingnan headquarters, with concurrent appointments as prefect of Haozhou and then Guizhou, until he reached the honorary rank of Grand Mentor.
units.literal: Conghui first served Liang, passing through the posts of commander of the Palace Crane Guards, deputy commissioner of the Saddlery Storehouse, left army patrol commissioner, envoy to the capital, left Thousand-Ox Grand General, and overall commander within the Jingnan headquarters, concurrently prefect of Haozhou, then changed to prefect of Guizhou, rising cumulatively to honorary Grand Mentor.

units.zh: 初，季興之將叛也，從誨常泣諫之，季興不從。
units.en: When Jixing was on the verge of rebellion, Conghui often pleaded with tears, but Jixing refused to heed him.
units.literal: When Jixing was about to rebel, Conghui often wept and remonstrated with him, but Jixing would not listen.

units.zh: 天成三年冬，季興薨，從誨乃上表謝罪，復修職貢。
units.en: In the winter of Tiancheng 3, after Jixing's death, Conghui submitted a memorial of repentance and restored regular tribute.
units.literal: In the winter of the third year of Tiancheng Jixing died; Conghui then submitted a memorial confessing guilt and resumed tribute duties.

units.zh: 明宗嘉之，尋命起復，授荊南節度使、兼待中。
units.en: Emperor Mingzong approved and soon recalled him from mourning to appoint him military commissioner of Jingnan and concurrent Palace Attendant.
units.literal: Emperor Mingzong commended this and soon ordered him to resume office from mourning, appointing him military commissioner of Jingnan and concurrent Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 長興三年，加檢校太尉。
units.en: In Changxing 3 he was promoted to honorary Grand Commandant.
units.literal: In the third year of Changxing he was given the honorary title of Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 應順中，封南平王。
units.en: During the Yingshun era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping.
units.literal: During Yingshun he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping.

units.zh: 清泰初，加檢校太師。
units.en: Early in the Qingtai era he was made honorary Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was given the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 晉天福中，加守中書令。
units.en: During the Later Jin Tianfu era he was appointed acting Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: During Tianfu of Jin he was made acting Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 六年，襄州安從進反，王師攻討，從誨饋軍食以助焉，詔書褒美，尋加守尚書令，從誨上章固讓，朝廷遣使敦勉，竟不受其命。
units.en: In the sixth year, when An Congjin rebelled at Xiangzhou, Conghui sent provisions to support the imperial campaign; the throne praised him in edict and soon offered him acting Director of the Department of State Affairs, but he firmly declined; though envoys pressed him, he never accepted.
units.literal: In the sixth year An Congjin of Xiangzhou rebelled; the imperial army attacked him, and Conghui supplied provisions to assist; an edict praised him, and soon he was made acting Director of the Department of State Affairs; Conghui memorialized firmly declining; the court sent envoys to urge him earnestly, but in the end he did not accept the appointment.

units.zh: 時有術士言從誨年命有厄，宜退避寵祿故也。
units.en: A diviner had warned that calamity threatened his lifespan and that he should step back from high office—hence his refusal.
units.literal: At the time a diviner said Conghui's fate had a calamity and that he should therefore withdraw from favor and rank.

units.zh: 及契丹入汴，漢高祖起義於太原，間道遣使奉貢，密有祈請，言俟車駕定河、汴，願賜郢州為屬郡，漢祖依違之。
units.en: When the Khitans seized Bian, as Emperor Gaozu of Later Han rose at Taiyuan, Conghui sent tribute by a back route with a secret plea: once the throne secured the Yellow River and Bian regions, he asked that Yingzhou be granted as his dependency—the Han founder wavered.
units.literal: When the Khitans entered Bian, Emperor Gaozu of Han rose in arms at Taiyuan; Conghui sent tribute by a secret route with a private request, saying that once the imperial carriage had settled the He and Bian regions he wished to be granted Yingzhou as a subordinate prefecture; the Han founder hesitated.

units.zh: 及入汴，從誨致貢，求踐前言，漢高祖不從。
units.en: After Gaozu entered Bian, Conghui sent tribute again and demanded the promised grant; Gaozu refused.
units.literal: When he entered Bian, Conghui sent tribute and asked to fulfill the earlier promise; Emperor Gaozu of Han did not agree.

units.zh: 從誨怒，率州兵攻郢州，旬日，為刺史尹實所敗，自是朝貢不至。
units.en: Enraged, Conghui led his troops against Yingzhou; within ten days Yin Shi, the prefect, routed him, and thereafter he sent no more tribute.
units.literal: Conghui grew angry, led his prefectural troops to attack Yingzhou, and within ten days was defeated by the prefect Yin Shi; from then on tribute ceased to arrive.

units.zh: 從誨東通於吳，西通於蜀，皆利其供軍財貨而已。
units.en: He dealt with Wu in the east and Shu in the west solely for the profit of their military goods and tribute.
units.literal: Conghui communicated east with Wu and west with Shu, seeking only profit from their military supplies and goods.

units.zh: 末年，以鎮星在翼、軫之分，乃釋羅紈，衣布素，飲食節儉，以禳災咎。
units.en: In his last years, with Saturn in the Wings and Chariot asterisms, he gave up silk, wore plain cloth, and ate frugally to ward off misfortune.
units.literal: In his later years, because the planet Saturn was in the mansions Yi and Zhen, he put aside silk and brocade, wore plain cloth, and ate sparingly to avert calamity.

units.zh: 尋令人祈托襄州安審琦，請歸朝待罪，朝廷亦開納之。
units.en: He soon asked An Shenqi of Xiangzhou to intercede for his return to court to await judgment, and the throne showed itself willing to receive him.
units.literal: Soon he had someone entreat An Shenqi of Xiangzhou to request permission to return to court and await punishment; the court also showed willingness to accept him.

units.zh: 漢乾祐元年冬十一月，以疾薨於位。
units.en: In the eleventh month of winter, Qianyou 1 of Later Han, he died in office of illness.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of winter in the first year of Qianyou of Han he died of illness in office.

units.zh: 詔贈尚書令，謚曰文獻。
units.en: An edict posthumously made him Director of the Department of State Affairs and gave him the posthumous name Wenxian, Literary and Offering.
units.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Director of the Department of State Affairs, with the posthumous title Literary and Offering.

units.zh: 子保融嗣，位至荊南節度使、守太傅、中書令，封南平王。
units.en: His son Baorong succeeded him, rising to military commissioner of Jingnan, acting Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Nanping.
units.literal: His son Baorong succeeded, rising to military commissioner of Jingnan, acting Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Nanping.

units.zh: 皇朝建隆元年秋卒。
units.en: He died in the autumn of the first year of Jianlong of the Song.
units.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Jianlong of the Imperial Dynasty he died.

units.zh: 謚曰貞懿。
units.en: He was given the posthumous name Zhenyi, Chaste and Virtuous.
units.literal: His posthumous title was Chaste and Virtuous.

units.zh: 其諸將之倚任者，則有王保義。
units.en: Among the generals he relied on was Wang Baoyi.
units.literal: Among the generals on whom he relied was Wang Baoyi.

units.zh: 保義本姓劉，名去非，幽州人。
units.en: Baoyi was born Liu Qufei, a native of Youzhou.
units.literal: Baoyi was originally surnamed Liu, named Qufei, a man of Youzhou.

units.zh: 少為縣吏，粗暴無行，習騎射，敢鬥擊。
units.en: As a youth he served as a county clerk, was violent and unrestrained, trained in horsemanship and archery, and was fearless in combat.
units.literal: In youth he was a county clerk, rough and without propriety, practiced riding and archery, and dared to fight.

units.zh: 劉仁恭之子守奇善射，惟去非許以為能。
units.en: Liu Shouqi, son of Liu Rengong, was a fine archer, and only Qufei would concede his skill.
units.literal: Liu Shouqi, son of Liu Rengong, was skilled at archery; only Qufei acknowledged his ability.

units.zh: 守奇以兄守光奪父位，亡入契丹，又自契丹奔太原，去非皆從之。
units.en: When Shouqi's brother Shouguang usurped their father's throne, Shouqi fled to the Khitans and later from there to Taiyuan, and Qufei followed him throughout.
units.literal: Shouqi, because his elder brother Shouguang seized their father's position, fled into the Khitans, then from the Khitans fled to Taiyuan; Qufei followed him in all of this.

units.zh: 莊宗之伐燕也，守奇從周德威引軍前進，師次涿州，刺史姜行敢登陴固守，去非呼行敢曰：「河東小劉郎領軍來為父除兇，爾何敢拒！」
units.en: During Zhuangzong's campaign against Yan, Shouqi marched with Zhou Dewei; at Zhuozhou the prefect Jiang Xinggan manned the walls; Qufei shouted, "The young Liu of Hedong comes to avenge his father—how dare you resist!"
units.literal: When Zhuangzong attacked Yan, Shouqi followed Zhou Dewei advancing the army; the force halted at Zhuozhou, and the prefect Jiang Xinggan mounted the walls to hold firm; Qufei called to Xinggan: "The young Liu of Hedong leads the army to avenge his father—how dare you resist!"

units.zh: 守奇免胄勞之，行敢遙拜，即開門迎降。
units.en: Shouqi doffed his helmet in greeting; Xinggan bowed from the wall and opened the gates in surrender.
units.literal: Shouqi removed his helmet to salute him; Xinggan bowed from afar and at once opened the gate to welcome surrender.

units.zh: 德威害其功，密告莊宗，言守奇心不可保。
units.en: Jealous of the credit, Dewei secretly told Zhuangzong that Shouqi's loyalty could not be trusted.
units.literal: Dewei envied his achievement and secretly reported to Zhuangzong that Shouqi's loyalty could not be trusted.

units.zh: 莊宗召守奇還計事，行次土門，去非說守奇曰：「公不施寸兵下涿郡，周公以得非己力，必有如簧之間，太原不宜往也。
units.en: Zhuangzong recalled Shouqi for consultation; at Tumen Pass, Qufei urged him, "You took Zhuo without a fight, yet Zhou Dewei will resent that the credit was not his—slander will follow; you should not go to Taiyuan.
units.literal: Zhuangzong summoned Shouqi back to discuss affairs; when they reached Tumen Pass, Qufei persuaded Shouqi: "You took Zhuo Prefecture without striking a blow, yet Duke Zhou will think it was not his own achievement—there will surely be slander like a reed flute; Taiyuan is not a place you should go.

units.zh: 公家於梁，素有君臣之分，宜往依之，介福萬全矣。」
units.en: Your house has long owed allegiance to Liang; go to them and you will be utterly safe."
units.literal: Your family has long had the relation of lord and minister with Liang; you should go rely on them—fortune will be entirely secure."

units.zh: 守奇乃奔梁，梁以守奇為滄州留後，以去非為河陽行軍司馬。
units.en: Shouqi fled to Liang, which made him military intendant of Cangzhou and Qufei campaigning marshal of Heyang.
units.literal: Shouqi then fled to Liang; Liang made Shouqi military intendant of Cangzhou and Qufei campaigning marshal of Heyang.

units.zh: 時謝彥章移去非為郢州刺史。
units.en: Xie Yanzhang then reassigned Qufei as prefect of Yingzhou.
units.literal: At that time Xie Yanzhang transferred Qufei to be prefect of Yingzhou.

units.zh: 及莊宗平河、洛，去非乃棄郡歸高季興，為行軍司馬，仍改易姓名。
units.en: When Zhuangzong conquered the Central Plains, Qufei abandoned his post, joined Gao Jixing as campaigning marshal, and changed his name.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified the He and Luo regions, Qufei abandoned his prefecture and returned to Gao Jixing, serving as campaigning marshal while also changing his name.

units.zh: 自是季興父子倚為腹心，凡守藩規畫，出兵方略，言必從之。
units.en: Thereafter the Gao father and son treated him as their closest adviser; on every matter of governance and military strategy they followed his counsel.
units.literal: From then on the Jixing father and son relied on him as their inner confidant; in all planning for holding the domain and strategies for dispatching troops, they invariably followed his words.

units.zh: 乾祐元年夏，高從誨奏為武泰軍節度留後，依前荊南行軍司馬，加檢校太尉。
units.en: In the summer of Qianyou 1, Gao Conghui had him appointed military intendant of the Wutai Army while retaining his post as Jingnan campaigning marshal, with the honorary rank of Grand Commandant.
units.literal: In the summer of the first year of Qianyou, Gao Conghui memorialized to make him military intendant of the Wutai Army, continuing as before as Jingnan campaigning marshal, with the addition of honorary Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 後卒於江陵。
units.en: He later died at Jiangling.
units.literal: Later he died at Jiangling.

units.zh: 保勖，季興之幼子也。
units.en: Baoxu was Jixing's youngest son.
units.literal: Baoxu was the youngest son of Jixing.

units.zh: 鐘愛尤甚，季興在世時，或因事盛怒，左右不敢竊視，惟保勖一見，季興則怒自解，故荊人目之為「萬事休」。
units.en: Jixing doted on him above all; when Jixing flew into a rage his attendants dared not look up, yet a single sight of Baoxu would calm him—so the people of Jing nicknamed the boy "All Affairs Cease."
units.literal: He was especially cherished; while Jixing lived, he might fly into great rage over some matter and those around him dared not even glance aside—only when Baoxu appeared would Jixing's anger dissolve of itself; therefore the people of Jing called him "All Affairs Cease."

units.zh: 皇朝建隆四年春卒。
units.en: He died in the spring of Jianlong 4 of the Song.
units.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Jianlong of the Imperial Dynasty he died.

units.zh: 是歲，荊門之地不為高氏所有，則「萬事休」之言，蓋先兆也。
units.en: That same year the Gao lost Jingmen—so the nickname "All Affairs Cease" had been a prophecy.
units.literal: That year the territory of Jingmen was no longer held by the Gao clan—thus the words "All Affairs Cease" were surely an omen beforehand.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：高季興，本陵州陜人。
units.en: (From the 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Gao Jixing was originally from Shan in Lingzhou.
units.literal: (《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Gao Jixing was originally a man of Shan in Ling Prefecture.

units.zh: 為太祖裨將，出為郢州防禦使。
units.en: He served the Liang founder as a staff general and was posted as defender of Yingzhou.
units.literal: He was a staff general of the Founding Emperor and went out as military commissioner of Yingzhou.

units.zh: 時荊南成汭征鄂州，不利而卒，太祖命季興為荊南留後。
units.en: When Cheng Yun of Jingnan campaigned against Ezhou, met defeat, and died, the Liang founder appointed Jixing military intendant of Jingnan.
units.literal: At that time Cheng Yun of Jingnan campaigned against Ezhou, met with ill fortune and died; the Founding Emperor appointed Jixing military intendant of Jingnan.

units.zh: 到未幾，會武陵土豪雷彥恭作亂，季興破之，遂以功授荊南節鉞。
units.en: Soon after he arrived, the Wuling magnate Lei Yingong rebelled; Jixing crushed him and was invested with full authority over Jingnan.
units.literal: Not long after his arrival, the local magnate Lei Yingong of Wuling rebelled; Jixing defeated him and was therefore granted the command seal of Jingnan.

units.zh: 莊宗定天下，季興首入覲，因拜中書令，封南平王。
units.en: When Zhuangzong unified the empire, Jixing was the first regional ruler to pay court, and was made Director of the Secretariat and Prince of Nanping.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong settled the realm, Jixing was the first to come to audience, and was thereupon made Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping.

units.zh: 初，季興嘗從梁太祖出征，引軍早發，至逆旅，未曉，有嫗秉燭迎門，具禮甚厚。
units.en: Once, marching with the Liang founder, Jixing led his men out before dawn; at an inn an old woman met him at the door with a candle and treated him with extraordinary respect.
units.literal: Earlier, Jixing had once followed the Liang Founding Emperor on campaign, setting out with the army early; arriving at an inn before dawn, an old woman came forth with a candle to welcome him at the door and showed him very generous courtesy.

units.zh: 季興疑而問之，對曰：「妾適夢有人叩關，呼曰：『速起，速起，有裂土王來。』
units.en: Puzzled, Jixing asked why; she said, "I dreamed someone knocked at the gate shouting, 'Get up, get up—a king who will carve out his own realm is coming.'
units.literal: Jixing was suspicious and questioned her; she replied: "I have just dreamed that someone knocked at the gate, calling, 'Rise quickly, rise quickly—a king who will split the land is coming.'

units.zh: 及起，盥嗽畢，秉燭開門，而君子奄至，得非所謂王者耶？
units.en: I rose, rinsed my mouth, lit a candle, and opened the door—and here you are. Are you not that king?
units.literal: When I rose, finished rinsing my mouth, took a candle and opened the door, the noble gentleman had already arrived—is this not the king of whom it was spoken?

units.zh: 所以不敢褻慢爾。」
units.en: That is why I dared not receive you casually."
units.literal: That is why I did not dare treat you with disrespect."

units.zh: 季興喜，及來荊南，竟至封王。
units.en: Delighted, Jixing later came to Jingnan and was indeed enfeoffed as a prince.
units.literal: Jixing was pleased; when he came to Jingnan he did indeed reach enfeoffment as king.

units.zh: 高從誨，季興之庶子而處長，為性寬厚，雖士大夫不如也。
units.en: Gao Conghui was Jixing's son by a concubine but the eldest by age; he was so generous and mild that even literati could not match him.
units.literal: Gao Conghui was a secondary son of Jixing but the eldest in age; his nature was generous and mild—even scholar-officials did not surpass him.

units.zh: 天成中，季興叛，從誨力諫之，不從。
units.en: During Tiancheng, when Jixing rebelled, Conghui argued fiercely against it, but Jixing would not listen.
units.literal: During Tiancheng Jixing rebelled; Conghui strongly remonstrated but was not heeded.

units.zh: 及季興卒，朝廷知從誨忠，使嗣，亦封南平王。
units.en: After Jixing's death the court, knowing Conghui's loyalty, let him succeed and again enfeoffed him as Prince of Nanping.
units.literal: When Jixing died, the court knew Conghui was loyal and had him succeed, also enfeoffing him as Prince of Nanping.

units.zh: 初，季興之事梁也，每行軍，常以愛姬張氏自隨。
units.en: In his early days serving Liang, Jixing always took his favorite concubine Lady Zhang on campaign.
units.literal: When Jixing first served Liang, on every campaign he usually took his beloved concubine Lady Zhang with him.

units.zh: 一旦軍敗，攜之而竄，遇夜，誤入深澗中。
units.en: Once, after a defeat, he fled with her and, in the dark, blundered into a deep gorge.
units.literal: Once when the army was defeated he fled with her; encountering night, he mistakenly entered a deep ravine.

units.zh: 時張氏方妊行遲，季興恐為所累，俟其寢酣，以劍刺岸邊，而壓殺之，然後馳去。
units.en: Lady Zhang was pregnant and could not keep pace; fearing she would slow him, Jixing waited until she slept, brought down the bank with his sword to crush her, and rode off.
units.literal: At that time Lady Zhang was pregnant and walked slowly; Jixing feared she would encumber him, waited until she slept soundly, stabbed the bank with his sword to bring it down upon her and crush her to death, then galloped away.

units.zh: 既而岸欲崩，張氏且驚起，呼季興曰：「妾適夢大山崩而壓妾身，有神人披金甲執戈以手托之，遂免。」
units.en: As the bank gave way she woke and cried to Jixing, "I dreamed a mountain fell on me, but a god in golden armor held it up with his spear and I was spared."
units.literal: Soon the bank was about to collapse; Lady Zhang woke in alarm and called to Jixing: "I have just dreamed that a great mountain collapsed and pressed upon my body, but a divine man in golden armor holding a spear supported it with his hand, and I was spared."

units.zh: 季興聞之，謂必生貴子，遂挈之行，後生從誨。
units.en: Hearing this, he decided she would bear a noble son, took her with him, and she later bore Conghui.
units.literal: Hearing this, Jixing said she would surely bear a noble son, took her along, and later she gave birth to Conghui.

units.zh: 梁震，蜀郡人。
units.en: Liang Zhen was from Shu Commandery.
units.literal: Liang Zhen was a man of Shu Commandery.

units.zh: 有才略，登第後寓江陵，高季興素聞其名，欲任為判官。
units.en: Talented and capable, he settled at Jiangling after passing the civil examinations; Gao Jixing, who had long heard of him, wished to make him chief administrator.
units.literal: He had talent and strategy; after passing the examinations he lodged at Jiangling; Gao Jixing had long heard his name and wished to appoint him as administrative aide.

units.zh: 震恥之，然難於拒，恐禍及，因謂季興曰：「本山野鄙夫也，非有意於爵祿，若公不以孤陋，令陪軍中末議，但白衣從事可矣。」
units.en: Ashamed yet afraid to refuse outright, Zhen told Jixing, "I am only a rustic with no ambition for office; if you will have me, let me join your councils in plain dress as a private adviser—that is enough."
units.literal: Zhen was ashamed of this, yet found it hard to refuse for fear of disaster, and therefore said to Jixing: "I am originally a rustic fellow of the hills and fields with no desire for rank and salary; if my lord does not disdain my lowliness, let me join the tail end of military deliberations as a plain-clothed attendant—that is enough."

units.zh: 季興奇而許之，自是震出入門下，稱前進士而已。
units.en: Jixing, impressed, agreed; thereafter Zhen attended him, calling himself simply a former jinshi.
units.literal: Jixing marveled at this and agreed; from then on Zhen came and went in his entourage, styling himself merely a former jinshi.

units.zh: 同光中，莊宗得天下，季興懼而入覲，時幕客皆贊成，震獨以為不可，謂季興曰：「大王本梁朝，與今上世稱仇敵，血戰二十年，卒為今上所滅，神器大寶雖歸其手，恐余怒未息，觀其舊將，得無加害之心，宜深慮焉。」
units.en: During Tongguang, when Zhuangzong unified the realm, a fearful Jixing went to court; his staff all urged him on, but Zhen alone objected: "You were a Liang man—the new emperor's hereditary enemy. After twenty years of war he destroyed you. Though the throne is his, his old generals may still wish you harm. Think carefully."
units.literal: During Tongguang Zhuangzong won the realm; Jixing feared this and went to audience; at the time all staff members urged approval, but Zhen alone thought it inadvisable and said to Jixing: "Your Highness was originally of the Liang court; with the present sovereign you were for generations called mortal enemies—twenty years of bloody war until you were finally destroyed by him; though the sacred vessel and great treasure have come into his hands, I fear lingering anger has not subsided; looking at his old generals, can there be no intent to harm? You should ponder this deeply."

units.zh: 季興不從。
units.en: Jixing would not heed him.
units.literal: Jixing did not listen.

units.zh: 及至，莊宗果欲留之，樞密郭崇韜切諫，以為不可：「天下既定，四方諸侯雖相繼稱慶，然不過子弟與將吏耳，惟季興而躬自入覲，可謂尊獎王室者也。
units.en: When he arrived, Zhuangzong did intend to detain him, but Guo Chongtao of the Privy Council argued fiercely against it: "The realm is settled. Other lords sent sons and officers to congratulate; only Jixing came in person—an act of honor to the throne.
units.literal: When he arrived, Zhuangzong indeed wished to detain him; Privy Councilor Guo Chongtao remonstrated urgently that it could not be done: "The realm is already settled; the regional lords of the four quarters, though they have congratulated one after another, are no more than sons, younger brothers, and military officers—only Jixing came in person to audience, which may be called honoring and rewarding the royal house.

units.zh: 禮待不聞加等，反欲留縶之，何以來遠臣？
units.en: You have not treated him with exceptional honor, yet you would imprison him—who will come from afar after that?
units.literal: His ceremonial treatment has not been heard to exceed the norm, yet you wish instead to detain and bind him—how will distant ministers come?

units.zh: 恐此事一行，則天下解體矣。」
units.en: If you do this, the empire will disintegrate."
units.literal: I fear that if this is done, the realm will fall apart."

units.zh: 莊宗遂令季興歸。
units.en: Zhuangzong then let Jixing go home.
units.literal: Zhuangzong thereupon ordered Jixing to return.

units.zh: 行已浹旬，莊宗易慮，遽以詔命襄州節度劉訓伺便囚之。
units.en: Ten days into his journey Zhuangzong changed his mind and ordered Liu Xun, military commissioner of Xiangzhou, to seize him at the first opportunity.
units.literal: He had been on the road for nearly ten days when Zhuangzong changed his mind and abruptly issued an edict ordering the military commissioner of Xiangzhou Liu Xun to seize him when opportunity offered.

units.zh: 而季興至襄州，就館而心動，謂吏曰：「吾方寸擾亂，得非朝廷使人追而殺吾耶！
units.en: When Jixing reached Xiangzhou and entered his lodging his heart misgave him; he told an attendant, "My mind is in turmoil—has the court sent men to pursue and kill me!
units.literal: When Jixing reached Xiangzhou and entered the lodge his heart was troubled; he said to an official: "My mind is in turmoil—could it be that the court has sent someone to pursue and kill me!

units.zh: 梁先輩之言中矣，與其住而生，不若去而死。」
units.en: Liang Zhen was right: better to flee and risk death than to remain and be killed."
units.literal: Senior Liang's words have hit the mark: better to leave and die than to stay and live."

units.zh: 遂棄輜重，與部曲趫健者數百人南走。
units.en: He abandoned his baggage train and fled south with several hundred of his fastest troops.
units.literal: He then abandoned baggage and fled south with several hundred swift and sturdy men of his command.

units.zh: 至鳳林關，已昏黑，於是斬關而去。
units.en: At Fenglin Pass, already in darkness, he cut his way through the gate and escaped.
units.literal: When he reached Fenglin Pass it was already dark; he then cut down the guards and passed through.

units.zh: 既而是夜三更，向之急遞果至襄州，劉訓料其去遠，不可追而止。
units.en: That night at the third watch the urgent order reached Xiangzhou; Liu Xun judged that Jixing was too far ahead to catch and gave up the pursuit.
units.literal: That same night at the third watch the urgent dispatch that had been sent did indeed reach Xiangzhou; Liu Xun judged that Jixing was already far away and could not be pursued, and stopped.

units.zh: 自是季興怨憤，以兵襲取復州之監利、玉沙二縣，命震草奏，請以江為界。
units.en: Thereafter, nursing his grievance, Jixing seized Jianli and Yusha in Fuzhou by force and had Zhen draft a memorial asking that the Yangzi be made the border.
units.literal: From then on Jixing nursed resentment and anger; with troops he seized the two counties of Jianli and Yusha in Fuzhou, ordered Zhen to draft a memorial, and requested that the Yangzi River serve as the boundary.

units.zh: 震又曰：「不可，若然則師必至矣，非大王之利也。」
units.en: Zhen objected again: "You must not—if you do, the imperial army will come, and that will not serve you."
units.literal: Zhen again said: "This cannot be done; if so the imperial army will surely come—it is not to Your Highness's advantage."

units.zh: 季興怒，卒使為之。
units.en: Jixing was furious but made him draft it anyway.
units.literal: Jixing was angry and in the end had him do it.

units.zh: 既而奏發，未幾，朝廷遣夏魯奇、房知溫等領兵來伐。
units.en: The memorial was sent; soon the court dispatched Xia Luqi, Fang Zhiwen, and others to attack him.
units.literal: Soon the memorial was sent; before long the court dispatched Xia Luqi, Fang Zhiwen, and others to lead troops against him.

units.zh: 季興登城望之，見其兵少，喜，欲開城出戰，震復諫曰：「大王何不思之甚耶！
units.en: Jixing climbed the wall, saw how few they were, and wanted to sally out; Zhen remonstrated again: "My lord, have you thought this through?
units.literal: Jixing mounted the wall to look at them, saw their troops were few, was pleased, and wished to open the city and go out to fight; Zhen again remonstrated: "Your Highness, why do you not think more deeply!

units.zh: 且朝廷禮樂征伐之所自出，兵雖小而勢實大，加以四方諸侯各以相吞噬為誌，但恨未見得其便耳。
units.en: The court is the source of all authority; though their force looks small, its power is vast. Every regional lord wants to swallow his neighbors and only waits for an opening.
units.literal: Moreover the court is the source of ritual, music, and punitive expeditions; though the army is small, its power is in truth great; add to this that the regional lords of the four quarters each aim to devour one another and only regret not yet finding the opportunity.

units.zh: 若大王不幸，或得一戰勝，則朝廷征兵於四方，其誰不欲仗順而起，以取大王之土地耶！
units.en: If you should win a battle, the court will summon armies from every direction—who would not rise to seize your territory in the name of loyalty!
units.literal: If Your Highness by misfortune should win a single battle, the court will levy troops from the four quarters—who would not wish to rise in the name of righteousness and seize Your Highness's lands!

units.zh: 如此則社稷休矣。
units.en: Your domain would be finished.
units.literal: In that case the altars of state would be finished.

units.zh: 為大王計者，莫若致書於主帥，且以牛酒為獻，然後上表自劾，如此則庶幾可保矣。
units.en: The wisest course is to write the commander, send cattle and wine as gifts, and submit a memorial of self-reproach—you may yet save yourself.
units.literal: For Your Highness's planning, nothing is better than sending a letter to the commander-in-chief and offering cattle and wine as gifts, then submitting a memorial impeaching yourself—thus you may perhaps be preserved.

units.zh: 不然，則非仆之所知也。」
units.en: Otherwise I cannot say what will become of you."
units.literal: Otherwise, that is not something your servant can foresee."

units.zh: 季興從之，果班師。
units.en: Jixing took his advice, and the imperial army withdrew.
units.literal: Jixing followed this advice, and the army indeed withdrew.

units.zh: 震之裨贊，皆此類也。
units.en: Zhen's counsel was always of this sort.
units.literal: Zhen's supportive counsel was all of this kind.

units.zh: 洎季興卒，子從誨繼立，震以從誨生於富貴，恐相知不深，遂辭居於龍山別業，自號處士。
units.en: When Jixing died and Conghui succeeded, Zhen, fearing that a man born to privilege would not know him well, retired to his estate on Long Mountain and called himself a recluse.
units.literal: When Jixing died and his son Conghui succeeded, Zhen, because Conghui had been born to wealth and rank and he feared they did not know each other deeply, resigned to live at his country estate on Long Mountain and styled himself a retired gentleman.

units.zh: 從誨見召，皆跨黃牛直抵廳事前下，呼從誨不以官閥，但郎君而已。
units.en: When summoned, he rode a yellow ox to the hall door and addressed Conghui not by title but simply as "young master."
units.literal: When Conghui summoned him, he always rode a yellow ox straight to the front of the hall, addressed Conghui not by rank or lineage but simply as "young master."

units.zh: 末年尤好篇詠，與僧齊已友善，貽之詩曰：「陳琳筆硯甘前席，角裏煙霞憶共眠。」
units.en: In his last years he loved poetry; befriending the monk Qiji, he sent him a verse: "Chen Lin's brush gladly took the front seat; Jiao Li's clouds recall our shared rest."
units.literal: In his later years he especially loved composing verse; he was friendly with the monk Qiji and presented him a poem: "Chen Lin's brush and inkstone gladly took the front mat; Jiao Li's mist and clouds recall sleeping together."

units.zh: 蓋以寫其高尚之趣也。）〉
units.en: Thus he expressed his refined tastes.) )〉
units.literal: This was to express his lofty temperament.) )〉

units.zh: 馬殷，字霸圖，許州鄢陵人也。
units.en: Ma Yin, whose courtesy name was Batu, came from Yanling in Xu Prefecture.
units.literal: Ma Yin, courtesy name Batu, was a native of Yanling in Xu Prefecture.

units.zh: 少為木工，及蔡賊秦宗權作亂，始應募從軍。
units.en: As a youth he worked as a carpenter; when Qin Zongquan of Cai rebelled, he enlisted.
units.literal: In youth he was a carpenter; when the Cai bandit Qin Zongquan rebelled, he first answered the call to enlist.

units.zh: 初，隨孫儒渡淮，陷廣陵。
units.en: He first followed Sun Ru across the Huai and took Guangling.
units.literal: At first he followed Sun Ru across the Huai and captured Guangling.

units.zh: 及儒敗於宣州，殷隨別將劉建峰過江西，連陷洪、鄂、潭、桂等州，建峰盡有湖南之地，遂自為潭帥。
units.en: After Sun Ru's defeat at Xuanzhou, Yin followed Liu Jianfeng into Jiangxi, capturing Hong, E, Tan, Gui, and other prefectures; when Jianfeng held all Hunan he made himself commander of Tan.
units.literal: When Ru was defeated at Xuanzhou, Yin followed the separate general Liu Jianfeng across Jiangxi, successively capturing Hong, E, Tan, Gui, and other prefectures; Jianfeng came to hold all the lands of Hunan and made himself commander of Tan.

units.zh: 頃之，建峰為部下所殺，潭人推行軍司馬張佶為帥。
units.en: Soon Jianfeng was killed by his own men, and the people of Tan elevated campaigning marshal Zhang Ji.
units.literal: Before long Jianfeng was killed by his subordinates, and the people of Tan promoted the campaigning marshal Zhang Ji as commander.

units.zh: 時殷方統兵攻邵州，佶曰：「吾才不及馬殷。」
units.en: Yin was then besieging Shaozhou; Ji said, "I am no match for Ma Yin."
units.literal: At that time Yin was commanding troops attacking Shaozhou; Ji said: "My talent does not match Ma Yin's."

units.zh: 即牒殷付以軍府事。
units.en: He immediately transferred command of the headquarters to Yin.
units.literal: He at once issued a dispatch handing military headquarters affairs to Yin.

units.zh: 殷自邵州旋軍，犒勞將士，誅害建峰者數十人，自為留後。
units.en: Yin marched back from Shaozhou, rewarded his troops, executed dozens of Jianfeng's killers, and made himself military intendant.
units.literal: Yin returned his army from Shaozhou, rewarded the officers and soldiers, executed several tens of those who had harmed Jianfeng, and made himself military intendant.

units.zh: 久之，朝廷命為湖南節度使，遂有潭、衡七州之地。
units.en: Eventually the court appointed him military commissioner of Hunan, giving him seven prefectures including Tan and Heng.
units.literal: After some time the court appointed him military commissioner of Hunan, and he came to hold the seven prefectures of Tan, Heng, and the rest.

units.zh: 唐天復中，楊行密急攻江夏，杜洪求援於荊南，成汭舉舟師援之。
units.en: During the Tang Tianfu era, as Yang Xingmi besieged Jiangxia, Du Hong sought aid from Jingnan and Cheng Yun sent a fleet to help.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era of Tang, Yang Xingmi pressed the attack on Jiangxia; Du Hong sought aid from Jingnan, and Cheng Yun raised a fleet to assist him.

units.zh: 時澧朗節度使雷彥恭乘汭出師，襲取荊州，載其寶貨，焚毀州城而去。
units.en: Lei Yingong, military commissioner of Li and Lang, seized the moment to raid Jingzhou, loot its treasures, burn the city, and withdraw.
units.literal: At that time Lei Yingong, military commissioner of Li and Lang, took advantage of Yun's departure to raid Jingzhou, loaded its treasures, burned the prefectural city, and left.

units.zh: 彥恭東連行密，斷江、嶺行商之路，殷與高季興合勢攻彥恭於澧朗。
units.en: Yingong allied with Xingmi in the east and blocked trade along the Yangzi and mountain routes; Yin and Gao Jixing combined forces to attack him in Li and Lang.
units.literal: Yingong linked east with Xingmi and cut the routes of merchants on the river and across the ranges; Yin joined forces with Gao Jixing to attack Yingong at Li and Lang.

units.zh: 數年，擒之，盡有其地，及以張佶為朗州節度使，由是兵力雄盛。
units.en: Within a few years they captured him and took his territory, appointing Zhang Ji military commissioner of Langzhou; their power grew formidable.
units.literal: After several years they captured him and came to hold all his territory; they also made Zhang Ji military commissioner of Langzhou; thus their military strength became formidable.

units.zh: 殷於梁貞明中，為時姑息，所求皆允，累官至守太師、兼中書令，封楚王。
units.en: During Liang Zhenming, Yin found the times indulgent and every request was granted; he rose to Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed King of Chu.
units.literal: During Zhenming of Liang, Yin found the times indulgent and every request was granted; he rose in rank to Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed as King of Chu.

units.zh: 又上章請依唐秦王故事，乃加天策上將軍之號。
units.en: He also petitioned to follow the Tang Prince of Qin precedent and was given the title Grand General of the Heavenly Stratagem.
units.literal: He also submitted a memorial asking to follow the precedent of the Tang Prince of Qin and was given the title Grand General of the Heavenly Stratagem.

units.zh: 又請官位內添制置靜江、武平、寧遠等軍事，皆從之。
units.en: He further asked that control of the Jingjiang, Wuping, Ningyuan, and other armies be added to his office, and all were granted.
units.literal: He further asked that within his office be added control of the Jingjiang, Wuping, Ningyuan, and other military commands, and all were granted.

units.zh: 既封楚王，仍請依唐諸王行臺故事，置諸天官幕府，有文苑學士之號，知詔令之名，總制二十餘州，自署官吏，征賦不供，民間采茶，並抑而買之。
units.en: Once enfeoffed King of Chu, he still asked to follow the Tang precedent of princely field headquarters, establishing a full staff with Literary Garden Academicians and authority over edicts; he controlled more than twenty prefectures, appointed officials himself, withheld taxes, and monopolized tea gathered among the people.
units.literal: Once enfeoffed as King of Chu, he still asked to follow the Tang precedent of princely field headquarters, establishing a full staff of heavenly offices with the title Literary Garden Academician and authority over edicts and orders; he controlled more than twenty prefectures, appointed officials himself, withheld tax payments, and monopolized the purchase of tea gathered among the people.

units.zh: 又自鑄鉛鐵錢，凡天下商賈所賫寶貨入其境者，只以土產鉛鐵博易之無餘，遂致一方富盛，窮極奢侈，貢奉朝廷不過茶數萬斤而已。
units.en: He also cast his own lead and iron coinage; whatever treasure merchants brought into his territory was exchanged only for local lead and iron until nothing remained, making the region rich and extravagance extreme, while tribute to the court amounted to no more than several tens of thousands of jin of tea.
units.literal: He also cast his own lead and iron coinage; whatever treasure goods merchants from all the realm brought into his territory were exchanged only for local lead and iron until nothing remained, so that one region grew rich and extravagance reached its limit, while tribute to the court amounted to no more than several tens of thousands of jin of tea.

units.zh: 於中原賣茶之利，歲百萬計。
units.en: Profits from selling tea in the Central Plains ran to a million a year.
units.literal: The profit from selling tea in the Central Plains amounted to a million each year.

units.zh: 唐同光初，首修職貢，復授太師、兼尚書令、楚王。
units.en: At the beginning of Tang Tongguang he first restored official tribute and was again given Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and King of Chu.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang of Tang he first restored official tribute and was again given Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and King of Chu.

units.zh: 天成初，加守尚書令。
units.en: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was further made Acting Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was further made Acting Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 長興二年十一月十日，薨於位，時年七十有八。
units.en: On the tenth day of the eleventh month of Changxing 2 he died in office at the age of seventy-eight.
units.literal: On the tenth day of the eleventh month of the second year of Changxing he died in office, aged seventy-eight.

units.zh: 明宗聞之，廢朝三日，謚曰武穆。
units.en: When Mingzong heard of it he suspended court for three days and gave the posthumous title Wumu.
units.literal: When Mingzong heard of it he suspended court for three days and gave the posthumous title Wumu.

units.zh: 子希聲嗣。
units.en: His son Xisheng succeeded him.
units.literal: His son Xisheng succeeded.

units.zh: 初，殷微時，隱隱見神人侍側，因默記其形像。
units.en: In his humble youth Yin had dimly seen a spirit attendant at his side and memorized its features.
units.literal: When Yin was still obscure, he dimly saw a divine being attending at his side and silently memorized its form.

units.zh: 及貴，因謁衡山廟，睹廟中神人塑像，宛如微時所見者。
units.en: After he rose to power he visited the Heng Mountain temple and found the deity's statue identical to what he had seen long before.
units.literal: When he had risen to eminence he visited the Heng Mountain temple and saw the sculpted image of the divine being in the temple, exactly like what he had seen in his humble days.

units.zh: 則知人之貴者，必有陰物護之，豈偶然哉！
units.en: Surely those destined for greatness are guarded by unseen powers—this was no accident!
units.literal: Thus one knows that those who attain eminence must have yin spirits protecting them—how could it be accidental!

units.zh: 希範，晉天福中，授江南諸道都統，又加天策上將軍。
units.en: During Later Jin Tianfu, Xifan was made overall commander of the Jiangnan circuits and Grand General of the Heavenly Stratagem.
units.literal: Xifan, during Tianfu of Jin, was appointed overall commander of the Jiangnan circuits and additionally made Grand General of the Heavenly Stratagem.

units.zh: 谿州洞蠻彭士愁寇辰、澧二州，希範討平之。
units.en: Peng Shichou, a tribal leader of Xizhou, raided Chen and Li; Xifan defeated him.
units.literal: Peng Shichou, a cave tribesman of Xizhou, raided Chen and Li prefectures; Xifan campaigned and pacified him.

units.zh: 士愁以五州乞盟，乃銘於銅柱。
units.en: Shichou surrendered five prefectures to sue for peace, and the terms were inscribed on a bronze pillar.
units.literal: Shichou offered the five prefectures to sue for peace, and an inscription was cast on a bronze pillar.

units.zh: 希範自言漢伏波將軍援之後，故鑄銅柱以繼之。
units.en: Xifan claimed descent from the Han general Ma Yuan and cast a bronze pillar to emulate his precedent.
units.literal: Xifan said of himself that he was a descendant of the Han General Who Quells the Waves Ma Yuan, and therefore cast a bronze pillar to continue that tradition.

units.zh: 〈（案：此傳有闕文，《馬希廣》、《希萼傳》全篇俱佚。
units.en: (Note: this biography is defective; the biographies of 《Ma Xiguang》 and 《Ma Xi'e》 are entirely lost.
units.literal: (Note: this biography has lacunae; the biographies of 《Ma Xiguang》 and 《Ma Xi'e》 are entirely lost.

units.zh: 《五代史補》：高郁為武穆王謀臣，莊宗素聞其名，及有天下，且欲離間之。
units.en: From the Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Gao Yu was strategist to Prince Wumu; Zhuangzong had long heard of him and, once he ruled the realm, sought to drive a wedge between them.
units.literal: Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Gao Yu was a strategist of Prince Wumu; Zhuangzong had long heard his name, and once he possessed the realm wished moreover to sow discord.

units.zh: 會武穆王使其子希範入覲，莊宗以希範年少易激發，因其敷奏敏速，乃拊其背曰：「國人皆言馬家社稷必為高郁所取，今有子如此，高郁安得取此耶！」
units.en: When Prince Wumu sent Xifan to court, Zhuangzong—finding the youth quick-witted and easily provoked—clapped his back and said, "Everyone says the Ma domain will fall to Gao Yu—but with a son like this, how could Yu seize it!"
units.literal: It happened that Prince Wumu sent his son Xifan to audience; Zhuangzong, because Xifan was young and easily stirred, and because his presentation was swift and keen, clapped his back and said: "The people all say the Ma family's altars will surely be taken by Gao Yu—yet with a son like this, how could Gao Yu take them!"

units.zh: 希範居常嫉郁，忽聞莊宗言，深以為然。
units.en: Xifan, who had long resented Yu, took the emperor's words to heart.
units.literal: Xifan had always resented Yu; hearing Zhuangzong's words he deeply believed them.

units.zh: 及歸，告武穆請誅之，武穆笑曰：「主上爭戰得天下，能用機數，以郁資吾霸業，故欲間之耳！
units.en: On returning he urged Wumu to execute Yu; Wumu laughed and said, "The emperor won the realm by war and knows stratagems—he uses Yu to support our power and wants to divide us!
units.literal: When he returned he told Wumu to request Yu's execution; Wumu laughed and said: "Our lord won the realm through battle and can use stratagems; because Yu supports our hegemony, he wishes to sow discord—that is all!

units.zh: 若梁朝罷王彥章兵權也。
units.en: It is like when the Liang court stripped Wang Yanzhang of command.
units.literal: It is like the Liang court stripping Wang Yanzhang of military authority.

units.zh: 蓋遭此計，必至破滅，今汝誅郁，正落其彀中，慎勿言也。」
units.en: Whoever falls for this plot is ruined; if you kill Yu now you walk into the trap—say nothing of it."
units.literal: Those who fall for this scheme are sure to be destroyed; if you now execute Yu you will fall right into the trap—be careful not to speak of it."

units.zh: 希範以武穆不決，禍在朝夕，因使誣告郁謀反而族滅之。
units.en: Thinking Wumu indecisive and disaster imminent, Xifan had Yu falsely accused of treason and his entire clan executed.
units.literal: Because Wumu would not decide, Xifan thought disaster was imminent and had Yu falsely accused of plotting rebellion and his clan exterminated.

units.zh: 自是軍中之政，往往失序，識者痛之。
units.en: Thereafter military affairs often fell into disorder, to the grief of the wise.
units.literal: From then on military administration often fell into disorder, and those with insight grieved over it.

units.zh: 初，郁與武穆俱起行陣，郁貪且僭，常以所居之井不甚清澈，思所以澄汰之，乃用銀葉護其四方，自內至外皆然，謂之「拓裏」，其奉養過差，皆此類也，故莊宗得以媒蘗。
units.en: Yu had risen with Wumu from the ranks but grew greedy and arrogant; dissatisfied with his well water, he lined it with silver leaves inside and out in what he called "tuoli"—extravagances of this sort gave Zhuangzong material for slander.
units.literal: Earlier, Yu and Wumu had both risen from the ranks; Yu was greedy and overstepping, often finding the well at his residence not very clear and thinking how to clarify it, using silver leaves to shield all four sides from inside to outside, calling this "tuoli"; his maintenance exceeded proper measure in ways of this kind, and therefore Zhuangzong was able to sow slander.

units.zh: 自後陰晦中見郁，後竟為所患爾。
units.en: Afterward he saw Yu's ghost in the gloom and was ultimately haunted by him.
units.literal: Afterward in dim gloom he would see Yu, and in the end was indeed afflicted by him.

units.zh: 馬希範，武穆之嫡子，性奢侈，嗣位未幾，乞依故事置天策府僚屬，於是擢從事有才行者，有若都統判官李鐸、靜江府節度判官潘玘、武安軍節度判官拓拔坦、都統掌書記李臯、鎮南節度判官李莊、昭順軍節度判官徐收、澧州觀察判官彭繼英、江南觀察判官廖圖、昭順軍觀察判官徐中雅、靜江府掌書記鄧懿文、武平軍節度掌書記李松年、鎮南軍節度掌書記衛嚴、昭順軍觀察支使彭繼勛、武平軍節度推官蕭銖、桂管觀察推官何仲舉、武安軍節度巡官孟元暉、容管節度推官劉昭禹等十八人，並為學士。
units.en: Ma Xifan, Wumu's legitimate son, was extravagant; soon after succeeding he asked to establish a Heavenly Stratagem Bureau on the old model and appointed eighteen able staff members—including Li Duo, Pan Qi, Tuoba Tan, Li Gao, He Zhongju, and Liu Zhaoyu—as academicians.
units.literal: Ma Xifan, the legitimate son of Wumu, was by nature extravagant; not long after succeeding he requested according to precedent to establish staff of the Heavenly Stratagem Bureau, and thereupon promoted eighteen men of ability and conduct among his staff—such as the overall commander's aide Li Duo, Jingjiang circuit military aide Pan Qi, Wu'an army military aide Tuoba Tan, overall command secretary Li Gao, Zhennan military aide Li Zhuang, Zhaoshun army military aide Xu Shou, Li prefecture observation aide Peng Jiying, Jiangnan observation aide Liao Tu, Zhaoshun army observation aide Xu Zhongya, Jingjiang secretary Deng Yiwen, Wuping army secretary Li Songnian, Zhennan army secretary Wei Yan, Zhaoshun army observation adjutant Peng Jixun, Wuping army legal aide Xiao Zhu, Guiguan observation legal aide He Zhongju, Wu'an army patrol officer Meng Yuanhui, Rongguan legal aide Liu Zhaoyu, and others—all as academicians.

units.zh: 其餘列校，自袁友恭、張少敵等各以次授任。
units.en: Other commanders, from Yuan Yougong and Zhang Shaodi down, received appointments in turn.
units.literal: The remaining commanders, from Yuan Yougong and Zhang Shaodi onward, were each given appointments in order.

units.zh: 莫不大興土木，以建興府庭，其最為壯麗者即有九龍、金華等殿。
units.en: All launched vast construction projects for the capital; the grandest were the Nine Dragons and Golden Splendor halls.
units.literal: All greatly raised earthworks and timber to build the halls of the capital prefecture; the most magnificent were the Nine Dragons and Golden Splendor halls.

units.zh: 殿之成也，用丹砂塗其壁，凡用數十萬斤石，每僚吏謁見，將升殿，但覺丹砂之氣，藹然襲人，其費用也皆此類。
units.en: The completed halls were coated with cinnabar using hundreds of thousands of jin of ore; officials ascending for audience were met by thick fumes of cinnabar—such was the scale of his extravagance.
units.literal: When the halls were completed, cinnabar was used to coat the walls, totaling several hundred thousand jin of ore; whenever staff came to audience and were about to ascend the hall, they felt the cinnabar vapor thickly assail them—the expenses were all of this kind.

units.zh: 初，教令既下，主者以丹砂非卒致之物，相顧憂色。
units.en: When the order was first issued, the supervisors despaired, for cinnabar could not be procured overnight.
units.literal: At first, when the order was issued, those in charge, because cinnabar was not something quickly obtainable, looked at one another with worried faces.

units.zh: 居無何，東境山崩，湧出丹砂，委積如丘陵，於是收而用之。
units.en: Soon a mountain in the east collapsed, spewing cinnabar in heaps like hills, and they gathered it for use.
units.literal: Before long a mountain in the eastern border collapsed and cinnabar poured forth, heaped like hills; they then collected and used it.

units.zh: 契丹南侵，聞其事，以為希範非常人，遽使冊為尚父。
units.en: When the Khitans invaded the south and heard of this, they judged Xifan extraordinary and promptly invested him as Imperial Father.
units.literal: When the Khitans invaded south they heard of this matter, thought Xifan no ordinary man, and quickly sent envoys to invest him as Imperial Father.

units.zh: 希範得冊，以為契丹推奉，欣然當之矣。
units.en: Xifan, taking this as Khitan endorsement, gladly accepted the title.
units.literal: Xifan received the investiture, took it as Khitan elevation, and gladly accepted the role.

units.zh: 丁思僅素有才略，為馬氏騎將。
units.en: Ding Sijin was a talented cavalry commander of the Ma house.
units.literal: Ding Sijin had always possessed talent and strategy and was a cavalry general of the Ma clan.

units.zh: 以希範受契丹冊命，深恥之，因謂希範曰：「今朝廷失守，正忠臣義士奮發之時，使馳檄四方，引軍直趨京師，驅契丹，天子反正，然後凱還，如此則齊桓、晉文不足數矣。
units.en: He was deeply shamed that Xifan accepted Khitan investiture and urged him: "The throne is lost—this is the hour for loyal men to act: proclaim to the realm, march on the capital, drive out the Khitans, restore the emperor, and return in triumph—you would surpass Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin.
units.literal: Because Xifan accepted Khitan investiture he was deeply shamed and therefore said to Xifan: "Now the court has lost its hold—this is the moment for loyal ministers and righteous men to rouse themselves: send proclamations to the four quarters, lead the army straight to the capital, drive out the Khitans, restore the Son of Heaven, then return in triumph—thus Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin would not be worth counting.

units.zh: 時不可失，願大王急圖之。」
units.en: The moment will not wait—my lord, act at once."
units.literal: The time cannot be lost—I beg Your Highness to plan this urgently."

units.zh: 希範本無遠略，加以興作府署未畢，不忍棄去，遂寢思僅之謀。
units.en: Xifan lacked long-range vision and could not bear to abandon his unfinished palaces—he set the plan aside.
units.literal: Xifan originally had no long-range strategy; moreover his construction of the capital offices was not finished and he could not bear to abandon it—he therefore set aside Sijin's plan.

units.zh: 思僅不勝其憤，謂所親曰：「古人疾沒世而名不稱，今遭逢擾攘，不能立功於天下，反顧戀數間屋子乎！
units.en: Sijin, unable to contain his rage, told his intimates, "The ancients feared dying without renown; in this chaos we cannot serve the realm yet cling to a few rooms of a palace!
units.literal: Sijin could not contain his anger and said to those close to him: "The ancients feared dying without their names being spoken; now in this turmoil we cannot establish merit under heaven yet cling to a few rooms of a house!

units.zh: 誠可痛也。」
units.en: It is heartbreaking."
units.literal: This is truly painful."

units.zh: 自是思僅常怏怏。
units.en: From then on Sijin brooded in discontent.
units.literal: From then on Sijin was often discontented.

units.zh: 文昭王夫人彭氏，封秦國夫人，常往城北報恩寺燒香。
units.en: Lady Peng, consort of Prince Wenzhao and enfeoffed as Lady of Qin, often went to Bao'en Temple north of the city to burn incense.
units.literal: Lady Peng, consort of Prince Wenzhao, enfeoffed as Lady of Qin, often went to Bao'en Temple north of the city to burn incense.

units.zh: 時僧魁謂之長老，問曰：「夫人誰家婦女？」
units.en: The monk Kui, called the elder, asked, "Madam, whose wife are you?"
units.literal: At that time the monk Kui, called the elder, asked: "Madam, whose household's woman are you?"

units.zh: 彭氏大怒，索檐子疾驅而歸，文昭驚曰：「何歸之速也？」
units.en: Furious, Lady Peng called for her sedan and rushed home; Wenzhao asked in alarm, "Why so soon?"
units.literal: Lady Peng was greatly angered, called for her sedan and hurried home; Wenzhao was startled and said: "Why return so quickly?"

units.zh: 夫人曰：「今日好沒興，被個老禿賊問妾是誰家婦女，且大凡婦女皆不善之辭，安得對妾而發！」
units.en: She said, "What ill luck—a bald old monk asked whose wife I was! Such words are unlucky for any woman—how dare he say them to me!"
units.literal: The lady said: "Today brought bad luck—a bald old thief asked whose household's woman I was; moreover such words are generally inauspicious for women—how could he speak them to me!"

units.zh: 文昭笑曰：「此所謂禪機也，夫人宜答弟子是彭家女，馬家婦，是則通其理矣，何怒之有乎！」
units.en: Wenzhao laughed: "That was a Chan teaching—you should have answered, 'I am a Peng daughter and Ma wife.' That would have met his point—why be angry?"
units.literal: Wenzhao laughed and said: "This is what is called a Chan pivot; madam should have answered, 'Your disciple is a daughter of the Peng house and wife of the Ma house'—that would have penetrated the principle; why be angry!"

units.zh: 夫人素負才智，恥不能對，乃曰：「如此則妾所謂無見性也。」
units.en: Intelligent as she was, she was ashamed of her failure and said, "Then I showed no insight at all."
units.literal: The lady, who had always possessed intelligence, was shamed at not having replied and said: "In that case what I showed was lack of insight."

units.zh: 於是慚赧數日。
units.en: She blushed for days afterward.
units.literal: She was then abashed for several days.

units.zh: 石文德，連州人。
units.en: Shi Wende was from Lianzhou.
units.literal: Shi Wende was a man of Lianzhou.

units.zh: 形質矬陋，好學，尤工詩。
units.en: Short and homely in appearance, he loved learning and was especially skilled at poetry.
units.literal: Short and ugly in form, he loved learning and was especially skilled at poetry.

units.zh: 霸國時，屢獻詩求用，文昭以其寢陋，未曾禮待，文德由是窮悴。
units.en: During the kingdom's rise he repeatedly submitted poems seeking office, but Wenzhao, finding him homely, never treated him courteously, and Wende fell into poverty.
units.literal: During the hegemonic state he repeatedly presented poems seeking employment, but Wenzhao, because he was homely in sleep, never treated him with courtesy; Wende was thereby reduced to poverty and distress.

units.zh: 有南宅王子者，素重士，延於門下，其後文昭知之，亦兼怒王宅，欲庭辱文德而逐之。
units.en: A prince of the Southern Residence, who had always valued scholars, took Wende into his household. When Wenzhao learned of this he was angry at the prince's residence as well and wished to humiliate Wende in open court and drive him out.
units.literal: There was a prince of the Southern Residence who had always valued scholars and kept Wende in his household. Later Wenzhao learned of it and was also angry at the prince's residence, wishing to humiliate Wende in open court and drive him away.

units.zh: 居無何，秦國夫人彭氏薨，文昭傷悼，乃命有文學者各撰挽詞，文德亦獻十餘篇，其一聯云：「月沈湘浦冷，花謝漢宮秋。」
units.en: Before long Lady Peng, the Lady of Qin, died. Wenzhao mourned and ordered literary men to compose elegies; Wende submitted more than ten pieces, one couplet reading, "The moon sinks cold at the Xiang shore; flowers fade in autumn at the Han palace."
units.literal: Before long Lady Peng, Lady of Qin, died. Wenzhao mourned and ordered men of letters each to compose elegiac verses; Wende also presented more than ten pieces, one couplet reading: "The moon sinks cold at the Xiang shore; flowers fade in autumn at the Han palace."

units.zh: 文昭覽之大驚，曰：「文德有此作用，吾但以寢陋而輕之，乃不如南宮小兒卻能知賢耶！」
units.en: Wenzhao was astonished and said, "Wende has such talent—I only slighted him for his looks, yet I am not even the equal of that Southern Residence lad in recognizing worth!"
units.literal: Wenzhao read them and was greatly startled, saying: "Wende has such talent—I only slighted him for being homely, yet I am not even the equal of that Southern Residence lad in knowing worth!"

units.zh: 於是始召文德而愧謝之。
units.en: He then summoned Wende and apologized in shame.
units.literal: Thereupon he at last summoned Wende and apologized in shame.

units.zh: 未幾，承制授水部員外郎，充融州刺史。
units.en: Before long he was commissioned Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and appointed prefect of Rongzhou.
units.literal: Before long, by imperial commission, he was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and served as prefect of Rongzhou.

units.zh: 文德晚尤好著述，乃撰《大唐新纂》十三卷，多名人遺事，詞雖不工，事或可采，時以多聞許之。
units.en: In his later years Wende especially loved writing and compiled the New Compendium of the Great Tang in thirteen scrolls, containing many anecdotes of famous men; though the style was not polished, the material was worth collecting, and contemporaries acknowledged him as widely learned.
units.literal: In his later years Wende especially loved writing and compiled the New Compendium of the Great Tang in thirteen scrolls, containing many anecdotes of famous men; though the style was not polished, the material was worth collecting, and people of the time acknowledged him as widely learned.

units.zh: 何仲舉，營道人。
units.en: He Zhongju was from Yingdao.
units.literal: He Zhongju was a man of Yingdao.

units.zh: 美姿容，年十三，俊邁絕倫。
units.en: Handsome and at thirteen already exceptionally gifted,
units.literal: Handsome in appearance, at thirteen he was surpassingly brilliant.

units.zh: 時家貧，輸稅不及限，李臯為營道令，怒之，乃荷項系獄，將槚楚焉。
units.en: his family was too poor to pay taxes on time; Magistrate Li Gao, enraged, had him shackled and imprisoned for beating.
units.literal: His family was poor and could not meet the tax quota; Li Gao was magistrate of Yingdao, was angry, had a cangue placed on his neck and bound him in prison, and was about to beat him.

units.zh: 或有言於臯曰：「此子雖丱，能為詩，往往間立成，希明府一察之。」
units.en: Someone told Gao, "Though young, this boy composes poetry on the spot—please examine him."
units.literal: Someone said to Gao: "This boy, though young, can compose poetry and often completes pieces on the spot—I hope the magistrate will examine him."

units.zh: 臯聞，遽召而問曰：「知汝有文，且速敏，今日之事，若能文不加點，為一篇以自述，吾當貸汝。」
units.en: Gao summoned him and said, "I know you are clever with words; if you can write a self-account without revision, I will spare you."
units.literal: Gao heard this and quickly summoned and asked him: "I know you have literary talent and are quick and keen; regarding today's matter, if you can write a piece about yourself without adding a dot of revision, I will spare you."

units.zh: 仲舉援筆而成，曰：「似玉來投獄，拋家去就枷。
units.en: Zhongju wrote at once: "Like jade cast into prison, leaving home for the stocks.
units.literal: Zhongju took up the brush and completed it, saying: "Like jade coming to cast itself into prison, leaving home to accept the cangue.

units.zh: 可憐兩片木，夾卻一枝花。」
units.en: Pitiable—two boards clamping a single blossom."
units.literal: Pitiable—two pieces of wood clamping a single spray of flowers."

units.zh: 臯大驚，因自為脫枷，延上廳與之抗禮，自是仲舉始銳意就學。
units.en: Amazed, Gao removed the shackles himself, received him in the hall as an equal, and from then on Zhongju devoted himself to study.
units.literal: Gao was greatly startled, removed the cangue himself, invited him to the hall and treated him as an equal, and from then on Zhongju began to study with keen purpose.

units.zh: 天成中入洛，時秦王為河南尹，尤重士，仲舉與張杭、江文蔚俱遊其門。
units.en: During Tiancheng he went to Luoyang, where the Prince of Qin, military commissioner of Henan, prized scholars; Zhongju associated with Zhang Hang and Jiang Wenwei at his court.
units.literal: During Tiancheng he entered Luoyang; at that time the Prince of Qin was military commissioner of Henan and especially valued scholars; Zhongju, together with Zhang Hang and Jiang Wenwei, all frequented his gate.

units.zh: 及其東薦也，公舉數百人，獨以仲舉為擅場，仲舉因獻詩曰：「碧雲章句才離手，紫府神仙盡點頭。」
units.en: At the metropolitan examination hundreds competed, but Zhongju alone dominated; he presented a verse: "Azure-cloud lines just leave the hand, purple-palace immortals all nod approval."
units.literal: When the eastern recommendation was held, several hundred men were nominated publicly, but Zhongju alone was judged to dominate the field; Zhongju therefore presented a poem: "Azure-cloud verses just left the hand, purple-palace immortals all nod their heads."

units.zh: 秦王大悅，稱賞不已，故一舉上第。
units.en: The prince was delighted and praised him endlessly; Zhongju passed at the top of his class.
units.literal: The Prince of Qin was greatly pleased and praised him without cease; thus he passed the examination at one attempt.

units.zh: 及歸，遇文昭馬氏承制，依唐太宗故事，於天策府置十八學士，以臯為學士之首，且執政柄，而仲舉自以出於臯之門下，雖策名中朝，事臯未嘗暫懈，臯感悅，遂加引用。
units.en: On returning he found Prince Wenzhao of Ma following Tang Taizong's precedent in appointing eighteen Heavenly Stratagem academicians, with Gao at their head and in power; though Zhongju had passed the central examinations, he never ceased serving Gao, who was moved and promoted him.
units.literal: When he returned, it happened that Prince Wenzhao of the Ma clan, exercising imperial authority, following the precedent of Emperor Taizong of Tang established eighteen academicians at the Heavenly Stratagem Bureau, with Gao as head academician who also held governmental power; Zhongju, considering himself from Gao's school, though he had attained rank at the central court, never slackened in serving Gao even briefly; Gao was moved and pleased and thereupon promoted his use.

units.zh: 未幾，與之同列，及出，又為全、衡二州刺史。
units.en: Soon he stood as Gao's equal in rank and later served as prefect of Quan and Heng.
units.literal: Before long he stood in the same rank with him, and when sent out served as prefect of Quan and Heng prefectures.

units.zh: 先是，湖南尤多詩人，其最顯者有沈彬、廖凝、劉昭禹、尚顏、齊己、虛中之徒，而仲舉在諸公間尤為輕淺，惟李臯獨推許之，往往對眾吟《秋日晚望詩》曰：「樹迎高鳥歸深野，雲傍斜陽過遠山。」
units.en: Hunan had many poets—Shen Bin, Liao Ning, Liu Zhaoyu, Shang Yan, Qiji, Xu Zhong, and others—and Zhongju was thought the shallowest; only Li Gao praised him, often reciting before company his "Autumn Evening View": "Trees welcome birds to the deep wilds; clouds drift past distant hills in the slanting sun."
units.literal: Earlier Hunan had especially many poets; the most prominent were Shen Bin, Liao Ning, Liu Zhaoyu, Shangyan, Qiji, Xuzhong, and the like, while among these gentlemen Zhongju was especially considered shallow; only Li Gao alone praised him, often reciting before the assembly his "Poem on Gazing in the Evening of an Autumn Day": "Trees welcome high birds returning to the deep wilds; clouds beside the slanting sun pass distant mountains."

units.zh: 以足扣地，嘆曰：「何仲舉乃詩家之高逸者也，諸官見取舍，其餘奴嶽，乃間氣爾。」
units.en: He stamped the floor and sighed, "He Zhongju is poetry's true recluse—you officials may judge as you will; the rest are mere hillocks of talent."
units.literal: He tapped the ground with his foot and sighed: "He Zhongju is a lofty recluse among poets; you officials see and choose— the rest are servile hills, merely sporadic breaths of talent."

units.zh: 故仲舉感臯之見知，卒能自奮，至於名節，亦終始無玷，論者以臯有知人之鑒。
units.en: Grateful for Gao's recognition, Zhongju applied himself and preserved his integrity to the end; critics credited Gao with true discernment.
units.literal: Therefore Zhongju was moved by Gao's recognition, was ultimately able to exert himself, and as to reputation and integrity was without stain from beginning to end; commentators considered that Gao had the discernment to know men.

units.zh: 歐陽彬，衡山人。
units.en: Ouyang Bin was from Hengshan.
units.literal: Ouyang Bin was a man of Hengshan.

units.zh: 世為縣吏，至彬特好學，工於詞賦。
units.en: His family had served as county clerks for generations, but Bin loved learning and excelled at poetry.
units.literal: His family for generations were county clerks; Bin in particular loved learning and was skilled at rhapsodies and fu.

units.zh: 馬氏之有湖南也，彬將希其用，乃攜所著詣府，求見之禮，必先通名紙。
units.en: When the Ma clan held Hunan, Bin hoped for employment, brought his writings to headquarters, and sought an audience—which required a calling card.
units.literal: When the Ma clan came to hold Hunan, Bin hoped to win their employment, carried his writings to the headquarters, and sought the rite of audience, which required first presenting a calling card.

units.zh: 有掌客吏，眾謂樊知客，好賄，陰使人謂彬曰：「足下之來，非徒然也，實欲顯族致身，而不以一物為貺，其可乎？」
units.en: The reception officer, known as Guest-Officer Fan, loved bribes; someone secretly told Bin, "You come seeking advancement—can you offer nothing?"
units.literal: There was a reception officer whom everyone called Guest-Officer Fan, who loved bribes; he secretly had someone tell Bin: "Your coming is not for nothing—you truly wish to elevate your clan and advance yourself, yet offer not a single gift—is that acceptable?"

units.zh: 彬恥以賄進，竟不與。
units.en: Ashamed to buy his way in, Bin refused.
units.literal: Bin was ashamed to advance through bribery and in the end gave nothing.

units.zh: 既而樊氏怒，擲名紙於地曰：「豈吏人之子欲幹謁王侯耶！」
units.en: Fan flung the card down in anger: "Does a clerk's son think he can solicit princes!"
units.literal: Fan then grew angry, threw the calling card to the ground, and said: "Does a clerk's son wish to solicit audience with kings and marquises!"

units.zh: 彬深恨之，因退而為詩曰：「無錢將乞樊知客，名紙生毛不為通。」
units.en: Deeply resentful, Bin wrote: "Without money one begs Guest-Officer Fan; the calling card grows mold and will not pass."
units.literal: Bin deeply resented this, withdrew, and composed a poem: "Without money one must beg Guest-Officer Fan; the calling card grows mold and will not pass through."

units.zh: 因而落魄街市，歌姬酒徒，無所不狎。
units.en: He drifted through the streets, consorting with singers and drunkards.
units.literal: He therefore fell into destitution in the market streets, consorting with singers and drinkers without exception.

units.zh: 有歌人瑞卿者，慕其才，遂延於家。
units.en: The singer Ruiqing, admiring his talent, took him into her home.
units.literal: There was a singer named Ruiqing who admired his talent and thereupon took him into her home.

units.zh: 瑞卿能歌，每歲武穆王生辰，必歌於筵上。
units.en: Ruiqing sang each year at Prince Wumu's birthday banquet.
units.literal: Ruiqing could sing; every year on Prince Wumu's birthday she would sing at the banquet.

units.zh: 時湖南自舊管七郡外，又加武陵、嶽陽，是九州，彬作《九州歌》以授瑞卿，至時使歌之，實欲感動武穆。
units.en: By then Hunan comprised nine prefectures—the seven it had long held, plus Wuling and Yueyang. Bin wrote the 《Song of the Nine Prefectures》 for Ruiqing to perform on the appointed day, hoping in truth to stir Prince Wumu's sympathy.
units.literal: At that time, apart from the seven prefectures Hunan had long administered, Wuling and Yueyang were added as well, making nine prefectures in all. Bin composed the 《Song of the Nine Prefectures》 and gave it to Ruiqing, intending to have her sing it when the time came—his real aim was to move Prince Wumu.

units.zh: 既而竟不問，彬嘆曰：「天下分裂之際，廝徒負養皆能自奮，我貧而至此耶！」
units.en: Ma Yin never responded. Bin sighed: "When the empire is torn apart, even servants and hangers-on can lift themselves up—am I so poor that I have sunk to this!"
units.literal: In the end Ma Yin never inquired after him. Bin sighed and said: "In an age when the realm is divided, even menials and retainers can rouse themselves to strive—am I so destitute as to have come to this!"

units.zh: 計無所出，思欲竄入鄰道，但未有所向。
units.en: He saw no way forward and thought of slipping into a neighboring circuit, though he did not yet know where to go.
units.literal: He could think of no plan, and wished to flee into a neighboring circuit, but had no destination in mind.

units.zh: 居無何，聞西蜀圖綱將發，彬遂謀入蜀，且私謂瑞卿曰：「吾以幹謁不遂，居於汝家，未嘗有倦色，其可輕棄乎！
units.en: Not long after, he learned that a tribute convoy for Western Shu was setting out and decided to go to Shu. He told Ruiqing privately: "My bid for patronage failed, yet I lived in your house without ever showing fatigue—would you abandon me so easily!
units.literal: Before long, hearing that a convoy boat bound for Western Shu was about to depart, Bin resolved to enter Shu, and privately said to Ruiqing: "My efforts to solicit patronage failed, yet while living in your home I never showed weariness—could you so lightly cast me aside!

units.zh: 然士以功名為不朽，不於此時圖之，恐貽後悔。
units.en: A gentleman's immortality lies in achievement and renown. If I do not seize this moment, I may regret it forever.
units.literal: Yet for a gentleman, merit and fame are what endure; if I do not seek them now, I fear I shall live to regret it.

units.zh: 今吾他適，庶幾有成，勿以為念。」
units.en: I am leaving now. Perhaps I will succeed—do not worry about me."
units.literal: Now I go elsewhere; perhaps I shall succeed—do not grieve over me."

units.zh: 瑞卿曰：「君於妾不可謂之無情，然一旦不以妾自滯，割愛而去，得非功名之將至耶！
units.en: Ruiqing said: "You have not been heartless toward me. Yet now you refuse to let love detain you and go—surely glory is near!
units.literal: Ruiqing said: "You cannot be called heartless toward me—yet suddenly you refuse to let me hold you back, cut love and leave—is it not that fame and achievement are at hand!

units.zh: 妾誠異之，家財約數緡，雖不豐，願分為半，以資路途。」
units.en: I am amazed. Our savings come to only a few strings of cash—not much, but I will give you half for the road."
units.literal: I am truly astonished. Our household goods amount to a few strings of cash; though not abundant, I wish to divide them in half to supply your journey."

units.zh: 彬亦不讓，因以瑞卿所贈盡賂綱吏，求為駕船仆夫，綱吏許之。
units.en: Bin accepted without protest, used everything Ruiqing gave him to bribe the convoy officer, and asked to serve as a boat hand and porter. The officer agreed.
units.literal: Bin did not decline, and with all that Ruiqing gave him bribed the convoy officer, asking to serve as boat hand and servant—the officer agreed.

units.zh: 既至蜀，遂獻《獨鯉朝天賦》，蜀主大悅，擢居清要。
units.en: On reaching Shu he presented the 《Rhapsody of the Lone Carp Turning toward Heaven》. The Shu ruler was delighted and placed him in an important office.
units.literal: Once he reached Shu, he presented the 《Rhapsody of the Lone Carp Turning toward Heaven》; the ruler of Shu was greatly pleased and promoted him to a distinguished post.

units.zh: 其後官至尚書左丞相，出為夔州節度使。
units.en: He later became Left Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and was appointed military governor of Kuizhou.
