units.literal: Later he rose to Left Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and was sent out as military governor of Kuizhou.

units.zh: 既領夔州，武穆王已薨，其子希範繼立，因致書於希範，敘疇昔入蜀之由，仍以衡山宗族為讬。
units.en: By the time he took office in Kuizhou, Prince Wumu was dead and his son Xifan had succeeded. Bin wrote to Xifan, explaining why he had once gone to Shu and asking him to look after his kinsmen at Hengshan.
units.literal: Once he took charge of Kuizhou, Prince Wumu had already died and his son Xifan succeeded; Bin therefore wrote to Xifan, recounting his old reasons for entering Shu, and entrusting his clan at Hengshan to him.

units.zh: 希範得書大慚，彬之親友悉免其賦役，下令搜訪草澤，由是士無賢不肖參謁，皆延客之，因彬所致也。
units.en: Ashamed after reading the letter, Xifan exempted all of Bin's relatives and friends from taxes and labor service and ordered a search for hidden talent. From then on every scholar who came to court, worthy or not, was welcomed as a guest—all because of Bin.
units.literal: Xifan was deeply shamed on receiving the letter. All of Bin's kin and friends were exempted from taxes and corvée; he issued orders to seek out talent in the wilds—henceforth scholars whether worthy or not who came to audience were all received as guests, all because of what Bin had written.

units.zh: 彬雅有風儀，其為文辭近而理真，聞之者雖不知書，亦釋然曉之，竟以此遇。
units.en: Bin had natural grace. His writing was plain but sound in reasoning, so that even the illiterate understood him at once. He rose to success through that gift.
units.literal: Bin had a refined bearing by nature; his literary style was plain yet his reasoning true—those who heard him, even if illiterate, understood clearly, and he rose to success by this means.

units.zh: 戴偃，金陵人。
units.en: Dai Yan came from Jinling.
units.literal: Dai Yan was a man of Jinling.

units.zh: 能為詩，尤好規諷。
units.en: He wrote poetry and was especially fond of satirical admonition.
units.literal: He could compose poetry and was especially fond of admonishing satire.

units.zh: 唐末罹亂，遊湘中，值馬氏有國，至文昭王以公子得位，尤好奢侈，起天策府，構九龍、金華等殿，土木之工，斤斧之聲，晝夜不絕。
units.en: When the Tang dynasty collapsed he wandered through the Xiang region, where the Ma clan had founded a kingdom. Prince Wenzhao, a young heir who had taken the throne, loved luxury above all. He established the Heavenly Strategies Office and built halls such as Nine Dragons and Golden Splendor; the ring of axes and hammers from construction never stopped, day or night.
units.literal: At the end of Tang he suffered the turmoil and wandered the Xiang region; the Ma clan had established a state, and when Prince Wenzhao succeeded as a young prince he was especially fond of luxury—he established the Heavenly Strategies Office and built halls such as Nine Dragons and Golden Splendor; the sounds of axes and hammers from carpentry and masonry work never ceased day or night.

units.zh: 偃非之，自稱玄黃子，著《漁父詩》百篇以獻，欲譏諷之，故其句有：「才把咽喉吞世界，蓋因奢侈致危亡。」
units.en: Yan disapproved. Calling himself the Master of Dark and Yellow, he wrote a hundred 《Fisherman's Poems》 and presented them as satire. One line ran: "Barely swallowing the world down one's throat—extravagance is what brings ruin."
units.literal: Yan disapproved; styling himself the Master of Dark and Yellow, he composed one hundred 《Fisherman's Poems》 to present, intending to satirize him—hence such lines as: "Barely swallowing the world down one's gullet—surely it is extravagance that brings peril and ruin."

units.zh: 又曰：「若須拋卻便拋卻，莫待風高更水深。」
units.en: Another read: "If you mean to cast it off, cast it off now—do not wait until the wind rises and the water runs deep."
units.literal: And again: "If you must cast it off, then cast it off now—do not wait until the wind rises higher and the water deepens."

units.zh: 文昭覽之怒，一旦謂賓佐曰：「戴偃何如人？」
units.en: Wenzhao read them and was furious. One day he asked his staff: "What sort of man is Dai Yan?"
units.literal: Wenzhao read them and grew angry; one day he said to his retainers: "What sort of man is Dai Yan?"

units.zh: 時賓佐不測，以偃為文昭所重，或對曰：「偃詩人，章句深為流輩所推許，方今在貧悴，大王哀之，置之髯參短簿之間足矣。」
units.en: The staff could not read his mood and assumed Yan was in favor. Someone answered: "Yan is a poet whose verses his peers greatly admire. He is poor and wretched now; if Your Highness would show mercy, a minor post among the clerks would be enough."
units.literal: The retainers could not guess his intent, thinking Yan was favored by Wenzhao; someone replied: "Yan is a poet—his lines are deeply admired by his peers. He is now in poverty and distress; if Your Highness pity him, placing him among the lower staff would suffice."

units.zh: 文昭曰：「數日前獻吾詩，想其為人，大抵務以漁鈞自娛爾，宜賜碧湘湖，便以遂其性，亦優賢之道也。」
units.en: Wenzhao said: "He sent me poems a few days ago. From the look of him, he mainly wants to fish for his own amusement. Grant him Bixiang Lake and let him have his way—that too is how one honors talent."
units.literal: Wenzhao said: "A few days ago he presented poems to me—I infer from his character that he chiefly seeks to amuse himself with fishing. It is fitting to grant him Bixiang Lake and let him follow his nature—that too is the way of honoring the worthy."

units.zh: 即日使遷居湖上，乃潛戒公私不得與之往還。
units.en: That same day Yan was moved to the lakeshore. Wenzhao secretly forbade officials and commoners alike from having any contact with him.
units.literal: That same day he had Yan moved to live on the lake—and secretly ordered officials and private persons alike not to have dealings with him.

units.zh: 自是偃窮餓日至，無以為計，乃謂妻曰：「與汝結髮，已生一男一女，今度不惟擠於溝壑，亦恐首領不得完全，宜分兒遁去，庶幾可免，不然旦夕死矣。」
units.en: From then on Yan grew hungrier by the day. At his wit's end he told his wife: "We have been married and have a son and a daughter. I expect we will not only be cast into a ditch, but our heads may not stay on our shoulders. We should split up with the children and flee—perhaps some of us may survive. Otherwise we die any day now."
units.literal: From then on Yan's starvation worsened day by day; finding no way out, he said to his wife: "Since we bound our hair together we have had a son and a daughter. Now I expect not only to be thrust into a ditch, but also fear our heads may not remain intact—we should divide the children and flee separately, that perhaps some may escape; otherwise we shall die before long."

units.zh: 於是舉骰子與妻子約曰：「彩多得兒，彩少得女。」
units.en: He rolled dice with his wife and agreed: "High roll takes the boy, low roll takes the girl."
units.literal: He then rolled dice with his wife and agreed: "Whoever rolls the higher count takes the son; the lower takes the daughter."

units.zh: 乃攜女，相與慟哭而別。
units.en: He took the girl, and they parted in tears.
units.literal: He then took the daughter, and they parted amid shared wailing and tears.

units.zh: 偃將奔嶺南，至永州，會文昭薨乃止，其後不知所終。
units.en: Yan was heading for Lingnan when he reached Yongzhou and learned of Wenzhao's death, so he stopped. After that, no one knows what became of him.
units.literal: Yan was about to flee to Lingnan; reaching Yongzhou, he stopped when Wenzhao died—after that, no one knows his end.

units.zh: 李臯與弟節俱在湖南幕下，節亦有文學。
units.en: Li Gao and his younger brother Jie both served on the Hunan staff, and Jie was also a man of letters.
units.literal: Li Gao and his younger brother Jie both served on Hunan's staff; Jie too had literary talent.

units.zh: 同光初，馬氏武穆王授湖南諸道都統，詔賜戰馬數百匹，臯為謝表，百餘字後，思意艱澀。
units.en: Early in the Tongguang era Prince Wumu of the Ma clan was made overall commander of Hunan's circuits and received several hundred war horses by imperial decree. Gao drafted the letter of thanks, but after a hundred-odd characters his phrasing grew stiff and awkward.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Tongguang era, Prince Wumu of the Ma clan was appointed overall commander of Hunan's circuits; the throne granted several hundred war horses. Gao drafted a letter of thanks—after a hundred-odd characters his ideas grew strained and awkward.

units.zh: 時節在側，臯顧謂之曰：「嘗聞馬有旋風之隊，如何得一事為對？」
units.en: Jie was at his side. Gao turned to him and said: "I have heard of horses arrayed in whirlwind squadrons—what phrase can I pair with that?"
units.literal: Jie was beside him; Gao turned and said: "I have heard that horses form whirlwind squadrons—how can I find a matching phrase?"

units.zh: 節曰：「馬即有旋風隊，軍亦有偃月營，何患耶？」
units.en: Jie said: "If horses have whirlwind squadrons, armies have crescent-moon camps—what is the problem?"
units.literal: Jie said: "If horses have whirlwind squadrons, armies also have crescent-moon camps—what is there to worry about?"

units.zh: 臯欣然下筆云：「尋當偃月之營，擺作旋風之隊。」
units.en: Gao wrote with pleasure: "Soon the crescent-moon camp will be drawn up and deployed as whirlwind squadrons."
units.literal: Gao gladly wrote: "Presently the crescent-moon camp shall be drawn up and deployed as whirlwind squadrons."

units.zh: 表遂成，論者以此對最為親切。
units.en: The memorial was complete, and critics judged this couplet the most apt of all.
units.literal: The memorial was finished; critics judged this couplet the most apt.

units.zh: 僧洪道，不知何許人。
units.en: The monk Hongdao was a man of unknown origin.
units.literal: The monk Hongdao—no one knew whence he came.

units.zh: 通內外學，道行尤高，大為時人所重。
units.en: He mastered both secular and Buddhist learning, his conduct was exceptionally lofty, and he was greatly respected.
units.literal: He mastered both secular and Buddhist learning; his spiritual attainment was especially lofty, and he was greatly esteemed by his age.

units.zh: 天福中，居於衡州石羊鎮山谷中。
units.en: During the Tianfu era he lived in the mountain valleys of Shiyang Town in Hengzhou.
units.literal: During the Tianfu era he lived in the mountain valleys of Shiyang Town, Hengzhou.

units.zh: 馬氏文昭王之嗣位也，聞其名，召於府，使於報慈寺住持。
units.en: When Prince Wenzhao of the Ma clan succeeded to the throne, he heard of Hongdao's fame, summoned him to court, and wanted him to serve as abbot of Baoci Temple.
units.literal: When Prince Wenzhao of the Ma clan succeeded, hearing his name he summoned him to headquarters and appointed him abbot of Baoci Temple.

units.zh: 洪不應命，文昭堅欲致之，督責州縣，憂懼，計無所出，率五七十人拱擁入州。
units.en: Hong refused the summons. Wenzhao insisted on bringing him in and pressed the local officials. Anxious and at a loss, the elders led fifty or seventy men and escorted him into the prefectural city.
units.literal: Hong did not accept; Wenzhao was determined to fetch him and pressed the prefectures and counties—anxious and afraid, finding no plan, the local elders led fifty or seventy men and escorted him into the prefecture.

units.zh: 洪道知之，乃引徒弟數輩轉徙入深山中，得一巖，遂且止息。
units.en: When Hongdao learned of this, he took several disciples and moved deeper into the mountains, found a cave, and stopped there for the time being.
units.literal: When Hongdao learned of this, he led several disciples and moved into the deep mountains, found a cave, and halted there for the time being.

units.zh: 然離舊居抵於山巖下，則眾鳥千萬和鳴而隨之，州縣雖失其蹤，或有相謂曰：「且深山之中，眾鳥何故而鳴，又聲韻優逸，得非和尚在彼耶？」
units.en: From the time he left his old dwelling until he reached the cliff, countless birds sang in harmony and followed him. Though the officials lost his trail, some said to one another: "In the deep mountains, why are so many birds singing so beautifully—could the master be there?"
units.literal: Yet from leaving his old dwelling until reaching the cliff, myriad birds sang in harmony and followed him. Though the prefecture and counties lost his trail, some said to one another: "And in the deep mountains—why do so many birds sing, and with such elegant sound—could the master be there?"

units.zh: 試尋，果得之於巖所。
units.en: They searched and indeed found him at the cave.
units.literal: They searched on a trial basis and indeed found him at the cave.

units.zh: 父老再拜曰：「和尚佛之徒也，佛不遺眾生願，大王崇重，要與和尚相見，輒不應召，竄入山林，於是和尚即得計矣，而州縣與鄉村得無勞擾，而和尚忍不為之開慈憫耶！」
units.en: The elders bowed twice and said: "Master, you are a follower of the Buddha, and the Buddha does not abandon the wishes of the living. The king honors you and wishes to see you, yet you refuse the summons and flee into the mountains. You may get your way—but will the officials and villages not be harassed without end? Can you not show them compassion!"
units.literal: The elders bowed twice and said: "Master, you are a follower of the Buddha; the Buddha does not abandon the wishes of living beings. The king honors you and wishes to see you—yet you refuse the summons and flee into the mountains. If you do, the master achieves his aim—but will the prefectures, counties, and villages not be troubled and harassed? Can you bear not to open your compassionate heart for them!"

units.zh: 洪道於是始點頭曰：「如此則吾為汝行矣。」
units.en: Hongdao nodded at last and said: "If that is how it is, then I will go for your sake."
units.literal: Hongdao then first nodded and said: "If that is so, then I shall go for your sake."

units.zh: 及至府，文昭以國師待之。
units.en: When he arrived at court, Wenzhao received him as National Preceptor.
units.literal: When he reached headquarters, Wenzhao treated him as National Preceptor.

units.zh: 未幾，堅乞歸山，文昭知不可留，乃許焉。
units.en: Before long he begged earnestly to return to the mountains. Wenzhao knew he could not be kept and consented.
units.literal: Before long he earnestly begged to return to the mountains; Wenzhao knew he could not be kept and granted it.

units.zh: 其後竟不知所終。
units.en: After that, no one knows what became of him.
units.literal: Afterward, no one knows his final whereabouts.

units.zh: 初，洪道之入巖也，見一虎在穴乳二子，徒弟大駭，洪道叱曰：「無懼，彼當移去。」
units.en: When Hongdao first entered the cave he saw a tigress nursing two cubs there. His disciples were terrified. Hongdao rebuked them: "Do not be afraid—they will leave."
units.literal: Earlier, when Hongdao entered the cave he saw a tigress nursing two cubs in the den; the disciples were greatly alarmed. Hongdao rebuked them: "Do not fear—they will move away."

units.zh: 言訖，虎銜二子趨出穴，至行之所感也如此。
units.en: As soon as he finished speaking, the tiger took the two cubs in its mouth and hurried from the cave. Such was the power of his conduct.
units.literal: When he finished speaking, the tiger took the two cubs in its mouth and hurried from the cave—such was the power his conduct inspired.

units.zh: 馬希範常重一僧，號報慈長老，能入定觀人休咎。
units.en: Ma Xifan greatly esteemed a monk called Elder Baoci, who could enter deep meditation and discern people's fortunes and misfortunes.
units.literal: Ma Xifan greatly esteemed a monk styled Elder Baoci, who could enter deep meditation and observe people's fortunes and misfortunes.

units.zh: 希範因問之曰：「吾於富貴，固無遺恨，但不知者壽爾。
units.en: Xifan asked him, "As for wealth and rank, I have no regrets; only my lifespan is unknown.
units.literal: Xifan therefore asked him, saying: "As to wealth and honor, I truly have no regrets left; only my lifespan is unknown.

units.zh: 吾師以為何如？」
units.en: What does my teacher think?"
units.literal: What does my teacher think of this?"

units.zh: 報慈曰：「大王無憂，當與佛齊年。」
units.en: Baoci said, "Great King, have no worry—you will live as long as the Buddha."
units.literal: Baoci said: "Great King, have no worry—you will live as long as the Buddha."

units.zh: 希範喜，以為享壽無窮，及薨也，止於四十九。
units.en: Xifan rejoiced, thinking he would live forever; yet when he died he was only forty-nine.
units.literal: Xifan rejoiced, thinking he would enjoy endless years; yet when he died, he was only forty-nine.

units.zh: 先是，希範常嫉高郁之為人，因莊宗言而殺之，至是方臨江觀競渡，置酒未及飲，而希範忽驚起，顧其弟曰：「高郁來！」
units.en: Earlier Xifan had resented Gao Yu and, prompted by Zhuangzong's words, had killed him. Now, as he watched boat races along the river with wine set out but not yet drunk, Xifan suddenly leapt up in alarm, turned to his brother, and cried, "Gao Yu is here!"
units.literal: Earlier Xifan had always resented Gao Yu's conduct and, because of Zhuangzong's words, had killed him. Now, as he was watching the boat races along the river and had set out wine but not yet drunk, Xifan suddenly started up in alarm, turned to his brother, and said: "Gao Yu has come!"

units.zh: 希廣亦驚曰：「高郁死久矣，大王勿妄言！」
units.en: Xiguang was alarmed too and said, "Gao Yu has been dead a long time—Great King, do not speak rashly!"
units.literal: Xiguang was also alarmed and said: "Gao Yu has been dead a long time—Great King, do not speak rashly!"

units.zh: 而希範血自鼻出，是夕遂卒。
units.en: Blood then poured from Xifan's nose, and that night he died.
units.literal: Then blood issued from Xifan's nose, and that night he died.

units.zh: 馬希範卒，判官李臯以希範同母弟希廣為天策府都尉，撫禦尤非所長，大校張少敵憂之，建議請立希廣庶兄武陵帥希萼，且曰：「希萼處長負氣，觀其所為，必不為都尉之下，加之在武陵，九溪蠻通好，往來甚歡，若不得立，必引蠻軍為亂，幸為思之。」
units.en: When Ma Xifan died, the administrator Li Gao made Xifan's younger uterine brother Xiguang Grand Marshal of the Heavenly Strategies Office, though governing was far from his strength. Senior commander Zhang Shaodi was alarmed and urged that Xiguang's elder half-brother Xie, military commissioner at Wuling, be enthroned instead. He said: "Xie is the elder and proud. He will never serve under the Grand Marshal. At Wuling he is on close terms with the Jiuxi tribes. If he is passed over, he will surely bring barbarian armies to revolt. Please think this through."
units.literal: When Ma Xifan died, the administrator Li Gao installed Xifan's younger brother by the same mother, Xiguang, as Grand Marshal of the Heavenly Strategies Office—governing and commanding were especially not his strengths. The senior commander Zhang Shaodi was worried and advised that Xifan's elder half-brother, Xie, commander at Wuling, should be enthroned, saying: "Xie is the elder and proud by nature; judging by his conduct, he will never submit to the Grand Marshal. Moreover, at Wuling he is on friendly terms with the Jiuxi barbarians and exchanges visits freely. If he is not enthroned, he will surely bring barbarian troops to raise rebellion—please consider this."

units.zh: 李臯忽怒曰：「汝輩何知？
units.en: Li Gao burst out angrily: "What do you people know?
units.literal: Li Gao suddenly flared in anger: "What do you lot know?

units.zh: 且先大王為都尉，俱為嫡嗣，不立之，卻用老婢兒可乎？」
units.en: The late king was also Grand Marshal, and both were sons of the principal wife. Is it acceptable not to install him and instead put a son of an old maidservant on the throne?"
units.literal: The former king was also Grand Marshal of the Heavenly Strategies Office, and both were sons of the principal wife—is it acceptable not to install him and instead use the son of an old slave woman?"

units.zh: 少敵曰：「國家之事，不可拘以一途，變而能通，所以國長久也。
units.en: Shaodi said: "State affairs cannot be tied to a single rule. Adaptation is what keeps a kingdom alive.
units.literal: Shaodi said: "State affairs cannot be bound to one path; change that still preserves order is what keeps a state enduring.

units.zh: 何嫡庶之雲乎？
units.en: What talk of legitimate versus illegitimate birth?
units.literal: What talk of principal versus secondary birth?

units.zh: 若明公必立都尉，當妙設方略以制武陵，使帖然不動乃可，不然則社稷去矣！」
units.en: If you insist on enthroning the Grand Marshal, you must devise a shrewd plan to control Wuling and keep him quiet. Otherwise the kingdom is lost!"
units.literal: If you must install the Grand Marshal, you should devise clever strategies to control Wuling and keep him tractable—otherwise the altars of state are lost!"

units.zh: 臯愈怒，竟不從少敵之謀。
units.en: Gao grew even angrier and refused Shaodi's advice.
units.literal: Gao grew angrier still and in the end did not follow Shaodi's counsel.

units.zh: 少敵度無可奈何，遂辭不出。
units.en: Shaodi saw there was nothing to be done and withdrew from public life.
units.literal: Shaodi saw nothing could be done and declined to come forth.

units.zh: 未幾，希萼果以武陵反，引洞溪蠻數路齊進，遂之長沙，縊希廣於郊外，而支解李臯，自是湖南大亂，未逾年而國滅，一如少敵之言。
units.en: Before long Xie rebelled from Wuling, leading Dongxi tribesmen in several columns against Changsha. He strangled Xiguang outside the city and had Li Gao torn limb from limb. Hunan plunged into chaos, and within a year the kingdom was destroyed—exactly as Shaodi had warned.
units.literal: Before long Xie indeed rebelled from Wuling, bringing Dongxi barbarians in several columns to advance together; he proceeded to Changsha, strangled Xiguang in the suburbs, and dismembered Li Gao. From then on Hunan fell into great chaos, and within a year the state was destroyed—just as Shaodi had said.

units.zh: 初希萼之來也，希廣以全軍付親校許可瓊，使遂擊之。
units.en: When Xie first marched on Changsha, Xiguang gave the entire army to his trusted officer Xu Keqiong and ordered him to strike immediately.
units.literal: When Xie first came, Xiguang entrusted the full army to his trusted officer Xu Keqiong and ordered him to attack at once.

units.zh: 可瓊睹希萼眾盛，恐懼，夜送旗鼓乞降，希萼大喜，於是兼可瓊之眾長驅而至。
units.en: Keqiong saw how large Xie's army was, panicked, and by night sent flags and drums to surrender. Xie was delighted and, adding Keqiong's troops to his own, marched straight on.
units.literal: Keqiong saw Xie's forces were vast, grew afraid, and by night sent flags and drums to sue for surrender—Xie was greatly pleased and, incorporating Keqiong's troops, drove straight on.

units.zh: 希廣素奉佛，聞之，計無所出。
units.en: Xiguang had always been devoted to Buddhism. On hearing the news he could think of nothing to do.
units.literal: Xiguang had always worshipped Buddhism; on hearing this he could think of nothing.

units.zh: 乃被緇衣引群僧念『寶勝如來』，謂之禳災。
units.en: He put on monastic robes, gathered monks, and had them chant the name of Treasure-Victory Tathagata, calling it a rite to avert disaster.
units.literal: He donned monastic robes, led a host of monks in chanting "Treasure-Victory Tathagata," calling it disaster-averting ritual.

units.zh: 頃之，府廨火起，人忽紛擾，猶念誦之聲未輟，其戇如此。
units.en: Before long fire broke out in the government offices and people panicked, yet the chanting never stopped. Such was his folly.
units.literal: Before long fire broke out in the government compound; people suddenly panicked—yet the chanting never stopped. Such was his obtuseness.

units.zh: 少敵憂之，良有以也。
units.en: Shaodi had had good reason to worry.
units.literal: Shaodi had had reason to worry.

units.zh: 先是，城中街道尚種槐，其柳即無十一二，至是內外一變皆種柳，無復槐矣。
units.en: Earlier the city streets had been lined mostly with locust trees; willows were scarce. Now inside and outside the city alike had switched to willows, and the locusts were gone.
units.literal: Previously the city streets still had locust trees planted, while willows numbered scarcely one or two in ten; by this time inside and outside alike had changed—all planted willows, and no locust trees remained.

units.zh: 又居人夜間好織草鞋，似槌芒之聲，聞於郊野，俄有童謠云：「湖南城郭好長街，竟栽柳樹不栽槐。
units.en: Residents also took to weaving straw sandals at night, and the sound of beating hemp carried into the countryside. Soon a children's rhyme spread: "Hunan's streets run long and fine—all plant willows, none plant locust.
units.literal: Moreover, the residents at night liked to weave straw sandals, and sounds like beating hemp echoed through the suburbs; soon a children's rhyme ran: "Hunan's walls and streets have fine long avenues—all plant willows, none plant locust.

units.zh: 百姓奔竄無一事，只是槌芒織草鞋。」
units.en: The people flee in panic with nothing to do but beat hemp and weave straw sandals."
units.literal: The common people flee in panic with nothing to do but beat hemp and weave straw sandals."

units.zh: 人無長少，皆誦之。
units.en: Everyone, young and old, chanted it.
units.literal: Young and old alike recited it.

units.zh: 未幾國亂，百姓奔竄，死於溝壑者十有八九，至是，議者始悟。
units.en: Before long the kingdom collapsed. The people fled, and eight or nine out of ten died in ditches and gullies. Only then did those who had heard the rhyme understand.
units.literal: Before long the state fell into chaos; the people fled in panic, and eight or nine out of ten died in ditches and gullies—only then did commentators begin to understand.

units.zh: 蓋長街者，通內外之路也；
units.en: The long avenues signified the roads linking the inner and outer city;
units.literal: The long avenues meant the roads connecting inside and outside;

units.zh: 槐者，皆言懷也；
units.en: locust trees stood for cherishing one another;
units.literal: locust trees all signified "cherish";

units.zh: 不裁槐，蓋兄弟不睦，以至國亡，失孔懷之義也。
units.en: not planting locust trees foretold discord among brothers, the fall of the kingdom, and the loss of true brotherly love.
units.literal: not planting locust trees signified brothers at odds, leading to the state's destruction—the loss of deep fraternal affection.

units.zh: 草鞋者，遠行所用，蓋百姓遠行奔竄之象也。
units.en: Straw sandals were for long journeys—a sign that the people would flee far from home.
units.literal: Straw sandals were for long journeys—an image of the people fleeing far in panic.

units.zh: 馬希萼既立，不治國事，數與僚吏縱酒為樂。
units.en: Once enthroned, Ma Xie neglected government and often drank and made merry with his officials.
units.literal: Once Ma Xie was enthroned, he did not govern state affairs and often drank in revelry with his officials.

units.zh: 有小吏謝廷擇者，本帳下廝養，有容貌，希萼素寵嬖之，每筵會，皆命廷擇預坐，諸官甚有在下者。
units.en: A minor clerk named Xie Tingze had been a household servant. Handsome and favored by Xie, he was seated at every banquet while many senior officials sat below him.
units.literal: There was a minor clerk named Xie Tingze, originally a household servant in the headquarters, handsome in appearance; Xie had long favored him intimately. At every banquet he ordered Tingze to sit with the guests—many officials ranked below him.

units.zh: 於是眾怒，往往偶語曰：「此輩舊制有燕會，唯用兵守門，以防他虞，今與我等齊列，何辱之甚耶？」
units.en: The officials were furious and whispered among themselves: "By old custom servants only guarded the gates at banquets. Now they sit with us—what an outrage!"
units.literal: Thereupon the crowd grew angry and often murmured among themselves: "By old custom at banquets such people were used only as armed gate guards against unexpected trouble—now they sit level with us; what gross insult is this?"

units.zh: 其弟希崇因眾怒咄咄，與其黨竊發，擒希萼囚之於衡陽，又自立。
units.en: His younger brother Xichong, exploiting the general anger, rose secretly with his faction, seized Xie, imprisoned him at Hengyang, and declared himself ruler.
units.literal: His younger brother Xichong, riding the crowd's anger, secretly rose with his faction, seized Xie, imprisoned him at Hengyang, and enthroned himself.

units.zh: 未數日，江南遣袁州刺史邊鎬乘其亂領兵來伐，希崇度不能敵，遂降。
units.en: Within days Jiangnan sent Yuanzhou prefect Bian Hao to invade while the kingdom was in turmoil. Xichong knew he could not resist and surrendered.
units.literal: Within days Jiangnan sent Bian Hao, prefect of Yuanzhou, to seize the chaos and lead troops to attack; Xichong saw he could not resist and surrendered.

units.zh: 先是，長沙重謠云：「鞭打焉，走不暇。」
units.en: Earlier a solemn rhyme in Changsha ran: "The lash strikes—no time to flee."
units.literal: Earlier a weighty rhyme in Changsha ran: "The lash strikes—no time to flee."

units.zh: 未幾，果為邊鎬所滅。
units.en: Before long the kingdom was indeed destroyed by Bian Hao.
units.literal: Before long it was indeed destroyed by Bian Hao.

units.zh: 初，鎬嘗為僧，以覘湖南，尤善弄鈸，每侵晨必弄鈸行乞，遇城往往擲起鈸以度門之高下。
units.en: Bian had once served as a monk spy in Hunan and was especially skilled at playing cymbals. Every dawn he played cymbals while begging, and at city gates he would toss them up to measure how high the gates were.
units.literal: Earlier Bian had once been a monk sent to spy on Hunan; he was especially skilled at playing cymbals. Every dawn he would play cymbals while begging; when he came to a city gate he often tossed the cymbals up to measure the gate's height.

units.zh: 及來湖南，士庶頗有識之者。
units.en: When he returned to Hunan, many people recognized him.
units.literal: When he came to Hunan, many among the gentry and commoners recognized him.

units.zh: 廖氏虔州贛縣人。
units.en: The Liao family came from Gan County in Qianzhou.
units.literal: The Liao clan were men of Gan County in Qianzhou.

units.zh: 有子三人：伯曰圖，仲曰偃，季曰凝。
units.en: They had three sons: the eldest, Tu; the second, Yan; the youngest, Ning.
units.literal: They had three sons: the eldest was Tu, the second Yan, the youngest Ning.

units.zh: 圖、凝皆有詩名，偃趨蹻勇絕倫，由是豪橫，遂為鄉里所憚。
units.en: Tu and Ning were both known as poets. Yan was swift and fearless beyond compare, grew domineering, and came to be feared throughout the countryside.
units.literal: Tu and Ning both had reputations as poets; Yan was swift and peerless in courage, and by this became overbearing—feared throughout the district.

units.zh: 江南命功臣鐘章為虔州刺史，深嫉之，於是圖與凝等議曰：「觀章所為，但欲滅吾族矣，若戀土不去，禍且及矣。」
units.en: Jiangnan appointed the meritorious official Zhong Zhang as prefect of Qianzhou, and he hated them deeply. Tu and Ning discussed the matter: "From Zhang's conduct, he means to destroy our clan. If we cling to our land, disaster will follow."
units.literal: Jiangnan appointed the meritorious official Zhong Zhang prefect of Qianzhou, who deeply resented them; Tu and Ning and the others then deliberated: "Judging by Zhang's conduct, he only wishes to destroy our clan. If we cling to our land and do not leave, disaster will soon reach us."

units.zh: 於是領其族暨部等三千餘人，具鎧仗號令而後行，章不敢逐，遂奔湖南。
units.en: They then led more than three thousand clansmen and followers, fully armed and in good order. Zhang did not dare pursue them, and they fled to Hunan.
units.literal: Thereupon they led their clan and followers, more than three thousand in all, fully armed and under command, and marched away—Zhang did not dare pursue, and they fled to Hunan.

units.zh: 時武穆王在位，見其眾盛，恐難制，欲盡誅之。
units.en: Prince Wumu was then on the throne. Seeing how large their force was, he feared they would be hard to control and wanted to kill them all.
units.literal: At that time Prince Wumu was on the throne; seeing their numbers were great, he feared they would be hard to control and wished to execute them all.

units.zh: 或者曰：「大王姓馬，而廖來歸，廖者料也。
units.en: Someone said: "Your surname is Ma, and the Liao have come to submit. Liao sounds like fodder.
units.literal: Someone said: "Your Highness's surname is Ma, and the Liao have come to submit—Liao means fodder.

units.zh: 馬得料其勢必肥，實國家大興之兆，其可殺之乎！」
units.en: A horse given fodder is sure to grow strong—it is a great omen of the kingdom's rise. How can you kill them!"
units.literal: A horse that gets fodder is sure to grow fat—this is truly a great omen of the state's rise. How can they be killed!"

units.zh: 武穆喜，遂善待。
units.en: Prince Wumu was delighted and treated them generously.
units.literal: Prince Wumu was pleased and thereupon treated them well.

units.zh: 仍制下以凝為永州刺史，圖為行軍司馬，偃為天策府列校，仍賜莊宅於衡山，自稱逸人。
units.en: He appointed Ning prefect of Yongzhou, Tu army march commander, and Yan a column commander of the Heavenly Strategies Office, and granted them estates at Hengshan. Yan styled himself a recluse.
units.literal: He also issued orders appointing Ning prefect of Yongzhou, Tu army march commander, and Yan a column commander of the Heavenly Strategies Office; he further granted them estates at Hengshan, and Yan styled himself a recluse.

units.zh: 偃能於馬上挺身而立，取濕衣振奮而服之，以示輕捷。
units.en: Yan could stand upright on horseback, shake out a wet coat, and put it on to show his agility.
units.literal: Yan could stand upright on horseback, take a wet garment, shake it vigorously, and put it on to display his lightness and agility.

units.zh: 荊南高季興次子，忘其名，管親軍雲猛都，謂之雲猛郎君。
units.en: The second son of Gao Jixing of Jingnan—his name is forgotten—commanded the personal army unit Yunmeng and was known as Young Master Yunmeng.
units.literal: The second son of Gao Jixing of Jingnan—his name is forgotten—commanded the personal army unit Yunmeng and was called Young Master Yunmeng.

units.zh: 聞偃名，因兩境交兵，請與偃鬥。
units.en: He had heard of Yan's reputation, and when the two states clashed he asked for a duel with him.
units.literal: Hearing Yan's fame, when the two borders clashed in battle he requested a duel with Yan.

units.zh: 偃欣然而往，雲猛能用槍，見偃瘦小，心輕之，馳騎而刺偃，垂及之，偃佯落馬，雲猛勢未及止，偃自後奮戈一擊墮地，因生擒之。
units.en: Yan went gladly. Young Master Yunmeng was skilled with the spear. Seeing Yan small and slight, he despised him, spurred forward, and thrust at him. Just as the point was about to reach him, Yan feigned a fall from his horse. Yunmeng could not check his charge; Yan struck from behind with a halberd, knocked him to the ground, and took him alive.
units.literal: Yan went gladly. Young Master Yunmeng was skilled with the spear; seeing Yan small and slight, he took him lightly, spurred his horse and thrust at Yan—just as he was about to reach him, Yan feigned falling from his horse. Yunmeng's momentum could not stop in time; Yan from behind struck fiercely with a halberd and knocked him to the ground, then took him alive.

units.zh: 自是其名愈振。
units.en: From then on his fame grew even greater.
units.literal: From then on his fame resounded all the more.

units.zh: 故武穆王終世不為鄰境所輕者，偃之力焉。
units.en: It was thanks to Yan that Prince Wumu was never looked down upon by neighboring states throughout his reign.
units.literal: Thus the reason Prince Wumu was never slighted by neighboring territories throughout his life was Yan's strength.

units.zh: 至其子希範嗣位，九溪蠻叛，命偃率兵討之，為流矢所傷，死於蠻中。
units.en: When his son Xifan succeeded, the Jiuxi tribes rebelled. Xifan ordered Yan to lead troops against them. Yan was struck by a stray arrow and died in the barbarian lands.
units.literal: When his son Xifan succeeded, the Jiuxi barbarians rebelled; he ordered Yan to lead troops to suppress them. Yan was wounded by a stray arrow and died among the barbarians.

units.zh: 兇訃至，希範使人報其母張氏。
units.en: When news of his death in battle arrived, Xifan sent a messenger to inform his mother, Lady Zhang.
units.literal: When word of his violent death arrived, Xifan sent a messenger to report to his mother, Lady Zhang.

units.zh: 張氏不哭，謂其使曰：「為妾謝大王，舉家三百餘口，受王分食解衣之賜，雖盡死未足以上報，況一子乎！
units.en: Lady Zhang did not weep. She told the messenger: "Please thank the king for me. Our family of more than three hundred souls has received his bounty of food and clothing. Even if we all died we could not repay him—what is one son!
units.literal: Lady Zhang did not weep and said to the messenger: "Please thank the king on my behalf. Our household of more than three hundred mouths has received the king's bounty of shared food and given garments—even if we all died it would not repay the debt, let alone one son!

units.zh: 望大王勿以為念。」
units.en: I hope Your Majesty will not trouble yourself on our account."
units.literal: I hope the king will not give it a thought."

units.zh: 希範聞而嘆曰：「廖氏有此母，欲不興其可得乎！」
units.en: When Xifan heard this, he sighed and said, "With a mother like this in the Liao clan, how could they fail to prosper!"
units.literal: When Xifan heard this he sighed and said: "The Liao clan has such a mother—how could they fail to rise!"

units.zh: 於是厚加存恤，仍遣使召凝，任為從事。
units.en: He then showered them with generous care and relief, sent envoys to summon Ning, and appointed him a staff officer.
units.literal: Thereupon he added great support and relief, and still sent envoys to summon Ning, appointing him as an aide.

units.zh: 至希範薨，國亂，為江南所滅，遂遷金陵。
units.en: When Xifan died, the kingdom collapsed into chaos and was overrun by Jiangnan, and Ning relocated to Jinling.
units.literal: When Xifan died, the state fell into chaos and was destroyed by Jiangnan; [Ning] then moved to Jinling.

units.zh: 唐主授以水部員外郎。
units.en: The Tang ruler appointed him Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
units.literal: The lord of Tang granted him the post of Vice Director in the Ministry of Works.

units.zh: 為洪州連昌縣令。
units.en: He served as magistrate of Lianchang County in Hongzhou.
units.literal: He served as magistrate of Lianchang County in Hong Prefecture.

units.zh: 未幾，又遷江州團練使。
units.en: Before long he was transferred again, becoming military training commissioner of Jiangzhou.
units.literal: Before long he was transferred again to military training commissioner of Jiang Prefecture.

units.zh: 凝為人不羈，好詼諧，嘗覽裴說《經杜工部墓詩》曰：「擬鑿孤墳破，重教大雅生。」
units.en: Ning was free-spirited and loved banter. Once, reading Pei Shuo's Poem on Passing Du Gongbu's Tomb, he came to the line: "I mean to break open that lonely tomb and bring great poetry back to life."
units.literal: Ning was unrestrained in character and fond of wit; once reading Pei Shuo's Poem on Passing Du Gongbu's Tomb, which says: "I plan to break open the lonely grave and bring the Great Elegance to life again."

units.zh: 因曰：「如此，裴說乃劫墳賊耳。」
units.en: He remarked, "By that logic, Pei Shuo is nothing but a tomb robber."
units.literal: He then said: "If so, Pei Shuo is nothing but a tomb-robbing thief."

units.zh: 聞者笑之。
units.en: Those who heard laughed.
units.literal: Those who heard laughed.

units.zh: 在江川，盛暑，嘗患體燥，乃以一大桶盛冷水，坐於其間，或至終日。
units.en: While in Jiangzhou, during a sweltering summer, he once suffered from the heat and had a great tub filled with cold water; he would sit in it, sometimes for an entire day.
units.literal: While at Jiangchuan, in the height of summer, he once suffered from bodily heat; he therefore filled a great tub with cold water and sat in it, sometimes for the whole day.

units.zh: 雖賓友謁見，出露其首與之談笑，其簡率如此。
units.en: Even when guests came to visit, he would merely poke his head out to chat and laugh with them—so unconventional was he.
units.literal: Even when guests and friends came to call, he would expose his head above the rim to talk and laugh with them—such was his informality.

units.zh: 先是，凝嘗夢人以印授之，拜捧之際，其印缺其一角，凝不能測。
units.en: Earlier Ning had dreamed that someone handed him a seal; as he bowed to receive it, he noticed one corner was chipped away, and he could not discern what it meant.
units.literal: Earlier, Ning had dreamed that someone presented him with a seal; as he bowed and received it, one corner of the seal was missing, and Ning could not fathom the meaning.

units.zh: 及授江州之命，始悟曰：「印缺一角，蓋偏裨之象也。
units.en: When the Jiangzhou appointment arrived, he at last understood. "The chipped corner on the seal," he said, "must symbolize a deputy command.
units.literal: When he received the appointment to Jiang Prefecture, he at last understood, saying: "The missing corner on the seal is surely the sign of a subordinate commander.

units.zh: 團練副使，不亦宜乎！」
units.en: Deputy military training commissioner—what could be more apt!"
units.literal: Deputy military training commissioner—is that not fitting!"

units.zh: 時人異之。）〉
units.en: People of the time found it remarkable. ）〉
units.literal: People of the time marveled at this. ）〉

units.zh: 劉言，本朗州之牙將也。
units.en: Liu Yan had originally been a garrison officer in Langzhou.
units.literal: Liu Yan was originally a garrison officer of Lang Prefecture.

units.zh: 初，馬氏舉族為江南所俘，朗州無帥，眾乃推列校馬光惠為武平軍留後，光惠署言為副使。
units.en: When the entire Ma clan was captured by Jiangnan and Langzhou was left without a commander, the troops promoted the officer Ma Guanghui to acting military governor of the Wuping Army, and Guanghui appointed Yan his deputy.
units.literal: At first, when the entire Ma clan was captured by Jiangnan and Lang Prefecture had no commander, the troops pushed the officer Ma Guanghui to be acting military governor of the Wuping Army; Guanghui appointed Yan as deputy commissioner.

units.zh: 既而光惠耽荒僭侈，軍情不附，遂行廢黜，以言代光惠為留後。
units.en: Before long Guanghui sank into idleness and extravagance, the army lost faith in him, and he was deposed; Yan replaced him as acting governor.
units.literal: Before long Guanghui became idle, extravagant, and arrogant; the troops lost heart, and he was deposed; Yan replaced Guanghui as acting governor.

units.zh: 時周廣順二年秋也。
units.en: This was autumn of the second year of Guangshun under the Zhou.
units.literal: It was autumn of the second year of Guangshun in Zhou.

units.zh: 言既立，北則遣使奉表於周太祖，東亦上章於江南李景，求正授旄鉞，景未之許。
units.en: Once Yan had taken power, he sent envoys north to submit a memorial to Emperor Taizu of Zhou and east to petition Li Jing of Jiangnan for formal investiture with full military authority; Jing refused.
units.literal: Once Yan was established, to the north he sent envoys to submit a memorial to Emperor Taizu of Zhou, and to the east he also sent a petition to Li Jing of Jiangnan, requesting formal appointment with full insignia; Jing did not grant it.

units.zh: 時邊鎬據湖南，潛遣人賫金帛說誘武陵谿洞諸蠻，欲合勢以攻朗州。
units.en: Bian Hao held Hunan and secretly sent men with gold and silk to win over the stream-cave tribes of Wuling, hoping to combine forces and attack Langzhou.
units.literal: At the time Bian Hao held Hunan and secretly sent men bearing gold and silk to win over the various Miao of Wuling's stream-cave districts, wishing to combine forces and attack Lang Prefecture.

units.zh: 會李景降偽詔，征言赴金陵，言懼，不從偽命，以其年冬十月三日，與其節度副使王進逵、行軍司馬何敬真、都指揮使周行逢等同領舟師以襲潭州。
units.en: When Li Jing issued a forged edict summoning Yan to Jinling, Yan feared the trap and refused. On the third day of the tenth month that winter, he joined his deputy commissioner Wang Jinkui, chief of staff He Jingzhen, and commander-in-chief Zhou Xingfeng in leading a fleet against Tanzhou.
units.literal: When Li Jing issued a forged edict summoning Yan to Jinling, Yan feared and refused the false order; on the third day of the tenth month that winter, together with his deputy commissioner Wang Jinkui, chief of staff He Jingzhen, and commander-in-chief Zhou Xingfeng, he jointly led a fleet to raid Tan Prefecture.

units.zh: 九日，攻拔益陽寨，殺淮軍數千人。
units.en: On the ninth they captured the Yiyang stockade and killed several thousand Huai troops.
units.literal: On the ninth they captured the Yiyang stockade and killed several thousand Huai troops.

units.zh: 十三日，至潭州城下。
units.en: On the thirteenth they reached the walls of Tanzhou.
units.literal: On the thirteenth they arrived below the walls of Tan Prefecture.

units.zh: 是夕，邊鎬領其部眾棄城東走，進逵、敬真遂入據其城。
units.en: That evening Bian Hao abandoned the city and fled east with his troops; Jinkui and Jingzhen entered and took possession of it.
units.literal: That evening Bian Hao led his forces and abandoned the city, fleeing east; Jinkui and Jingzhen then entered and seized it.

units.zh: 言乃遣牙將張崇嗣奉表於周太祖，且言潭州兵戈之後，焚燒殆盡，乞移使府於朗州，從之。
units.en: Yan dispatched the officer Zhang Congsi to submit a memorial to Emperor Taizu of Zhou, explaining that Tanzhou had been nearly burned to ashes in the fighting and begging to move the headquarters to Langzhou; the request was granted.
units.literal: Yan then dispatched the officer Zhang Congsi to submit a memorial to Emperor Taizu of Zhou, stating that after the fighting Tan Prefecture had been nearly burned to ashes, and begging to move the headquarters to Lang Prefecture; the request was granted.

units.zh: 詔升朗州為大都督府，在潭州之上。
units.en: An edict promoted Langzhou to a grand protectorate, ranking above Tanzhou.
units.literal: An edict promoted Lang Prefecture to a Grand Protectorate, ranking above Tan Prefecture.

units.zh: 廣順三年春正月，制以言為檢校太師、同平章事、朗州大都督，充武平軍節度使，制置武安、靜江等軍事；
units.en: In the first month of spring in the third year of Guangshun, Yan was appointed Honorary Grand Preceptor, Co-Governor, Grand Protector of Langzhou, Military Governor of the Wuping Army, with authority over military affairs in Wu'an, Jingjiang, and related commands;
units.literal: In the first month of spring in the third year of Guangshun, Yan was appointed Honorary Grand Preceptor, Co-Governor, Grand Protector of Lang Prefecture, Military Governor of the Wuping Army, with authority over military affairs in Wu'an, Jingjiang, and related commands;

units.zh: 又以王進逵為武安軍節度使，何敬真為靜江軍節度使，並檢校太尉；
units.en: Wang Jinkui was made military governor of the Wu'an Army and He Jingzhen military governor of the Jingjiang Army, both with the honorary title Grand Guardian;
units.literal: Wang Jinkui was made Military Governor of the Wu'an Army, He Jingzhen Military Governor of the Jingjiang Army, both Honorary Grand Guardians;

units.zh: 以周行逢領集州刺史，充武安軍節度行軍司馬。
units.en: Zhou Xingfeng was made prefect of Jizhou and chief of staff of the Wu'an military command.
units.literal: Zhou Xingfeng was given the post of prefect of Ji Prefecture and served as chief of staff of the Wu'an military command.

units.zh: 未幾，言遣何敬真帥軍南擊廣賊，敬真失律，奔歸潭州，為王進逵所殺。
units.en: Before long Yan sent He Jingzhen south to attack Guang bandits; Jingzhen lost control of his troops, fled back to Tanzhou, and was killed by Wang Jinkui.
units.literal: Before long Yan sent He Jingzhen south at the head of an army to strike Guang bandits; Jingzhen lost discipline, fled back to Tan Prefecture, and was killed by Wang Jinkui.

units.zh: 其年秋，進逵奏：「劉言與淮賊通連，差指揮使鄭交部領兵士，欲並當道，鄭交為軍眾所執，奔入武陵，劉言尋為諸軍所廢，臣已至朗州安撫訖。」
units.en: That autumn Jinkui memorialized: "Liu Yan has been in contact with the Huai bandits. He dispatched Commander Zheng Jiao with troops intending to seize control of our route. Zheng Jiao was seized by the soldiers and fled into Wuling. Liu Yan was soon deposed by the armies. I have already reached Langzhou and restored order."
units.literal: That autumn Jinkui memorialized: "Liu Yan is in contact with the Huai bandits. He dispatched Commander Zheng Jiao to lead troops intending to seize control of our route. Zheng Jiao was seized by the soldiers and fled into Wuling. Liu Yan was soon deposed by the various armies. I have already reached Lang Prefecture and restored order."

units.zh: 周太祖詔劉言宜勒歸私第，委王進逵取便安置。
units.en: Emperor Taizu of Zhou ordered Liu Yan to retire to his private residence and entrusted Wang Jinkui to settle him as he saw fit.
units.literal: Emperor Taizu of Zhou ordered Liu Yan to retire to his private residence and entrusted Wang Jinkui to settle him as he saw fit.

units.zh: 言尋遇害，朝廷乃正授進逵朗州節制。
units.en: Before long Yan was murdered, and the court formally invested Jinkui with control of Langzhou.
units.literal: Before long Yan was murdered, and the court formally invested Jinkui with control of Lang Prefecture.

units.zh: 顯德元年秋，制以武安軍節度副使周行逢為鄂州節度使，權知潭州軍府事，加檢校太尉。
units.en: In autumn of the first year of Xiande, Zhou Xingfeng, deputy military governor of the Wu'an Army, was made military governor of Ezhou, provisional administrator of Tanzhou headquarters, and granted the honorary title Grand Guardian.
units.literal: In autumn of the first year of Xiande, Zhou Xingfeng, deputy military governor of the Wu'an Army, was made military governor of E Prefecture, provisional administrator of Tan Prefecture headquarters, and granted the honorary title Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 三年春正月，世宗將伐淮甸，詔進逵率兵入江南界。
units.en: In the first month of spring in the third year, as Emperor Shizong prepared to campaign against the Huai region, Jinkui was ordered to lead troops into Jiangnan territory.
units.literal: In the first month of spring in the third year, as Emperor Shizong prepared to campaign against the Huai region, Jinkui was ordered to lead troops into Jiangnan territory.

units.zh: 二月，進逵準詔而行，仍遣部將潘叔嗣領兵五千為先鋒。
units.en: In the second month Jinkui set out as ordered and dispatched his officer Pan Shusi with five thousand men as vanguard.
units.literal: In the second month Jinkui set out according to the edict and dispatched the officer Pan Shusi with five thousand men as vanguard.

units.zh: 行及鄂州界，叔嗣回戈以襲朗州。
units.en: When they reached the border of Ezhou, Shusi turned his troops about and struck Langzhou.
units.literal: When they reached the border of E Prefecture, Shusi turned his blades and struck Lang Prefecture.

units.zh: 進逵聞之，倍道先入武陵，叔嗣遽攻其城，進逵敗，為叔嗣所殺。
units.en: On hearing this Jinkui raced ahead by forced marches into Wuling, but Shusi promptly assaulted the city. Jinkui was defeated and killed by Shusi.
units.literal: On hearing this Jinkui raced ahead by forced marches into Wuling; Shusi promptly assaulted the city. Jinkui was defeated and killed by Shusi.

units.zh: 遣人詣潭州請周行逢至朗州，斬叔嗣於市。
units.en: He sent someone to Tanzhou to summon Zhou Xingfeng to Langzhou and had Shusi executed in the market.
units.literal: He sent someone to Tan Prefecture to summon Zhou Xingfeng to Lang Prefecture and had Shusi executed in the market.

units.zh: 其年秋七月，制以行逢為朗州大都督，充武平軍節度使，加兼侍中。
units.en: In the seventh month that autumn Xingfeng was appointed Grand Protector of Langzhou and Military Governor of the Wuping Army, with the additional title of Palace Attendant.
units.literal: In the seventh month that autumn Xingfeng was appointed Grand Protector of Lang Prefecture and Military Governor of the Wuping Army, with the additional title of Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 自是潭、朗之地，遂為行逢所有。
units.en: From then on the lands of Tan and Lang came entirely under Xingfeng's control.
units.literal: From then on the lands of Tan and Lang came entirely under Xingfeng's possession.

units.zh: 皇朝建隆初，就加中書令。
units.en: At the beginning of Jianlong under the Imperial Song he was further given the title of Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong in the Imperial Song he was further given the title of Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 四年，行逢卒，三軍立其子保權為帥。
units.en: In the fourth year Xingfeng died, and the three armies installed his son Baoquan as commander.
units.literal: In the fourth year Xingfeng died; the three armies installed his son Baoquan as commander.

units.zh: 未幾，朗軍亂，求救於朝廷。
units.en: Before long the Lang army mutinied and begged the court for aid.
units.literal: Before long the Lang army mutinied and begged aid from the court.

units.zh: 及王師平定荊、湖，保權入朝，由是湖湘之地盡為王土矣。
units.en: When the imperial army pacified Jing and Hu, Baoquan presented himself at court, and the lands of Hunan and Hubei became entirely territory of the throne.
units.literal: When the imperial army pacified Jing and Hu, Baoquan presented himself at court; thereby the lands of Hunan and Hubei became entirely territory of the throne.

units.zh: 錢镠，杭州臨安縣人。
units.en: Qian Liu came from Lin'an County in Hangzhou.
units.literal: Qian Liu was a native of Lin'an County in Hang Prefecture.

units.zh: 少拳勇，喜任俠，以解仇報怨為事。
units.en: In youth he was bold in combat, delighted in chivalry, and made settling scores his business.
units.literal: In youth he was bold in boxing, delighted in chivalry, and made settling vendettas his business.

units.zh: 唐乾符中，事於潛鎮將董昌為部校。
units.en: During the Tang Qianfu era he served the Yuqian garrison commander Dong Chang as a company officer.
units.literal: In the Qianfu era of Tang he served the Yuqian garrison commander Dong Chang as a company officer.

units.zh: 屬天下喪亂，黃巢寇嶺表，江、淮之盜賊群聚，大者攻州郡，小者剽閭裏，董昌聚眾，恣橫於杭、越之間，杭州八縣，每縣召募千人為一都，時謂之「杭州八都」，以遏黃巢之沖要。
units.en: As the realm fell into chaos, Huang Chao raided the south; bandits along the Yangzi and Huai gathered in groups—large bands attacking prefectures and counties, small ones plundering villages. Dong Chang gathered troops and rampaged between Hang and Yue. In Hangzhou's eight counties, each county recruited a thousand men as one company; the time called them the "Eight Companies of Hangzhou," to block Huang Chao's vital route.
units.literal: As the realm fell into chaos, Huang Chao raided Lingbiao; bandits along the Yangzi and Huai gathered in groups—large bands attacking prefectures and counties, small ones plundering villages. Dong Chang gathered troops and rampaged between Hang and Yue. In Hang Prefecture's eight counties, each county recruited a thousand men as one company; the time called them the "Eight Companies of Hang Prefecture," to block Huang Chao's vital route.

units.zh: 時有劉漢宏者，聚徒據越州，自稱節度使，攻收鄰郡；
units.en: At the time one Liu Hanhong gathered followers, seized Yuezhou, styled himself military governor, and attacked neighboring prefectures;
units.literal: At the time there was one Liu Hanhong, who gathered followers, seized Yue Prefecture, styled himself military governor, and attacked neighboring prefectures;

units.zh: 潤州牙將薛朗逐其節度使周寶，自稱留後。
units.en: the garrison officer Xue Lang of Runzhou drove out its military governor Zhou Bao and styled himself acting governor.
units.literal: the garrison officer Xue Lang of Run Prefecture drove out its military governor Zhou Bao and styled himself acting governor.

units.zh: 唐僖宗在蜀，詔董昌討伐，昌以軍政委镠，率八都之士進攻越州，誅漢宏，回戈攻潤州，擒薛朗。
units.en: Emperor Xizong of Tang was in Shu and ordered Dong Chang to campaign against them; Chang entrusted military affairs to Liu, led the Eight Companies against Yuezhou, executed Hanhong, turned his blades on Runzhou, and captured Xue Lang.
units.literal: Emperor Xizong of Tang was in Shu and ordered Dong Chang to campaign against them; Chang entrusted military affairs to Liu, led the men of the Eight Companies to attack Yue Prefecture, executed Hanhong, turned his blades to attack Run Prefecture, and captured Xue Lang.

units.zh: 江、浙平，董昌為浙東節度使、越州刺史，表镠代己為杭州刺史。
units.en: When Jiang and Zhe were pacified, Dong Chang became military governor of Zhedong and prefect of Yuezhou, and memorialized that Liu replace him as prefect of Hangzhou.
units.literal: When Jiang and Zhe were pacified, Dong Chang became Military Governor of Zhedong and prefect of Yue Prefecture, and memorialized that Liu replace him as prefect of Hang Prefecture.

units.zh: 唐景福中，朝廷以李鋋為浙江西道鎮海軍節度使。
units.en: During the Tang Jingfu era the court appointed Li Qian military governor of the Zhenhai Army in Zhejiang West Circuit.
units.literal: In the Jingfu era of Tang the court appointed Li Qian military governor of the Zhenhai Army in Zhejiang West Circuit.

units.zh: 時孫儒、楊行密交亂，淮海煙塵數千里，镠常率師以為防捍，孫儒據宣州，不敢侵江、浙，由是镠勛名日著。
units.en: Sun Ru and Yang Xingmi were locked in mutual turmoil, and battle smoke covered the Huai and sea region for thousands of li. Liu often led troops in defense; Sun Ru held Xuanzhou and dared not invade Jiang and Zhe, and Liu's fame for merit grew daily.
units.literal: At the time Sun Ru and Yang Xingmi were in mutual turmoil; battle smoke covered the Huai and sea region for thousands of li. Liu often led troops in defense; Sun Ru held Xuan Prefecture and dared not invade Jiang and Zhe—thereby Liu's fame for merit grew daily.

units.zh: 久之，李鋋終不至治所，朝廷以镠為鎮海軍節度，仍移潤州軍額於杭州為治所，又立威勝軍於越州，董昌為節度使。
units.en: After a long time Li Qian never reached his headquarters; the court appointed Liu military governor of the Zhenhai Army, moved the Runzhou military designation to Hangzhou as headquarters, and established the Weisheng Army at Yuezhou with Dong Chang as military governor.
units.literal: After a long time Li Qian never reached his headquarters; the court appointed Liu military governor of the Zhenhai Army, moved the Run Prefecture military designation to Hang Prefecture as headquarters, and established the Weisheng Army at Yue Prefecture with Dong Chang as military governor.

units.zh: 昌漸驕貴，自言身應符讖，又為妖人王百藝所誑，僭稱尊號，乃於越州自稱羅平國王，年號大聖，偽命镠為兩浙都將。
units.en: Chang gradually grew proud and exalted; he claimed his person matched prophetic signs and was further deceived by the sorcerer Wang Baiyi into usurping a royal title. At Yuezhou he styled himself King of the Luoping State, with the era name Dasheng, and falsely ordered Liu to be commander-in-chief of the Two Zhes.
units.literal: Chang gradually grew proud and exalted; he claimed his person matched prophetic signs and was further deceived by the sorcerer Wang Baiyi into usurping a royal title. At Yue Prefecture he styled himself King of the Luoping State, with the era name Dasheng, and falsely ordered Liu to be commander-in-chief of the Two Zhes.

units.zh: 镠不受命，以狀聞，唐昭宗命镠討昌。
units.en: Liu refused the order, reported the situation, and Emperor Zhaozong of Tang ordered Liu to campaign against Chang.
units.literal: Liu refused the order, reported the situation, and Emperor Zhaozong of Tang ordered Liu to campaign against Chang.

units.zh: 乾寧四年，镠率浙西將士破越州，擒昌以獻，朝廷嘉其功，賜镠鐵券，又除宰臣王溥為威勝軍節度使。
units.en: In the fourth year of Qianning Liu led the officers and soldiers of western Zhe to break Yuezhou, captured Chang and presented him to the court; the court praised his merit, granted Liu an iron certificate, and appointed the chief minister Wang Pu military governor of the Weisheng Army.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Qianning Liu led the officers and soldiers of western Zhe to break Yue Prefecture, captured Chang and presented him; the court praised his merit, granted Liu an iron certificate, and appointed the chief minister Wang Pu military governor of the Weisheng Army.

units.zh: 而兩浙士庶拜章，請以镠兼杭、越二鎮，朝廷不能制，因而授之，改威勝軍為鎮東，镠乃兼鎮海、鎮東兩藩節制。
units.en: The gentry and commoners of the Two Zhes submitted memorials asking that Liu hold both Hang and Yue commands; the court could not restrain them and therefore granted it, changed the Weisheng Army to Zhendong, and Liu then held command over both the Zhenhai and Zhendong circuits.
units.literal: The gentry and commoners of the Two Zhes submitted memorials asking that Liu hold both Hang and Yue commands; the court could not restrain them and therefore granted it, changed the Weisheng Army to Zhendong, and Liu then held command over both the Zhenhai and Zhendong circuits.

units.zh: 镠既兼兩鎮，精兵三萬，而楊行密連歲興戎，攻蘇、湖、潤等州，欲兼並兩浙，累為镠所敗，亦為行密侵盜數州，而镠所部止一十三州而已。
units.en: Once Liu held both commands he had thirty thousand elite troops; yet Yang Xingmi raised arms year after year, attacking Suzhou, Huzhou, Runzhou, and other prefectures, wishing to annex the Two Zhes. He was repeatedly defeated by Liu, but also seized several prefectures from Liu—Liu's domain amounted to only thirteen prefectures.
units.literal: Once Liu held both commands he had thirty thousand elite troops; yet Yang Xingmi raised arms year after year, attacking Su, Hu, Run, and other prefectures, wishing to annex the Two Zhes. He was repeatedly defeated by Liu, but also seized several prefectures from Liu—Liu's domain amounted to only thirteen prefectures.

units.zh: 天復中，镠大將許再思、徐綰叛，引宣州節度使田頵謀襲杭州。
units.en: In the Tianfu era Liu's great generals Xu Zaisi and Xu Wan rebelled, bringing in Tian Yun, military governor of Xuanzhou, to plot a raid on Hangzhou.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era Liu's great generals Xu Zaisi and Xu Wan rebelled, bringing in Tian Yun, military governor of Xuan Prefecture, to plot a raid on Hang Prefecture.

units.zh: 田頵等率師掩至城下，镠激厲軍士，一戰敗之，生擒徐綰，田頵遁走。
units.en: Tian Yun and others led troops in a surprise attack to the foot of the walls; Liu roused his soldiers, defeated them in one battle, captured Xu Wan alive, and Tian Yun fled.
units.literal: Tian Yun and others led troops in a surprise attack to the foot of the walls; Liu roused his soldiers, defeated them in one battle, captured Xu Wan alive, and Tian Yun fled.

units.zh: 镠於臨安故裏興造第舍，窮極壯麗，歲時遊於里中，車徒雄盛，萬夫羅列。
units.en: Liu built mansions in his old home district of Lin'an, extravagantly magnificent; at the seasons he toured the village with a grand procession of chariots and attendants, ten thousand men arrayed in ranks.
units.literal: Liu built mansions in his old home district of Lin'an, extravagantly magnificent; at the seasons he toured the village with a grand procession of chariots and attendants, ten thousand men arrayed in ranks.

units.zh: 其父寬每聞镠至，走竄避之，镠即徒步訪寬，請言其故。
units.en: His father Kuan, whenever he heard Liu was coming, would flee and hide; Liu then went on foot to visit Kuan and asked the reason.
units.literal: His father Kuan, whenever he heard Liu was coming, would flee and hide; Liu then went on foot to visit Kuan and asked the reason.

units.zh: 寬曰：「吾家世田漁為事，未嘗有貴達如此，爾今為十三州主，三面受敵，與人爭利，恐禍及吾家，所以不忍見汝。」
units.en: Kuan said, "Our family for generations has made its living by farming and fishing; never has anyone risen to such eminence. You are now master of thirteen prefectures, beset on three sides, contending with others for profit—I fear calamity will reach our house, and so I cannot bear to see you."
units.literal: Kuan said: "Our family for generations has made its living by farming and fishing; never has anyone risen to such eminence. You are now master of thirteen prefectures, beset on three sides, contending with others for profit—I fear calamity will reach our house, and so I cannot bear to see you."

units.zh: 镠泣謝之。
units.en: Liu wept and apologized.
units.literal: Liu wept and apologized.

units.zh: 镠於唐昭宗朝，位至太師、中書令、本郡王，食邑二萬戶。
units.en: Under Emperor Zhaozong of Tang Liu rose to Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of his home commandery, with a fief of twenty thousand households.
units.literal: Under Emperor Zhaozong of Tang Liu rose to Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of his home commandery, with a fief of twenty thousand households.

units.zh: 梁祖革命，以镠為尚父、吳越國王。
units.en: When the Liang founder changed the dynasty, Liu was made Sire Father and King of Wuyue.
units.literal: When the Liang founder changed the dynasty, Liu was made Sire Father and King of Wuyue.

units.zh: 梁末帝時，加諸道兵馬元帥。
units.en: Under the Last Emperor of Liang he was further given the title Marshal of All Armies of the Circuits.
units.literal: Under the Last Emperor of Liang he was further given the title Marshal of All Armies of the Circuits.

units.zh: 同光中，為天下兵馬都元帥、尚父、守尚書令，封吳越國王，賜玉冊、金印。
units.en: In the Tongguang era he became Grand Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven, Sire Father, and Acting Director of the Secretariat; he was enfeoffed as King of Wuyue and granted a jade register and gold seal.
units.literal: In the Tongguang era he became Grand Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven, Sire Father, and Acting Director of the Secretariat; he was enfeoffed as King of Wuyue and granted a jade register and gold seal.

units.zh: 初，莊宗至洛陽，镠厚陳貢奉，求為國王，及玉冊詔下，有司詳議，群臣咸言：「玉簡金字，惟至尊一人，錢镠人臣，不可。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong reached Luoyang, Liu lavishly presented tribute and sought to be made king. When the jade-register edict was issued, the responsible offices deliberated in detail, and the ministers all said, "The golden characters on the jade slips belong to the supreme sovereign alone; Qian Liu is a subject—this cannot be.
units.literal: At first, when Emperor Zhuangzong reached Luoyang, Liu lavishly presented tribute and sought to be made king. When the jade-register edict was issued, the responsible offices deliberated in detail, and the ministers all said: "The golden characters on the jade slips belong to the supreme sovereign alone; Qian Liu is a subject—this cannot be.

units.zh: 又本朝己來，除四夷遠藩，羈縻冊拜，或有國王之號，而九州之內亦無此事。」
units.en: Moreover, since this dynasty began, apart from distant tribes and far frontiers where investiture was granted in the manner of loose control, there might be the title of king—but within the Nine Provinces there has never been such a thing."
units.literal: Moreover, since this dynasty began, apart from distant tribes and far frontiers where investiture was granted in the manner of loose control, there might be the title of king—but within the Nine Provinces there has never been such a thing."

units.zh: 郭崇韜尤不容其僭，而樞密承旨段徊，奸幸用事，能移崇韜之意，曲為镠陳情，崇韜黽勉從之。
units.en: Guo Chongtao especially would not tolerate the usurpation, but Duan Huai, chief drafter of the Bureau of Military Affairs, a favorite who held power, was able to shift Chongtao's mind and plead Liu's case at length; Chongtao reluctantly assented.
units.literal: Guo Chongtao especially would not tolerate the usurpation, but Duan Huai, chief drafter of the Bureau of Military Affairs, a favorite who held power, was able to shift Chongtao's mind and plead Liu's case at length; Chongtao reluctantly assented.

units.zh: 镠乃以鎮海、鎮東軍節度使名目授其子元瓘，自稱吳越國王，命所居曰宮殿，府署曰朝廷，其參佐稱臣，僭大朝百僚之號，但不改年號而已。
units.en: Liu then granted the titles of Military Governor of the Zhenhai and Zhendong Armies to his son Yuan Guan, styled himself King of Wuyue, called his residence a palace and his headquarters a court, had his aides address him as minister, and usurped the titles of the great court's officials—only he did not change the era name.
units.literal: Liu then granted the titles of Military Governor of the Zhenhai and Zhendong Armies to his son Yuan Guan, styled himself King of Wuyue, called his residence a palace and his headquarters a court, had his aides address him as minister, and usurped the titles of the great court's officials—only he did not change the era name.

units.zh: 偽行制冊，加封爵於新羅、渤海，海中夷落亦皆遣使行封冊焉。
units.en: He falsely issued edicts of investiture, granting titles to Silla and Bohai, and also sent envoys to perform investiture among the tribal settlements of the sea.
units.literal: He falsely issued edicts of investiture, granting titles to Silla and Bohai, and also sent envoys to perform investiture among the tribal settlements of the sea.

units.zh: 明宗即位之初，安重誨用事，镠嘗與重誨書，云「吳越國王致書於某官執事」，不敘暄涼，重誨怒其無禮。
units.en: Early in Emperor Mingzong's reign An Chonghui held power. Liu once wrote to Chonghui, "The King of Wuyue writes to a certain official in charge," without the usual seasonal greetings, and Chonghui was angered by the discourtesy.
units.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Mingzong's reign An Chonghui held power. Liu once wrote to Chonghui, saying, "The King of Wuyue writes to a certain official in charge," without the usual greetings of season; Chonghui was angry at the discourtesy.

units.zh: 屬供奉官烏昭遇使於兩浙，每以朝廷事私於吳人，仍目镠為殿下，自稱臣，謁镠行舞蹈之禮。
units.en: When the palace attendant Wu Zhaoyu was sent as envoy to the two Zhe regions, he privately disclosed court affairs to the Wu people, addressed Liu as Your Highness, styled himself a minister, and performed the bowing and dancing rites when visiting him.
units.literal: When the palace attendant Wu Zhaoyu was sent as envoy to the two Zhe regions, he privately disclosed court affairs to the Wu people, still addressed Liu as Your Highness, styled himself minister, and performed the bowing and dancing rites when visiting Liu.

units.zh: 及回，副使韓玫具述其事，重誨因削镠元帥、尚父、國王之號，以太師致仕。
units.en: On his return the vice envoy Han Mei reported the matter in full; Chonghui therefore stripped Liu of his titles as Marshal, Sire Father, and King and retired him as Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: When he returned, the vice envoy Han Mei fully reported the matter; Chonghui therefore stripped Liu of the titles Marshal, Sire Father, and King and retired him as Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 久之，其子元瓘等上表陳敘。
units.en: After a long while his son Yuan Guan and others submitted a memorial explaining the matter.
units.literal: After a long while his son Yuan Guan and others submitted a memorial explaining the case.

units.zh: 時淮寇攻逼荊南，明宗疑其同惡，因降詔詰之，元瓘等復遣使自淮南間道上表，云：竊念臣父天下兵馬都元帥、吳越國王臣镠，爰自乾符之歲，便立功勞；
units.en: At that time Huai bandits pressed Jingnan, and Mingzong suspected collusion; he therefore issued an edict of inquiry. Yuan Guan and the others again sent envoys by a secret route through Huainan to submit a memorial, saying: I respectfully reflect that my father, Grand Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven and King of Wuyue, subject Liu, from the year of Qianfu onward established merit and toil;
units.literal: At that time Huai bandits pressed Jingnan, and Mingzong suspected Liu of sharing their evil; he therefore issued an edict of inquiry. Yuan Guan and the others again sent envoys by a secret route through Huainan to submit a memorial, saying: I respectfully reflect that my father, Grand Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven and King of Wuyue, subject Liu, from the year of Qianfu onward established merit and toil;

units.zh: 至於天復之初，已封茅土。
units.en: by the beginning of Tianfu he had already received a fief.
units.literal: by the beginning of Tianfu he had already received a fief.

units.zh: 兩殄稽山之僭偽，頻叨鳳詔之褒崇，賜鐵券而礪嶽帶河，藏清廟而銘鐘鏤鼎。
units.en: Twice he extinguished the usurpation at Mount Ji, repeatedly received the phoenix edicts of praise and elevation, was granted an iron certificate binding his merit as enduring as mountains and rivers, and had his honors stored in the Clear Temple and inscribed on bells and cauldrons.
units.literal: Twice he extinguished the usurpation at Mount Ji, repeatedly received the phoenix edicts of praise and elevation, was granted an iron certificate binding his merit as enduring as mountains and rivers, and had his honors stored in the Clear Temple and inscribed on bells and cauldrons.

units.zh: 歷事列聖，竭誠累朝，罄臣節以無虧，荷君恩而益重。
units.en: Serving successive sovereigns through many reigns, he exhausted his loyalty without failing in duty, and bore the emperor's grace ever more heavily.
units.literal: Serving successive sovereigns through many reigns, he exhausted his loyalty without failing in duty, and bore the emperor's grace ever more heavily.

units.zh: 楚茅吳柚，常居群後之先；
units.en: With Chu hemp and Wu citrus, he always stood ahead among the vassals;
units.literal: With Chu hemp and Wu citrus, he always stood ahead among the vassals;

units.zh: 赤豹黃羆，不在諸方之後。
units.en: with red leopards and yellow bears, he was not behind the other regions.
units.literal: with red leopards and yellow bears, he was not behind the other regions.

units.zh: 雲臺寫像，盟府書勛，戮力本朝，一心體國。
units.en: His portrait was painted at the Cloud Platform, his merit recorded in the League Office; he exerted his strength for the dynasty and devoted his heart to the state.
units.literal: His portrait was painted at the Cloud Platform, his merit recorded in the League Office; he exerted his strength for the dynasty and devoted his heart to the state.

units.zh: 常戒臣兄弟曰：「汝等諸子，須記斯言：老父起自諸都，早平多難，素推忠勇，實效辛勤，遂蒙聖主之疇庸，獲忝真主之列壤，恒積滿盈之懼，豫懷燕翼之憂。
units.en: He often admonished us brothers, saying, "You sons must remember these words: your old father rose from the various companies, early pacified many troubles, was always praised for loyalty and courage, and truly rendered hard service; thus he received the sage sovereign's selection for merit and was honored with a fief from the true lord. I constantly harbor fear of fullness and overflow, and forebode the worry of sheltering posterity.
units.literal: He often admonished us brothers, saying: "You sons must remember these words: your old father rose from the various companies, early pacified many troubles, was always praised for loyalty and courage, and truly rendered hard service; thus he received the sage sovereign's selection for merit and was honored with a fief from the true lord. I constantly harbor fear of fullness and overflow, and forebode the worry of sheltering posterity.

units.zh: 蓋以恩禮殊尤，寵榮亢極，名品既逾於五等，春秋將及於八旬，不諱之談，爾當靜聽。
units.en: Because favor and ritual were exceptionally great and glory reached its height, rank and title already exceeded the five grades, and my years approach eighty, this unreserved talk—you must listen quietly.
units.literal: Because favor and ritual were exceptionally great and glory reached its height, rank and title already exceeded the five grades, and my years approach eighty, this unreserved talk—you must listen quietly.

units.zh: 而況手殲妖亂，親睹興亡，豈宜自為厲階，更尋覆轍。
units.en: Moreover, having with my own hands destroyed demonic rebellion and witnessed rise and fall with my own eyes, how could I make myself a source of disaster and again follow a path to ruin?
units.literal: Moreover, having with my own hands destroyed demonic rebellion and witnessed rise and fall with my own eyes, how could I make myself a source of disaster and again follow a path to ruin?

units.zh: 老身猶健，且作國王之呼；
units.en: This old body is still hale; let me for now accept the title of king;
units.literal: This old body is still hale; let me for now accept the title of king;

units.zh: 嗣子承家，但守藩臣之分。」
units.en: the heir who inherits the house should only keep to the station of a frontier vassal."
units.literal: the heir who inherits the house should only keep to the station of a frontier vassal."

units.zh: 臣等鯉庭灑袂，雁序書紳，中心藏之，敬聞命矣。
units.en: We brothers, with tears in the carp courtyard and the geese order written on our sashes, hid it in our hearts and respectfully received the command.
units.literal: We brothers, with tears in the carp courtyard and the geese order written on our sashes, hid it in our hearts and respectfully received the command.

units.zh: 頃以濟陰歸邸，梁苑稱尊，所在英雄，遞相仿斅，互起投龜之詬，皆興逐鹿之謀。
units.en: Recently, when the lord returned to his seat at Jiyin and claimed supremacy in the Liang garden, heroes everywhere imitated one another in turn, each raising the reproach of casting the tortoise, all stirring schemes to contend for the realm.
units.literal: Recently, when the lord returned to his seat at Jiyin and claimed supremacy in the Liang garden, heroes everywhere imitated one another in turn, each raising the reproach of casting the tortoise, all stirring schemes to contend for the realm.

units.zh: 惟臣父王，未嘗隨例。
units.en: Only my father the king never followed the example.
units.literal: Only my father the king never followed the example.

units.zh: 從微至著，悉蒙天子之絲綸；
units.en: From obscurity to eminence, he wholly received the Son of Heaven's silk edicts;
units.literal: From obscurity to eminence, he wholly received the Son of Heaven's silk edicts;

units.zh: 啟土封王，自守諸侯之土宇。
units.en: opening land and receiving enfeoffment as king, he kept to a vassal's territory.
units.literal: opening land and receiving enfeoffment as king, he kept to a vassal's territory.

units.zh: 乙酉歲，伏蒙莊宗皇帝遙降玉冊、金印，恩加曲阜營丘，顯自大朝，來封小國，遂有強名之改補，實無幹紀之包藏。
units.en: In the yiyou year we respectfully received from afar Emperor Zhuangzong's descent of the jade register and gold seal, grace added like Qufu and Yingqiu, clearly from the great court coming to enfeoff our small state; there was thus a change and supplement of a strong title, but in truth no harboring of rebellion against the statutes.
units.literal: In the yiyou year we respectfully received from afar Emperor Zhuangzong's descent of the jade register and gold seal, grace added like Qufu and Yingqiu, clearly from the great court coming to enfeoff our small state; there was thus a change and supplement of a strong title, but in truth no harboring of rebellion against the statutes.

units.zh: 兼使人徐筠等進貢之時，禮儀有失，尚蒙赦宥，未置典刑，敢不投杖責躬，負荊請罪。
units.en: Moreover, when our envoy Xu Yun and others presented tribute, there were lapses in ritual; we still received pardon and were not subjected to statutory punishment—how could we not cast aside our staffs to blame ourselves and come bearing thorns to beg forgiveness?
units.literal: Moreover, when our envoy Xu Yun and others presented tribute, there were lapses in ritual; we still received pardon and were not subjected to statutory punishment—how could we not cast aside our staffs to blame ourselves and come bearing thorns to beg forgiveness?

units.zh: 且爽為臣之禮，誠乖事上之儀，夙夜包羞，寢食俱廢，捧詔而神魂戰栗，拜章而芒刺交並。
units.en: Moreover, having failed in the rites of a subject and truly departed from the protocol of serving superiors, day and night we are wrapped in shame, sleep and food both abandoned; receiving the edict our spirits tremble, submitting memorials thorns pierce us on every side.
units.literal: Moreover, having failed in the rites of a subject and truly departed from the protocol of serving superiors, day and night we are wrapped in shame, sleep and food both abandoned; receiving the edict our spirits tremble, submitting memorials thorns pierce us on every side.

units.zh: 伏以皇帝陛下，浚哲文思，含宏光大，智周萬物，日辟四方，既容能改之非，許降自新之恕，將功補過，舍短從長，矧茲近代相持，豈足深機遠料。
units.en: I respectfully consider that Your Majesty the Emperor is deep in wisdom and literary thought, broad and magnanimous, knowing all things and daily opening the four quarters; having already allowed faults that can be corrected and granted pardon for renewal, weighing merit against faults and setting aside the short for the long—how much less should recent rivalries be grounds for deep suspicion and distant calculation.
units.literal: I respectfully consider that Your Majesty the Emperor is deep in wisdom and literary thought, broad and magnanimous, knowing all things and daily opening the four quarters; having already allowed faults that can be corrected and granted pardon for renewal, weighing merit against faults and setting aside the short for the long—how much less should recent rivalries be grounds for deep suspicion and distant calculation.

units.zh: 且臣本道，與淮南雖連疆畛，久結仇讎，交惡尋盟，十翻九覆，縱敵已逾於三紀，弭兵才僅於數年，諒非唇齒之邦，真謂腹心之疾。
units.en: Moreover, our circuit, though it shares a border with Huainan, has long been bound in enmity; hostility alternates with alliance, ten times overturned and nine times reversed; letting the enemy go has already exceeded three reigns, and ceasing arms has lasted only a few years—it is surely not a lip-and-teeth state, but truly a disease of the heart and vitals.
units.literal: Moreover, our circuit, though it shares a border with Huainan, has long been bound in enmity; hostility alternates with alliance, ten times overturned and nine times reversed; letting the enemy go has already exceeded three reigns, and ceasing arms has lasted only a few years—it is surely not a lip-and-teeth state, but truly a disease of the heart and vitals.

units.zh: 今奉詔書責問，合陳本末端由，布在眾多，寧煩覼縷，彼既人而無禮，此亦和而不同。
units.en: Now that we have received your edict of inquiry and reproof, we ought to set forth the full origin and end of the matter; the account is already spread among many records and need not weary you with exhaustive detail—they are men without propriety, while we, for our part, seek harmony yet stand apart from them.
units.literal: Now, having received the edict of inquiry and reproof, we ought to set forth the origin and end of the matter in full; the account is spread among many and need not weary you with exhaustive detail—they are men without propriety, while we, for our part, are harmonious yet not the same.

units.zh: 近知侵軼荊門，乖張事大，儻王師之問罪，願率眾以齊攻，必致先登，庶觀後效。
units.en: We have recently learned of their encroachment and raids on Jingmen—conduct perverse toward the throne. If the imperial army should call them to account, we wish to lead our forces in a joint attack and will surely strive to be first over the walls, that Your Majesty may witness our future service.
units.literal: Recently we learned of their encroachment and raids on Jingmen, perverse conduct toward the Great State; if the royal army should call them to account, we wish to lead our forces in joint attack and surely strive to be first to scale the walls, that you may observe our later merit.

units.zh: 橫秋雕鶚，只待指呼；
units.en: Like autumn eagles poised on the wing, we wait only for your command;
units.literal: Like autumn eagles poised in flight, we wait only for a command;

units.zh: 躍匣蛟龍，誓平讎隙。
units.en: Like dragons leaping from their sheath, we vow to settle this feud.
units.literal: Like dragons leaping from their casket, we vow to settle the feud.

units.zh: 今則訓齊樓櫓，淬礪戈鋋，決副天威，冀明臣節。
units.en: We are now drilling siege towers and rams, sharpening spears and blades, resolved to support the imperial might and hoping thereby to make our loyalty as subjects plain.
units.literal: Now we are drilling towers and rams, sharpening spears and blades, resolved to assist Heaven's majesty and hoping to make clear our loyalty as subjects.

units.zh: 伏以臣父王镠，已於泛海，繼有飛章。
units.en: I respectfully note that my father, King Liu, has already crossed the sea to court and has since sent urgent memorials.
units.literal: I respectfully note that my father, King Liu, already crossed the sea and subsequently sent urgent memorials.

units.zh: 陳父子之丹誠，高懸皎日；
units.en: They affirmed father-and-son devotion, bright as the sun in the sky;
units.literal: Declaring the father-and-son loyalty bright as the sun hung high;

units.zh: 展君臣之大義，上指圓穹。
units.en: displaying the great bond between sovereign and subject, pointing upward to the dome of Heaven.
units.literal: Displaying the great bond between sovereign and subject, pointing upward to the dome of Heaven.

units.zh: 其將修貢賦於梯航，混車書而表率，如虧奉職，自有陰誅。
units.en: We shall continue to send tribute by ship and overland routes, unify chariots and script as your exemplar; should we fail in our duty, Heaven's hidden punishment will come of itself.
units.literal: We shall continue tribute by ship and ladder-path, unify chariots and script as an exemplar; if we fail in duty, Heaven's hidden punishment will come of itself.

units.zh: 今春已具表章，未蒙便賜俞允，地遠而經年方達，天高而瀝懇難通。
units.en: This spring we already submitted our memorial in full, yet have not promptly received your approval; our land is distant and a full year passes before it arrives, Heaven is high and our earnest pleas are hard to convey.
units.literal: This spring we already submitted our memorial in full, yet have not promptly received approval; the land is far and a full year passes before it arrives, Heaven is high and our earnest pleas are hard to convey.

units.zh: 伏乞聖慈，曲行明命。
