units.en: We humbly beg Your sacred grace to grant us your clear command.
units.literal: We humbly beg Your sacred grace to bend your clear command to us.

units.zh: 淩霜益翠，始知松柏之心；
units.en: Enduring frost they grow greener still—thus the steadfast heart of pine and cypress is known;
units.literal: Enduring frost they grow greener still—thus the steadfast heart of pine and cypress is known;

units.zh: 異日成功，方顯忠貞之節。
units.en: only when success comes on another day will our loyal fidelity be fully revealed.
units.literal: Only when success comes on another day will our loyal fidelity be fully revealed.

units.zh: 臣元瓘等無任感激祈恩戰懼依投之至。
units.en: Your subjects Yuanguan and others are overcome with gratitude, praying for grace, trembling in awe, and bound in utmost devotion.
units.literal: Your subjects Yuanguan and others are overcome with gratitude, praying for grace, trembling in awe, and bound in utmost devotion.

units.zh: 謹遣急腳，間道奉絹表陳乞奏謝以聞。
units.en: We respectfully dispatch a swift courier by secret route to present this silk memorial, stating our petition and expressing our thanks for your attention.
units.literal: We respectfully dispatch a swift courier by secret route to present this silk memorial, stating our petition and expressing thanks for report.

units.zh: 明宗嘉之，乃降制復授镠天下兵馬都元帥、尚父、吳越國王。
units.en: Mingzong approved this and issued an edict reappointing Liu as Commander-in-Chief of All Armed Forces Under Heaven, Imperial Sire-Father, and King of Wuyue.
units.literal: Mingzong approved this and issued an edict reappointing Liu as Commander-in-Chief of All Armed Forces Under Heaven, Imperial Sire-Father, and King of Wuyue.

units.zh: 未幾，又詔賜上表不名。
units.en: Before long, another edict granted him the privilege of not being named when submitting memorials.
units.literal: Before long, another edict granted him the privilege of not being named when submitting memorials.

units.zh: 〈（《五代會要》載長興二年四月詔曰：周榮呂望，有尚父之稱；
units.en: (The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 records an edict of the fourth month of the second year of Changxing saying: Zhou had Rong and Lü Wang, who bore the title Imperial Sire-Father;
units.literal: (The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 records an edict of the fourth month of the second year of Changxing saying: Zhou had Rong and Lü Wang, who bore the title Imperial Sire-Father;

units.zh: 漢重蕭何，有不名之禮。
units.en: Han honored Xiao He with the ritual of not being named.
units.literal: Han honored Xiao He with the ritual of not being named.

units.zh: 錢珝冠公侯之位，統吳越之封，宜示異恩，俾當縟禮，其錢珝宜賜不名。）〉
units.en: Qian Xu holds the rank of duke or marquis and rules the Wuyue fief; exceptional favor should be shown and the full ceremonial granted—Qian Xu should be granted the privilege of not being named.)〉
units.literal: Qian Xu holds the rank of duke or marquis and rules the Wuyue fief; exceptional favor should be shown and the full ceremonial granted—Qian Xu should be granted the privilege of not being named.)〉

units.zh: 镠在杭州垂四十年，窮奢極貴。
units.en: Liu resided in Hangzhou for nearly forty years, living in the utmost luxury and splendor.
units.literal: Liu resided in Hangzhou for nearly forty years, exhausting luxury and reaching the utmost of wealth and rank.

units.zh: 錢塘江舊日海潮逼州城，镠大庀工徒，鑿石填江，又平江中羅剎石，悉起臺榭，廣郡郭周三十里，邑屋之繁會，江山之雕麗，實江南之勝概也，镠學書，好吟詠。
units.en: In former days the sea tide of the Qiantang River pressed upon the prefectural city; Liu mustered a great force of laborers, carved stone to fill the river, and leveled the Luocha Rock in midstream, raising towers and pavilions everywhere and expanding the city walls for thirty li around—the throng of houses and the carved splendor of river and hills were truly the finest sights of Jiangnan. Liu studied calligraphy and loved to compose and recite poetry.
units.literal: In former days the sea tide of the Qiantang River pressed upon the prefectural city; Liu greatly assembled workers, carved stone to fill the river, and also leveled the Luocha Rock in midstream, raising towers and pavilions everywhere and expanding the city walls for thirty li around—the throng of houses and the carved splendor of river and hills were truly the finest sights of Jiangnan. Liu studied calligraphy and loved to compose and recite poetry.

units.zh: 江東有羅隱者，有詩名，聞於海內，依镠為參佐。
units.en: In Jiangdong there was Luo Yin, famed for poetry and known throughout the realm, who served Liu as a staff adviser.
units.literal: In Jiangdong there was Luo Yin, famed for poetry and known throughout the realm, who joined Liu as a staff adviser.

units.zh: 镠嘗與隱唱和，隱好譏諷，嘗戲為詩，言镠微時騎牛操挺事，镠亦怡然不怒，其通恕也如此。
units.en: Liu once exchanged verses with Yin; Yin loved satire and once playfully composed a poem about Liu riding an ox and wielding a staff in his humble days—Liu remained placid and unangered. His indulgence and forbearance were such as this.
units.literal: Liu once exchanged verses with Yin; Yin loved satire and once playfully composed a poem about Liu riding an ox and wielding a staff in his humble days—Liu remained placid and unangered; his indulgence and forbearance were such as this.

units.zh: 镠雖季年荒恣，然自唐朝，於梁室，莊宗中興已來，每來揚帆越海，貢奉無闕，故中朝亦以此善之。
units.en: Though Liu in his later years was wasteful and unrestrained, from the Tang dynasty through the Liang and since Zhuangzong's restoration, whenever ships sailed across the sea tribute was never lacking; the central court therefore held this in his favor.
units.literal: Though Liu in his later years was wasteful and unrestrained, from the Tang dynasty through the Liang and since Zhuangzong's restoration, whenever ships sailed across the sea tribute was never lacking; the central court therefore held this in his favor.

units.zh: 镠以長興三年三月二十八日薨，年八十一。
units.en: Liu died on the twenty-eighth day of the third month of the third year of Changxing, at age eighty-one.
units.literal: Liu died on the twenty-eighth day of the third month of the third year of Changxing, at age eighty-one.

units.zh: 制曰：「故天下兵馬都元帥、尚父、吳越國王錢镠，累朝元老，當代勛賢，位已極於人臣，名素高於簡冊。
units.en: An edict said: "The late Commander-in-Chief of All Armed Forces Under Heaven, Imperial Sire-Father, and King of Wuyue, Qian Liu, was an elder statesman of successive reigns and a meritorious worthy of his age; his rank had already reached the summit among subjects, and his name had long stood high in the historical records.
units.literal: An edict said: "The late Commander-in-Chief of All Armed Forces Under Heaven, Imperial Sire-Father, and King of Wuyue, Qian Liu, was an elder statesman of successive reigns and a meritorious worthy of his age; his rank had already reached the summit among subjects, and his name had long stood high in the historical records.

units.zh: 贈典既無其官爵，易名宜示其優崇，宜令所司定謚，以王禮葬，仍賜神道碑。」
units.en: Since there is no posthumous office or rank to confer, a change of name should show exceptional honor; the appropriate offices should determine his posthumous title, bury him with royal rites, and grant a spirit-way stele."
units.literal: Since there is no posthumous office or rank to confer, a change of name should show exceptional honor; the appropriate offices should determine his posthumous title, bury him with royal rites, and grant a spirit-way stele."

units.zh: 謚曰武肅。
units.en: His posthumous title was Wusu.
units.literal: His posthumous title was Wusu.

units.zh: 镠初事董昌，時年甫壯室，性尚剛烈。
units.en: When Liu first served Dong Chang, he was just entering manhood and his nature was fierce and unyielding.
units.literal: When Liu first served Dong Chang, he was just entering manhood and his nature was fierce and unyielding.

units.zh: 時有儒士謁於主帥，已進刺矣，見镠稍怠，镠怒，投之羅剎江，及典謁者將召，镠詐云：「客已拂衣去矣。」
units.en: Once a scholar came to call on the commander-in-chief; he had already presented his card, but when he saw Liu he grew somewhat negligent. Liu in anger threw him into the Luocha River. When the usher was about to summon him, Liu falsely said, "The guest has already brushed his robes and departed."
units.literal: Once a scholar came to call on the commander-in-chief; he had already presented his card, but when he saw Liu he grew somewhat negligent. Liu in anger threw him into the Luocha River. When the usher was about to summon him, Liu falsely said, "The guest has already brushed his robes and departed."

units.zh: 及為帥時，有人獻詩云：「一條江水檻前流。」
units.en: When he became commander, someone presented a poem saying, "A single stretch of river flows before the balustrade."
units.literal: When he became commander, someone presented a poem saying, "A single stretch of river flows before the balustrade."

units.zh: 镠不悅，以為譏己，尋害之。
units.en: Liu was displeased, took it as a satire on himself, and soon had the man killed.
units.literal: Liu was displeased, took it as a satire on himself, and soon had the man killed.

units.zh: 迨於晚歲，方愛人下士，留心理道，數十年間，時甚歸美。
units.en: Only in his later years did he come to cherish men and honor scholars, devoting himself to the Way; for several decades the age greatly praised him.
units.literal: Only in his later years did he come to cherish men and honor scholars, devoting himself to the Way; for several decades the age greatly praised him.

units.zh: 镠尤恃崇盛，分兩浙為數鎮，其節制署而後奏。
units.en: Liu especially relied on his grandeur and prosperity, dividing the Two Zhes into several prefectures and appointing their military commissioners first, reporting afterward.
units.literal: Liu especially relied on his grandeur and prosperity, dividing the Two Zhes into several prefectures, appointing their military commissioners first and reporting afterward.

units.zh: 左右前後皆兒孫甥侄，軒陛服飾，比於王者，兩浙裏俗咸曰「海龍王」。
units.en: On his left and right, before and behind, were all sons, grandsons, nephews, and cousins; the halls and steps, dress and adornment, rivaled those of a king. Throughout the Two Zhes the common people all called him "Sea Dragon King."
units.literal: On his left and right, before and behind, were all sons, grandsons, nephews, and cousins; the halls and steps, dress and adornment, rivaled those of a king. Throughout the Two Zhes the common people all called him "Sea Dragon King."

units.zh: 梁開平中，浙民上言，請為镠立生祠，梁太祖許之，令翰林學士李琪撰生祠堂碑以賜之，至今蒸黎饗之，子孫保之，斯亦近代之名王也。
units.en: In the Kaiping era of Liang, the people of Zhe petitioned to erect a living shrine to Liu; Emperor Taizu of Liang approved it and ordered Hanlin Academician Li Qi to compose the shrine stele and bestow it. To this day the common people offer sacrifice there and his descendants preserve it—thus he was also a famed king of recent times.
units.literal: In the Kaiping era of Liang, the people of Zhe petitioned to erect a living shrine to Liu; Emperor Taizu of Liang approved it and ordered Hanlin Academician Li Qi to compose the shrine stele and bestow it. To this day the common people offer sacrifice there and his descendants preserve it—thus he was also a famed king of recent times.

units.zh: 元瓘，镠第五子也。
units.en: Yuanguan was Liu's fifth son.
units.literal: Yuanguan was Liu's fifth son.

units.zh: 起家為鹽鐵發運巡官，表授尚書金部朗中，賜金紫。
units.en: He began his career as an inspector of the Salt and Iron Transport Office; by memorial he was appointed Director of the Ministry of Revenue's Gold Department and granted the gold seal and purple robe.
units.literal: He began his career as an inspector of the Salt and Iron Transport Office; by memorial he was appointed Director of the Ministry of Revenue's Gold Department and granted the gold seal and purple robe.

units.zh: 天復中，本州裨校許再思等為亂，構宣州節度使田頵，頵領兵奄至，镠擊敗再思，與頵通和。
units.en: In the Tianfu era, the local adjutants Xu Zaisi and others rebelled, colluding with Xuancheng Military Commissioner Tian Yun; Yun led troops in a sudden arrival. Liu defeated Zaisi and made peace with Yun.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era, the local adjutants Xu Zaisi and others rebelled, colluding with Xuancheng Military Commissioner Tian Yun; Yun led troops in a sudden arrival. Liu defeated Zaisi and made peace with Yun.

units.zh: 頵要盟於镠，镠遍召諸子問之曰：「誰能為吾為田氏之婿者？」
units.en: Yun demanded a marriage alliance with Liu; Liu summoned all his sons and asked, "Who among you can become my son-in-law to the Tian clan?"
units.literal: Yun demanded a marriage alliance with Liu; Liu summoned all his sons and asked, "Who among you can become my son-in-law to the Tian clan?"

units.zh: 例有難色，時元瓘年十六，進曰：「惟大王之命。」
units.en: As a rule they showed reluctance, but Yuanguan, then sixteen, stepped forward and said, "I await only the Great King's command."
units.literal: As a rule they showed reluctance, but Yuanguan, then sixteen, stepped forward and said, "I await only the Great King's command."

units.zh: 由是就親於宣州。
units.en: Thereupon he went to Xuancheng to marry.
units.literal: Thereupon he went to Xuancheng to marry.

units.zh: 唐天祐初，承制累遷檢校尚書左僕射、內衙都指揮使，數年之間，伐叛禦寇，大著勛績。
units.en: At the beginning of Tianyou of Tang, by imperial order he was repeatedly promoted to Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Commander of the Inner Palace Guard; within a few years, suppressing rebels and repelling invaders, he achieved great merit.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou of Tang, by imperial order he was repeatedly promoted to Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Commander of the Inner Palace Guard; within a few years, suppressing rebels and repelling invaders, he achieved great merit.

units.zh: 梁貞明四年夏，镠大舉伐吳，以元瓘為水戰諸軍都指揮使。
units.en: In the summer of the fourth year of Zhenming of Liang, Liu launched a major campaign against Wu and appointed Yuanguan Commander of All Naval Forces.
units.literal: In the summer of the fourth year of Zhenming of Liang, Liu launched a major campaign against Wu and appointed Yuanguan Commander of All Naval Forces.

units.zh: 戰棹抵東洲，吳人以舟師拒戰，元瓘為火筏順風揚灰以岔之，白晝如霧，吳師迷方，遂敗之，擒軍使彭彥章並軍校七十餘人，得戰艦四百隻。
units.en: The battle fleet reached Dongzhou; the Wu sent a naval force to resist. Yuanguan built fire rafts and, riding the wind, scattered ash to blind them; by day it was like fog, the Wu army lost its bearings, and he defeated them, capturing Army Commissioner Peng Yanzhang along with more than seventy officers and taking four hundred warships.
units.literal: The battle fleet reached Dongzhou; the Wu sent a naval force to resist. Yuanguan built fire rafts and, riding the wind, scattered ash to confuse them; by day it was like fog, the Wu army lost its bearings, and he defeated them, capturing Army Commissioner Peng Yanzhang along with more than seventy officers and taking four hundred warships.

units.zh: 吳人知不可校，通好於镠，以功奏授鎮海軍節度副使、檢校司徒。
units.en: The Wu knew they could not contend and made peace with Liu; for his merit he was memorialized and appointed Deputy Military Commissioner of Zhenhai Army and Acting Minister of Education.
units.literal: The Wu knew they could not contend and made peace with Liu; for his merit he was memorialized and appointed Deputy Military Commissioner of Zhenhai Army and Acting Minister of Education.

units.zh: 梁末，遷清海軍節度使、檢校太傅、同平章事。
units.en: At the end of Liang he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Qinghai Army, Acting Grand Tutor, and Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
units.literal: At the end of Liang he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Qinghai Army, Acting Grand Tutor, and Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

units.zh: 後唐同光初，加檢校太師、兼中書令、鎮東等軍節度觀察處置等使。
units.en: At the beginning of Tongguang of Later Tang he was further made Acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and Military Commissioner, Observation Commissioner, and Disposition Commissioner of Zhendong and other armies.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang of Later Tang he was further made Acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and Military Commissioner, Observation Commissioner, and Disposition Commissioner of Zhendong and other armies.

units.zh: 時镠自為天下兵馬都元帥、尚父、守尚書令、吳越國王，及镠為太師致仕，元瓘累貢章疏，乞復舊號，唐明宗許之。
units.en: At that time Liu himself was Commander-in-Chief of All Armed Forces Under Heaven, Imperial Sire-Father, Acting Director of the Secretariat, and King of Wuyue; when Liu retired as Grand Preceptor, Yuanguan repeatedly submitted memorials begging restoration of the former titles, and Tang Mingzong granted this.
units.literal: At that time Liu himself was Commander-in-Chief of All Armed Forces Under Heaven, Imperial Sire-Father, Acting Director of the Secretariat, and King of Wuyue; when Liu retired as Grand Preceptor, Yuanguan repeatedly submitted memorials begging restoration of the former titles, and Tang Mingzong granted this.

units.zh: 镠既年高，欲立嗣，召諸子使各論功，請讓於元瓘。
units.en: Liu, now advanced in years, wished to establish a successor; he summoned his sons to each recount their merits and asked that the succession be yielded to Yuanguan.
units.literal: Liu, now advanced in years, wished to establish a successor; he summoned his sons to each recount their merits and asked that the succession be yielded to Yuanguan.

units.zh: 及镠病篤，召將吏謂之曰：「余病不起，兒皆愚懦，恐不能為爾帥。
units.en: When Liu's illness grew grave, he summoned his generals and officials and said, "My illness will not improve; my sons are all foolish and weak—I fear they cannot be your commander.
units.literal: When Liu's illness grew grave, he summoned his generals and officials and said, "My illness will not improve; my sons are all foolish and weak—I fear they cannot be your commander.

units.zh: 與爾輩決矣，帥當自擇。」
units.en: I have decided this with you all—the commander should be chosen by yourselves."
units.literal: I have decided this with you all—the commander should be chosen by yourselves."

units.zh: 將吏號泣言曰：「大令公有軍功，多賢行仁孝，已領兩鎮，王何苦言及此！」
units.en: The generals and officials wept aloud and said, "The Heir Apparent has military merit, many worthy deeds, and filial piety; he already commands two prefectures—Great King, why speak of this!"
units.literal: The generals and officials wept aloud and said, "The Heir Apparent has military merit, many worthy deeds, and filial piety; he already commands two prefectures—Great King, why speak of this!"

units.zh: 镠曰：「此渠定堪否？」
units.en: Liu said, "Is he truly fit or not?"
units.literal: Liu said, "Is he truly fit or not?"

units.zh: 曰：「眾等願奉賢帥。」
units.en: They said, "We all wish to serve the worthy commander."
units.literal: They said, "We all wish to serve the worthy commander."

units.zh: 即出符鑰數篚於前，謂元瓘曰：「三軍言爾可奉，領取此。」
units.en: He then brought out several baskets of seals and keys before them and said to Yuanguan, "The three armies say you are fit to lead—take these."
units.literal: He then brought out several baskets of seals and keys before them and said to Yuanguan, "The three armies say you are fit to lead—take these."

units.zh: 镠薨，遂襲父位。
units.en: When Liu died, Yuanguan succeeded to his father's position.
units.literal: When Liu died, Yuanguan succeeded to his father's position.

units.zh: 唐長興四年，遣將作監李纮起復元瓘官爵，又命戶部侍郎張文寶授兼尚書令。
units.en: In the fourth year of Changxing of Tang, the Director of the Directorate for Palace Buildings Li Hong was sent to restore Yuanguan's offices and rank from mourning, and Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Zhang Wenbao was ordered to invest him as Concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing of Tang, the Director of the Directorate for Palace Buildings Li Hong was sent to restore Yuanguan's offices and rank from mourning, and Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Zhang Wenbao was ordered to invest him as Concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 清泰初，封吳王。
units.en: At the beginning of Qingtai he was enfeoffed as King of Wu.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was enfeoffed as King of Wu.

units.zh: 二年，封越王。
units.en: In the second year he was enfeoffed as King of Yue.
units.literal: In the second year he was enfeoffed as King of Yue.

units.zh: 天福元年，賜金印。
units.en: In the first year of Tianfu he was granted a gold seal.
units.literal: In the first year of Tianfu he was granted a gold seal.

units.zh: 三年，封吳越國王。
units.en: In the third year he was enfeoffed as King of Wuyue.
units.literal: In the third year he was enfeoffed as King of Wuyue.

units.zh: 五年，加天下兵馬元帥。
units.en: In the fifth year he was made Commander-in-Chief of All Armed Forces Under Heaven.
units.literal: In the fifth year he was made Commander-in-Chief of All Armed Forces Under Heaven.

units.zh: 六年，授天下兵馬都元帥。
units.en: In the sixth year he was invested as Supreme Commander-in-Chief of All Armed Forces Under Heaven.
units.literal: In the sixth year he was invested as Supreme Commander-in-Chief of All Armed Forces Under Heaven.

units.zh: 其年夏有疾，秋府署災，焚之一空，乃移於他所，其焰皆隨而發焉，元瓘因驚悸發狂，以是歲八月二十四日薨，年五十五歲。
units.en: That summer he fell ill; in autumn the government offices caught fire and were burned to nothing. When they were moved elsewhere, the flames followed and broke out again. Yuanguan, shaken and terrified, went mad; on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month of that year he died, at age fifty-five.
units.literal: That summer he fell ill; in autumn the government offices caught fire and were burned to nothing. When they were moved elsewhere, the flames followed and broke out again. Yuanguan, shaken and terrified, went mad; on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month of that year he died, at age fifty-five.

units.zh: 謚曰文穆。
units.en: His posthumous title was Wenmu.
units.literal: His posthumous title was Wenmu.

units.zh: 元瓘幼聰敏，長於撫馭，臨戎十五年，決事神速，為軍民所附，然奢僭營造，甚於其父，故有回祿之災焉。
units.en: Yuanguan was clever from youth and skilled in winning men; for fifteen years in command he decided affairs with swift decisiveness and was beloved by soldiers and civilians alike. Yet his extravagant presumption in construction exceeded even his father's, and therefore he suffered the calamity of Huilu.
units.literal: Yuanguan was clever from youth and skilled in winning men; for fifteen years in command he decided affairs with swift decisiveness and was attached to by soldiers and civilians alike. Yet his extravagant presumption in construction exceeded even his father's, and therefore he suffered the calamity of Huilu.

units.zh: 元瓘有詩千篇，編其尤者三百篇，命曰《錦樓集》，浙中人士皆傳之。
units.en: Yuanguan composed a thousand poems; he selected the finest three hundred and titled the collection the 《Jade Tower Collection》; scholars throughout Zhe all circulated it.
units.literal: Yuanguan had a thousand poems; he selected the finest three hundred and titled the collection the 《Jade Tower Collection》; scholars throughout Zhe all circulated it.

units.zh: 子佐為嗣。
units.en: His son Zuo succeeded him.
units.literal: His son Zuo succeeded him.

units.zh: 佐，字元祐，元瓘薨，遂襲其位。
units.en: Zuo, courtesy name Yuanyou, when Yuanguan died succeeded to his position.
units.literal: Zuo, courtesy name Yuanyou, when Yuanguan died succeeded to his position.

units.zh: 晉天福末，制授檢校太師、兼中書令、吳越王，仍篆玉為冊以賜之。
units.en: At the end of Tianfu of Jin, by edict he was made Acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and King of Wuyue; a jade tablet was carved into a patent of investiture and bestowed on him.
units.literal: At the end of Tianfu of Jin, by edict he was made Acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and King of Wuyue; a jade tablet was carved into a patent of investiture and bestowed on him.

units.zh: 前代玉冊，冊夷王有之，偽梁時欲厚於镠，首為式例，故因而不改。
units.en: Jade patents of investiture in former ages had been granted to barbarian kings; in the false Liang they wished to honor Liu richly and first established this as a precedent, so it was retained unchanged.
units.literal: Jade patents of investiture in former ages had been granted to barbarian kings; in the false Liang they wished to honor Liu richly and first established this as a precedent, so it was retained unchanged.

units.zh: 俄授開府儀同三司、守太尉。
units.en: Soon he was made Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the Ceremonial of Three Departments and Acting Grand Commandant.
units.literal: Soon he was made Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the Ceremonial of Three Departments and Acting Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 時以建安為淮寇所攻，授東南面兵馬都元帥，佐尋遣舟師進討，淮入大敗，以功加守太師。
units.en: At that time Jian'an was being attacked by Huai bandits; he was made Commander-in-Chief of Southeastern Armed Forces. Zuo soon sent a naval force to advance and attack; the Huai invaders were greatly defeated, and for his merit he was further made Acting Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: At that time Jian'an was being attacked by Huai bandits; he was made Commander-in-Chief of Southeastern Armed Forces. Zuo soon sent a naval force to advance and attack; the Huai invaders were greatly defeated, and for his merit he was further made Acting Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 漢高祖入汴，佐首獻琛飐，表率東道，漢祖嘉之，授諸道兵馬都元帥。
units.en: When Emperor Gaozu of Han entered Bian, Zuo was first to present precious tribute, setting an example for the eastern circuits; Emperor Gaozu commended this and made him Commander-in-Chief of All Armed Forces of the Circuits.
units.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Han entered Bian, Zuo was first to present precious tribute, setting an example for the eastern circuits; Emperor Gaozu commended this and made him Commander-in-Chief of All Armed Forces of the Circuits.

units.zh: 佐居列土凡七年，境內豐阜，祖父三世皆為元帥，時以為榮。
units.en: Zuo ruled his domain for seven years in all; within his borders prosperity was abundant, and grandfather, father, and son for three generations had all been commanders-in-chief—the age regarded this as glory.
units.literal: Zuo ruled his domain for seven years in all; within his borders prosperity was abundant, and grandfather, father, and son for three generations had all been commanders-in-chief—the age regarded this as glory.

units.zh: 漢初，以疾卒於位，謚曰忠獻。
units.en: At the beginning of Han he died in office from illness; his posthumous title was Zhongxian.
units.literal: At the beginning of Han he died in office from illness; his posthumous title was Zhongxian.

units.zh: 佐幼好書，性溫恭，能為五七言詩，凡官屬遇雪月佳景，必同宴賞，由此士人歸心。
units.en: Zuo from youth loved books; his nature was mild and courteous, and he could compose five- and seven-character verse. Whenever his officials encountered fine scenes of snow or moonlight, he always shared banquets and appreciation—thereby winning the hearts of scholars.
units.literal: Zuo from youth loved books; his nature was mild and courteous, and he could compose five- and seven-character verse. Whenever his officials encountered fine scenes of snow or moonlight, he always shared banquets and appreciation—thereby winning the hearts of scholars.

units.zh: 其班品亦有丞相已下名籍，而祿給甚薄，罕能自濟，每朝廷降吏，則去其偽官，或與會則公府助以仆馬，處事齷齪，多如此類。
units.en: His official ranks also had rosters from Chancellor downward, but salaries were very meager and few could support themselves. Whenever the court sent down officials, their false titles were removed; if they attended gatherings the public office would assist with servants and horses—affairs were handled in petty, cramped ways, mostly of this sort.
units.literal: His official ranks also had rosters from Chancellor downward, but salaries were very meager and few could support themselves. Whenever the court sent down officials, their false titles were removed; if they attended gatherings the public office would assist with servants and horses—affairs were handled in petty, cramped ways, mostly of this sort.

units.zh: 然航海所入，歲貢百萬，王人一至，所遺至廣，故朝廷寵之，為群藩之冠。
units.en: Yet what came in by sea amounted to a million in annual tribute; whenever envoys of the king arrived, the gifts given were exceedingly broad—therefore the court favored him, and he stood at the head of all the feudatories.
units.literal: Yet what came in by sea amounted to a million in annual tribute; whenever envoys of the king arrived, the gifts given were exceedingly broad—therefore the court favored him, and he stood at the head of all the feudatories.

units.zh: 佐有子昱，年五歲，未任庶務，乃以其弟倧襲位。
units.en: Zuo had a son Yu, five years old and not yet fit for ordinary affairs; therefore his younger brother Zong succeeded to the position.
units.literal: Zuo had a son Yu, five years old and not yet fit for ordinary affairs; therefore his younger brother Zong succeeded to the position.

units.zh: 倧，性明敏嚴毅，未立時，常以佐性寬善，疑掌兵權者難制，及代佐為帥，以禮法繩下，宿將舊勛，不甚優禮。
units.en: Zong's nature was bright, keen, stern, and resolute. Before he was established he had often thought that because Zuo's nature was lenient and good, those who held military power would be hard to control; when he replaced Zuo as commander he restrained subordinates with ritual and law, and did not greatly honor veteran generals and old merit.
units.literal: Zong's nature was bright, keen, stern, and resolute. Before he was established he had often thought that because Zuo's nature was lenient and good, those who held military power would be hard to control; when he replaced Zuo as commander he restrained subordinates with ritual and law, and did not greatly honor veteran generals and old merit.

units.zh: 大將胡進思頗不平之，乃密與親軍謀去倧。
units.en: The great general Hu Jinsi was quite discontent with this and secretly plotted with his personal troops to remove Zong.
units.literal: The great general Hu Jinsi was quite discontent with this and secretly plotted with his personal troops to remove Zong.

units.zh: 漢祖入汴之歲，十二月，進思率甲士三百大噪，突入衙署，倧闔戶以拒之，左右與之格鬥，盡為進思所殺，遂遷倧於別館，以甲士送，幽於衣錦軍，立倧異母弟俶為帥。
units.en: In the year Emperor Gaozu of Han entered Bian, in the twelfth month Jinsi led three hundred armored soldiers in a great uproar and burst into the government offices. Zong shut the doors to resist; his attendants fought with them and were all killed by Jinsi. He then moved Zong to a separate lodge, sent armored soldiers to escort him, and imprisoned him in the Yijin Army, establishing Zong's younger half-brother Chu as commander.
units.literal: In the year Emperor Gaozu of Han entered Bian, in the twelfth month Jinsi led three hundred armored soldiers in a great uproar and burst into the government offices. Zong shut the doors to resist; his attendants fought with them and were all killed by Jinsi. He then moved Zong to a separate lodge, sent armored soldiers to escort him, and imprisoned him in the Yijin Army, establishing Zong's younger half-brother Chu as commander.

units.zh: 其年夏四月，進思疽發背而卒，越人快之，以為陰靈之誅逆也。
units.en: That summer in the fourth month Jinsi died of a carbuncle on his back; the people of Yue rejoiced, taking it as the hidden spirits' punishment of a traitor.
units.literal: That summer in the fourth month Jinsi died of a carbuncle on his back; the people of Yue rejoiced, taking it as the hidden spirits' punishment of a traitor.

units.zh: 俶，元瓘之子，倧之異母弟也。
units.en: Chu was Yuanguan's son and Zong's younger half-brother.
units.literal: Chu was Yuanguan's son and Zong's younger half-brother.

units.zh: 倧既為軍校所幽，時俶為溫州刺史，眾以無帥，遂迎立之，時漢乾祐元年正月十五日也。
units.en: After Zong was imprisoned by the military officers, Chu was at that time Prefect of Wenzhou; since there was no commander, the multitude welcomed and established him—this was the fifteenth day of the first month of the first year of Ganyou of Han.
units.literal: After Zong was imprisoned by the military officers, Chu was at that time Prefect of Wenzhou; since there was no commander, the multitude welcomed and established him—this was the fifteenth day of the first month of the first year of Ganyou of Han.

units.zh: 其年八月，始授檢校太師、兼中書令，充鎮海鎮東等軍節度使、東南面兵馬都元帥。
units.en: That August he was first invested as Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, serving as Military Commissioner of Zhenhai, Zhendong, and other armies and Commander-in-Chief of Southeastern Armed Forces.
units.literal: That August he was first invested as Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, serving as Military Commissioner of Zhenhai, Zhendong, and other armies and Commander-in-Chief of Southeastern Armed Forces.

units.zh: 周廣順中，累官至守尚書令、中書令、吳越國王。
units.en: In Guangshun of Zhou he rose through offices to Acting Director of the Secretariat, Director of the Secretariat, and King of Wuyue.
units.literal: In Guangshun of Zhou he rose through offices to Acting Director of the Secretariat, Director of the Secretariat, and King of Wuyue.

units.zh: 皇朝建隆初，復加天下兵馬大元帥，其後事具皇朝日曆。
units.en: At the beginning of Jianlong of the Imperial Dynasty he was again made Grand Commander-in-Chief of All Armed Forces Under Heaven; his subsequent affairs are fully recorded in the Imperial Dynasty calendar.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong of the Imperial Dynasty he was again made Grand Commander-in-Chief of All Armed Forces Under Heaven; his subsequent affairs are fully recorded in the Imperial Dynasty calendar.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：錢珝封吳越國王後，大興府署，版築斤斧之聲晝夜不絕，士卒怨嗟。
units.en: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: After Qian Xu was enfeoffed as King of Wuyue, he greatly expanded the government offices; the sounds of ramming earth and wielding axes never ceased day or night, and the soldiers grumbled.
units.literal: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: After Qian Xu was enfeoffed as King of Wuyue, he greatly expanded the government offices; the sounds of ramming earth and wielding axes never ceased day or night, and the soldiers grumbled.

units.zh: 或有中夜潛用白土大書於門曰：「沒了期，侵早起，抵暮歸。」
units.en: Some at midnight secretly used white earth to write large characters on a gate saying, "No end to it—rise early at dawn, return only at dusk."
units.literal: Some at midnight secretly used white earth to write large characters on a gate saying, "No end to it—rise early at dawn, return only at dusk."

units.zh: 珝一見欣然，遽命書吏亦以白土書數字於其側曰：「沒了期，春衣才罷又冬衣。」
units.en: Xu, on seeing it, was pleased and immediately ordered a clerk also to write several characters in white earth beside it saying, "No end to it—spring clothes just finished, then winter clothes again."
units.literal: Xu, on seeing it, was pleased and immediately ordered a clerk also to write several characters in white earth beside it saying, "No end to it—spring clothes just finished, then winter clothes again."

units.zh: 時人以為神輔，自是怨嗟頓息矣。
units.en: The people of the age regarded this as divine assistance; from then on the grumbling suddenly ceased.
units.literal: The people of the age regarded this as divine assistance; from then on the grumbling suddenly ceased.

units.zh: 僧昭者，通於術數，居兩浙，大為錢塘錢珝所禮，謂之國師。
units.en: There was a monk named Zhao, versed in numerology and divination, who lived in the Two Zhes and was greatly honored by Qian Xu of Qiantang, who called him State Preceptor.
units.literal: There was a monk named Zhao, versed in numerology and divination, who lived in the Two Zhes and was greatly honored by Qian Xu of Qiantang, who called him State Preceptor.

units.zh: 一旦謁珝，有宮中小兒嬉於側，墜下錢數十文，珝見，謂之曰：「速收，慮人恐踏破汝錢。」
units.en: One day he came to call on Xu; a small boy from the palace was playing at the side and dropped several dozen cash. Xu saw this and said to him, "Quick, pick them up—I fear someone may step on and break your money."
units.literal: One day he came to call on Xu; a small boy from the palace was playing at the side and dropped several dozen cash. Xu saw this and said to him, "Quick, pick them up—I fear someone may step on and break your money."

units.zh: 昭師笑曰：「汝錢欲踏破，須是牛即可。」
units.en: Master Zhao laughed and said, "If you want that money crushed, you'll need an ox."
units.literal: Master Zhao laughed and said, "If you wish your money to be stepped on and broken, it would take an ox to do it."

units.zh: 珝喜，以為社稷堅牢之義。
units.en: Xu was delighted and took this as a sign that the realm would endure.
units.literal: Xu was pleased and took this as an omen that the altars of state would stand firm.

units.zh: 後至曾孫俶，舉族入朝，因而國除。
units.en: Eventually his great-grandson Chu led the entire clan to court, and the kingdom was absorbed.
units.literal: Later, down to his great-grandson Chu, the whole clan entered court audience, and thereby the state was abolished.

units.zh: 俶年屬醜為牛，可謂牛踏錢而破矣。
units.en: Chu was born in the year of the ox—so the ox did indeed tread the Qian domain underfoot.
units.literal: Chu's birth year fell under the sign chou, the ox—one may say the ox stepped on the money and broke it.

units.zh: 錢珝末年患雙目，有醫人不知所從來，自雲累世醫內外障眼，其術皆善於用針，無不效者。
units.en: In his last years Qian Xu went blind in both eyes; a physician of unknown origin appeared, claiming generations of skill in treating cataracts and other eye ailments with needles that never failed.
units.literal: In his later years Qian Xu suffered in both eyes; a physician appeared from no one knew where, saying of himself that for generations his family had treated inner and outer eye obstructions, and that his techniques, all skilled in the use of needles, never failed.

units.zh: 珝聞，召而使觀之，醫人曰：「可治，然大王非常人，患殆天與之，若醫，是違天地也，恐無益於壽，幸思之。」
units.en: Xu summoned him; the physician said, "I can treat this, but you are no ordinary man—this ailment may be Heaven's gift. To cure it would defy Heaven and may not prolong your life. Think carefully."
units.literal: Xu heard of this and summoned him to examine his eyes; the physician said: "It can be treated, yet Your Highness is no ordinary man—this affliction was likely given by Heaven; if I treat it, I would violate Heaven and Earth, and I fear it would not benefit your lifespan. Please consider this."

units.zh: 珝曰：「吾起自行伍，跨有方面，富貴足矣，但得兩眼見物，為鬼不亦快乎！」
units.en: Xu replied, "I rose from the ranks to rule a region—I've had wealth and honor enough; let me see again—even as a ghost I would be content!"
units.literal: Xu said: "I rose from the ranks and hold a region—wealth and honor are enough; only let me see with both eyes again—even as a ghost would that not be joy!"

units.zh: 既而下手，莫不應手豁然。
units.en: The physician treated him, and his sight cleared immediately.
units.literal: The physician then applied his treatment, and in every case vision cleared at once.

units.zh: 珝喜，所賜動以萬計，醫人皆辭不受。
units.en: Delighted, Xu offered rewards in the tens of thousands, but the physician refused them all.
units.literal: Xu was pleased; the gifts he offered ran to tens of thousands, but the physician declined them all.

units.zh: 明年，珝卒。
units.en: The following year Xu died.
units.literal: The next year Xu died.

units.zh: 僧契盈，閩中人。
units.en: The monk Qiying was from Fujian.
units.literal: The monk Qiying was a man of Min.

units.zh: 通內外學，性尤敏速。
units.en: He mastered secular and Buddhist learning and was exceptionally quick-witted.
units.literal: He mastered both secular and Buddhist learning and was especially quick and keen by nature.

units.zh: 廣順初，遊戲錢塘。
units.en: Early in the Guangshun era he visited Qiantang.
units.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he traveled about Qiantang.

units.zh: 一旦，陪吳越王遊碧浪亭，時潮水初滿，舟楫輻輳，望之不見其首尾，王喜曰：「吳越地去京師三千餘里，而誰知一水之利有如此耶！」
units.en: One day he accompanied the King of Wuyue to Bilang Pavilion as the tide reached full flood; boats packed the water as far as eye could see. The king exclaimed, "Wuyue lies three thousand li from the capital—who knew a single waterway could hold such power!"
units.literal: One day he accompanied the King of Wuyue to tour Bilang Pavilion; the tide had just reached full flood, boats and oars crowded thickly, and looking out one could not see the head or tail; the king said with pleasure: "The lands of Wuyue are more than three thousand li from the capital—who would have known that the profit of a single waterway could be like this!"

units.zh: 契盈對曰：「可謂三千里外一條水，十二時中兩度潮。」
units.en: Qiying replied, "Three thousand li away, one river; twice each day, the tide."
units.literal: Qiying replied: "It may be said: three thousand li away, a single stretch of water; twice in twelve hours, the tide."

units.zh: 時人謂之佳對。
units.en: Contemporaries hailed it as a perfect couplet.
units.literal: People of the time called this an excellent couplet.

units.zh: 時江南未通，兩浙貢賦自海路而至青州，故云三千里也。）〉
units.en: Jiangnan was not yet linked by land; the two Zhe regions sent tribute by sea to Qingzhou—hence the three thousand li.) )〉
units.literal: At that time Jiangnan was not yet connected by land; the tribute and taxes of the two Zhe regions came by sea route to Qingzhou—hence the saying of three thousand li.) )〉

units.zh: 史臣曰：自唐末亂離，海內分割，荊、湖、江、浙，各據一方，翼子貽孫，多歷年所。
units.en: The historian writes: From the chaos at the end of Tang the realm split apart; Jingnan, Hunan, the Yangzi delta, and Zhejiang each held its own territory, passing power from generation to generation for decades.
units.literal: The historiographer says: From the disorder and separation at the end of Tang, the realm within the seas was divided; Jing, Hu, Jiang, and Zhe each held a region, passing domain from winged sons to grandsons, for many years.

units.zh: 夫如是者何也？
units.en: Why was this so?
units.literal: Why was it so?

units.zh: 蓋值諸夏多艱，王風不競故也。
units.en: Because the heartland faced endless hardship and imperial authority could not prevail.
units.literal: It was because the central states faced many hardships and royal influence could not compete.

units.zh: 洎皇宋之撫運也，因朗、陵之肇亂，命王師以遄征，一矢不亡，二方俱服。
units.en: When the Song received Heaven's mandate, rebellion at Lang and Ling brought the imperial army in swift campaign; not an arrow was wasted, and both regions submitted.
units.literal: When the Imperial Song received the mandate of fortune, because of the initial rebellion at Lang and Ling, the court ordered the royal army on swift campaign—not an arrow lost, both regions submitted together.

units.zh: 遂使瑤琨筿簜，鹹遵作貢之文；
units.en: Jade, bamboo, and fine reeds all alike fulfilled their tribute obligations;
units.literal: Thereupon jade, bamboo, and fine reeds all alike observed the rites of tribute;

units.zh: 江、漢、雎、章，盡鼓朝宗之浪。
units.en: the Yangzi, Han, Ju, and Zhang all surged with the tide of loyalty to the throne.
units.literal: the Jiang, Han, Ju, and Zhang all beat the waves of gathering toward the court.

units.zh: 夫如是者何也？
units.en: Why was this so?
units.literal: Why was it so?

units.zh: 蓋屬大統有歸，人寰允洽故也。
units.en: Because the great mandate had found its rightful heir and the realm was united in peace.
units.literal: It was because the great succession had found its home and the human realm was truly harmonized.

units.zh: 惟錢氏之守杭、越，逾八十年，蓋事大勤王之節，與荊楚、湖湘不侔矣。
units.en: Only the Qian clan's hold on Hangzhou and Yue lasted more than eighty years—for their loyalty to the throne and dutiful service to the dynasty set them apart from Jing-Chu and Hunan.
units.literal: Only the Qian clan's holding of Hang and Yue exceeded eighty years—because their observance of serving the great power and diligently aiding the royal house was not comparable to Jing-Chu and Hu-Xiang.
